# Principal Architect Audit — Dependency Injection, Session Persistence and Token Rotation

This tranche resolves the dependency-injection question raised in the previous review. It also identifies a separate refresh-token rotation concern in SkillHubCore.

## SU-SESSION-007 — Shared `SessionService` cannot be constructed correctly by the default container

P1 — Runtime dependency

The API server's [dependency-injection container](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/core/container.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L28-L50) creates unregistered classes using `new token()` without constructor arguments.

The shared [SessionService](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/auth/src/session.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L15-L29) requires a `SessionRepository` constructor dependency.

The [logout-all route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/auth/logout-all/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L16-L36) obtains this shared service from the container.

If it has not been explicitly registered elsewhere, the container constructs it without a repository. Its methods then attempt to call methods on an undefined dependency.

Confirmed: The default container has no automatic constructor-dependency injection.

Conditional: The logout-all runtime failure depends on whether a separate registration occurs before the route executes.

Required correction: Explicitly register the shared service with a compatible repository, or consolidate session management behind the approved brand-aware service abstraction.

## SU-SESSION-008 — Session repository interfaces are incompatible

The shared `SessionService` expects methods including `findByRefreshToken()`, `revokeAllForUser()` and `updateLastActivity()`.

The API server's [DrizzleSessionRepository](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/repositories/implementations/drizzle-session.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) implements `findByUser()`, `deleteAllUserSessions()` and `cleanupExpired()` instead.

These are not interchangeable interfaces.

Priority: P1 — architecture contract. Simply injecting the existing Drizzle repository into the shared service would not fix the problem.

## SHC-AUTH-001 — SkillHubCore refresh rotation uses a non-atomic Redis check

P1 — Refresh-token replay protection

Source: [SkillHubCore TokenRotationService](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/token-rotation.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L32-L102).

The service reads the currently stored refresh token from Redis, compares it with the submitted token, and later replaces it with a newly generated token.

The comparison and replacement are not performed as one atomic operation.

Two concurrent refresh requests could therefore both read the same old token before either updates Redis.

The database transaction helps coordinate session changes, but the reviewed code does not establish an atomic compare-and-swap across Redis and the database.

Required correction: Design single-use refresh-token rotation with atomic consumption, explicit concurrency behavior and family-compromise handling. The exact mechanism must be chosen after reviewing the underlying repository methods and Redis deployment.

## SHC-AUTH-002 — Missing Redis refresh-token state is treated as acceptable

In the same service, the mismatch check is:

```
if (storedRefreshToken !== null && storedRefreshToken !== refreshToken)
```

If Redis returns `null`, the mismatch check is skipped.

The code subsequently checks the token family and database session, so this does not automatically establish unauthorized refresh. But the Redis state is not mandatory for the rotation to continue.

Priority: P1 — replay-protection consistency. We need to establish whether Redis is authoritative, a cache, or an optional secondary control.

## SHC-AUTH-003 — Redis writes occur inside a database transaction callback

The rotation code updates Redis inside `userRepo.transaction()`.

A database rollback cannot automatically roll back an already successful Redis write.

Confirmed: The operation spans two persistence systems without a demonstrated distributed consistency mechanism.

Potential impact: A failed database transaction could leave Redis pointing to a token that the database has not accepted.

## SU-SESSION-009 — Shared session expiry extension is unimplemented

Source: [SessionService.extendSession()](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/auth/src/session.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L173-L186).

The method calculates a new expiration time but never persists it. The repository update is commented out.

Confirmed: Calling this method can complete without extending the session.

Priority: P2, potentially higher if production callers depend on it.

# Principal Architect Audit — SkillHubCore Session Repository and Rotation Tests

I have now traced SkillHubCore's refresh-token rotation into its actual People database repository and reviewed the associated test suite.

This reveals a stronger finding than the earlier concurrency concern: the database repository does not persist the refresh-token value that the rotation service passes to it.

## SHC-AUTH-004 — Refresh-token persistence contract is misleading

P1 — Authentication integrity

In [DrizzleUserRepository.createSession()](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/user/user.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L180-L194), the method accepts `refreshTokenHash` as part of its input, but the database insert writes only `userId`, `jwtFamily` and `platform`.

The refresh-token hash is discarded.

Confirmed: The session repository does not persist the supplied refresh-token hash.

Implication: Rotation relies on Redis for exact-token comparison rather than using the session record as an independent token-validity check.

This becomes especially important because the rotation service allows a missing Redis value to pass its mismatch check.

## SHC-AUTH-005 — Session-family lookup does not require an active session

Source: [findSessionByFamily()](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/user/user.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L261-L272).

The query checks user ID, family ID and soft-deletion state, but does not filter out revoked sessions.

The rotation service subsequently checks `revokedAt`, which provides protection at the service layer.

Assessment: This is not independently an authentication bypass. However, the repository method's name and contract should make clear that it can return revoked sessions.

## SHC-AUTH-006 — Token-family ownership is not checked by family lookup

Source: [findTokenFamilyByFamilyId()](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/user/user.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L313-L324).

The token-family lookup accepts only `familyId` and does not verify `userId`.

The rotation service obtains `payload.sub` from a verified JWT and subsequently performs a user-scoped session lookup, which mitigates the immediate risk.

Nevertheless, family ownership is not an invariant of the repository API.

Priority: P2 — defense in depth.

## SHC-AUTH-007 — Rotation lacks a database-enforced single-active-session constraint

Source: [People database SSO session schema](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-people/src/schema/sso-sessions.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L5-L15).

The `sso_sessions` table has a primary key on session ID and an index on `(jwt_family, revoked_at)`.

It does not define a uniqueness constraint limiting a token family to one active session.

The rotation service revokes the old family session and creates a new session within a transaction, but the reviewed schema alone does not prevent concurrent transactions from producing multiple active sessions for the same family.

Priority: P1 — concurrency and session integrity.

The correct solution needs both atomic token consumption and a database invariant appropriate to the chosen rotation model.

## SHC-TEST-001 — Rotation tests do not model real transaction behavior

Source: [Fake repository implementation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/__tests__/token-rotation.service.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L34-L143).

The fake repository's `transaction()` method simply invokes the callback. It does not model commit, rollback, locking or isolation.

Its session store is also keyed by family ID, so creating a replacement session overwrites the prior entry. This differs from the production database, which permits multiple rows per family.

Confirmed: The fake's storage model cannot reveal several of the concurrency and multi-session behaviors possible in production.

## SHC-TEST-002 — Only successful rotation and stale-token reuse are tested

The test suite contains two test cases: successful rotation and a stale-token replay that marks a family compromised.

Both are valuable, but important cases are missing: concurrent refresh requests, Redis key loss, database rollback after Redis mutation, revoked-session reuse, cross-user family ownership and duplicate active sessions.

The test suite also does not assert that a token hash is stored, which aligns with the repository's omission.

## Additional file assessments

`SsoService` is a thin delegation layer for listing, granting and revoking platform access. Its reviewed methods do not independently establish authorization; callers must enforce who is permitted to grant or revoke access.

`services/skillhubcore-service/src/lib/db.ts` correctly re-exports the People database client and schema. No standalone defect was established in this two-line module.

| `services/skillhubcore-service/src/lib/db.ts`                       | 2              | People DB re-export                               |

### Principal Architect checkpoint

The repository confirms a meaningful difference between the intended token-family security model and the actual guarantees supplied by Redis, the People database and the tests.

My recommended review order is now to inspect SkillHubCore's login and logout services, the authentication route middleware, and the remaining token-family tests. That will establish whether the rotation weaknesses can be reached through the public API and whether logout reliably invalidates both Redis state and database sessions.

The review remains strictly read-only. No code changes, tests, commits, pull requests or deployments were performed.

## SHC-AUTH-008 — Password login automatically grants platform access

P1 — Brand isolation

Source: [AuthService.login()](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L103-L133).

After verifying a user's password, the login method calls:

```
const platforms = await this.ssoService.grantPlatformAccess(user.id, input.platform);
```

This means a successful login does not merely check existing platform membership: it grants membership to the platform requested in the login body.

The repository implementation can also restore previously revoked platform access.

This is a concrete authorization-policy concern. If platform access is meant to be provisioned by enrollment, invitation or administrator approval, this login path bypasses that provisioning decision.

It is not evidence that the user receives administrator privileges; the existing role is retained. But it can undermine SkillUp/RTH platform isolation.

Required architecture decision: Define whether platform access is self-service or explicitly provisioned. If provisioned, login must validate access rather than grant it.

## SHC-AUTH-009 — Session revocation does not remove Redis refresh-token state

Source: [Session management methods](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L227-L266).

There are three distinct revocation paths:

| Operation             | Database session  | Redis refresh key |
| --------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- |
| `logout()`            | Revoked by family | Deleted           |
| `revokeSession()`     | Revoked           | Not deleted       |
| `revokeAllSessions()` | Revoked           | Not deleted       |

The rotation service checks database revocation, so a revoked session should not simply become valid because its Redis key remains.

Nevertheless, the stale Redis state creates inconsistent lifecycle behavior and unnecessary retained credentials.

Priority: P2 — session lifecycle consistency.

## SHC-AUTH-010 — Login and registration can leave orphaned Redis state

Source: [Registration](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L40-L100) and [Login](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L125-L150).

Registration writes the refresh token to Redis inside a database transaction callback.

Login writes to Redis before opening the database transaction.

If the database work subsequently fails, the Redis key may remain even though the corresponding session was never committed.

The token validator's cross-domain callback flow uses the same pattern.

Priority: P1 — cross-store consistency.

## SHC-AUTH-011 — Cross-domain callback trusts token roles without reloading current access

Source: [TokenValidatorService.validateBrandAccessToken()](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/token-validator.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L80-L145).

The callback validator verifies the signed brand token and checks that its brand matches the requested brand. Those are positive controls.

It then copies roles, subscriptions and platforms from the verified token into a new SkillHubCore token. The reviewed method does not reload the user's current account status, platform grants or roles from the People database.

Potential impact: Changes made after the original token was issued may not be reflected when the callback exchanges it.

Priority: P1 — authorization freshness, subject to confirming the intended token lifetime and revocation policy.

## SHC-AUTH-012 — Invalid or missing roles default to `student`

The callback validator's `normalizeRoles()` returns `['student']` when it cannot recognize any roles.

That is a permissive identity-normalization policy, although it does not grant administrative privileges.

Priority: P2. Prefer explicit claim validation and rejection of malformed authorization data over inventing a role.

## SHC-AUTH-013 — Session routes default an absent brand to RealTutorialHub

Source: [Session endpoints](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/auth.routes.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L185-L229).

The session-listing and revocation routes use:

```
const platform = authUser.brand ?? 'realtutorialhub';
```

Whether this is dangerous depends on what `requireAuth` guarantees about the brand claim.

For a brand-isolated system, a missing brand should generally be rejected rather than silently assigned to another platform.

Priority: P2 — verify middleware contract.

## Positive controls confirmed

The reviewed code also contains meaningful protections:

- Administrative login verifies the user's existing `admin` or `super_admin` role.
- Single-session revocation checks both user ownership and platform before performing the mutation.
- Callback validation verifies the token signature, user audience and expected brand.
- Login, registration and refresh endpoints have rate-limiting checks.
- SkillHubCore logout deletes the corresponding Redis refresh key.

These controls should be preserved during remediation.

The most important architectural concern in this tranche is platform access being granted as a side effect of login. That behavior should be reconciled with the approved identity and brand-isolation architecture before any implementation is proposed.

The next review should examine `verify-jwt.ts`, the authentication route tests and the service's application-level middleware. This will establish whether the session routes' brand fallback and the cross-domain token exchange are adequately protected at their entry points.

# Principal Architect Audit — SkillHubCore JWT Middleware and Route Integration

The next four files reveal a significant integration issue. The authentication routes are tested in isolation, but the actual SkillHubCore application entry point does not register those routes.

## SHC-ROUTE-001 — Authentication routes are not mounted in the reviewed application entry point

P1 — Runtime integration

Source: [SkillHubCore application registration](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/index.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L15-L33).

The application mounts health checks, public marketing, admin SSO management, event consumers and hierarchy routes.

It does not mount `createAuthRoutes()`.

Confirmed: This entry point does not expose the login, refresh, callback, logout and session endpoints defined in `auth.routes.ts`.

Not yet confirmed: Whether another deployment entry point mounts them or whether this is an intentionally dormant implementation.

This is a key distinction: vulnerabilities in an unmounted route cannot be assumed externally exploitable through this server.

## SHC-AUTH-014 — JWT middleware silently switches brands

Source: [Brand selection in requireAuth](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/middleware/verify-jwt.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L35-L41).

The middleware accepts an `x-platform` or `x-brand` header. If the requested brand is not recognized or is not in the token's platform list, it silently falls back to the token's first platform.

For example, a caller requesting SkillUp with a token authorized only for RTH may be treated as an RTH caller instead of receiving an explicit cross-brand rejection.

This does not itself grant SkillUp access, but it makes brand selection ambiguous and can cause operations to execute in the wrong brand context.

Priority: P1 — brand isolation contract.

## SHC-AUTH-015 — Authorization relies on token claims without checking current platform grants

The reviewed `requireAuth` middleware verifies the JWT and checks that the token contains platform and identity claims. It does not query the People database to establish whether those platform grants are still active.

`requirePlatform()` then checks the platforms contained in the token.

Confirmed: These guards authorize against signed token claims rather than current platform-access records.

This can be an intentional short-lived JWT design, but it requires a documented revocation and freshness policy. Without one, a platform grant removed after token issuance may remain usable until the token expires.

Priority: P1 — authorization freshness.

## SHC-TEST-003 — Middleware tests cover only one negative case

Source: [JWT middleware tests](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/middleware/__tests__/verify-jwt.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

The file contains one test: rejection of a token missing its platform claim.

It does not test unsupported brand headers, unauthorized brand switching, missing bridge identity claims, revoked platform access or super-admin behavior.

The route tests likewise mount `createAuthRoutes()` directly on a test Hono application, rather than exercising the production `createApp()` registration. That explains why the tests can pass without detecting the missing authentication route mount.

## SHC-GATEWAY-001 — Gateway secret comparison is not timing-safe

Source: [Gateway secret verification](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/middleware/verify-gateway-secret.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L12-L20).

The middleware uses direct string inequality to compare the supplied gateway secret with the configured secret.

It correctly rejects requests when the secret is absent or incorrect, but a timing-safe comparison would be more appropriate for a security-sensitive shared secret.

Priority: P2 — hardening. Practical exploitability has not been established.

## SHC-SSO-001 — Administrative platform-grant routes have explicit role protection

Source: [SSO administration routes](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/services/skillhubcore-service/src/modules/auth/sso/sso.routes.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L18-L42).

These routes require a verified JWT and either `admin` or `super_admin` role before reading or changing a user's platform access.

That is a positive control.

The administrative grant/revoke mechanism also reinforces why `AuthService.login()` granting platform access automatically is a policy inconsistency worth resolving.

# SkillUp Principal Architect Audit — Authentication and Learner Identity

I have returned to SkillUp-specific code. This review covers the learner authentication guard and the SkillUp logout and refresh routes.

## SU-AUTH-001 — Learner identity falls back to the wrong identity namespace

P1 — Identity integrity

Source: [SkillUp student-auth.ts, lines 84–112](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L84-L112).

The guard verifies a signed user access token and then chooses:

```
const userId =
  typeof payload.shadowUserId === 'string' && payload.shadowUserId.trim().length > 0
    ? payload.shadowUserId.trim()
    : typeof payload.userId === 'string' && payload.userId.trim().length > 0
      ? payload.userId.trim()
      : null;
```

This is problematic because the SkillUp learner data layer queries the shared People database using the returned ID. In the intended identity model, `shadowUserId` identifies the People record, while `userId` may identify the original SkillUp account.

Confirmed: The fallback exists, and the guard does not require a valid `shadowUserId`.

Risk: A token missing its bridge identity could cause learner queries to run with an ID from a different database namespace.

This is an identity-integrity defect, although unauthorized access to another user's record has not been demonstrated.

Recommended correction: Require both identity claims and use the People shadow ID explicitly for People database queries. Keep the original SkillUp ID separately for SkillUp-owned records.

## SU-AUTH-023 — Learner authentication accepts privileged roles as student access

Source: [Allowed roles](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L5-L6) and [Role authorization](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L126-L140).

The allowed role set includes `student`, `faculty`, `admin` and `super_admin`.

That may be intentional for staff preview or support workflows. But the function is named `requireStudentAuth()` and grants access to learner-specific endpoints without checking whether the caller is enrolled as a student.

Confirmed: Any of these signed roles passes the role check when the token brand is `skillup`.

Policy question: Should staff be able to use learner routes as themselves, or should staff preview require a separate audited impersonation mechanism?

Until that policy is established, I classify this as P2 — authorization ambiguity, not a proven privilege escalation.

## Positive controls

The same file correctly verifies the JWT with the user audience, requires the token's brand to be exactly `skillup`, rejects missing tokens and normalizes role casing.

These are valuable controls to preserve.

## SU-AUTH-004 — SkillUp logout discards backend cookie-clearing headers

P1 — Logout reliability

Source: [SkillUp logout route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L17-L44).

The shared authentication proxy already forwards and rewrites upstream `Set-Cookie` headers.

But SkillUp's logout handler builds another response and explicitly excludes those headers:

```
if (key.toLowerCase() !== 'set-cookie') {
  response.headers.set(key, value);
}
```

It then creates its own expired cookies without a `domain` attribute.

If the original authentication cookies were issued for `.skillupitacademy.com`, these host-only deletion cookies may not remove them.

Confirmed: Backend cookie-clearing headers are discarded, and replacement deletion cookies omit the domain.

Potential consequence: Logout can appear successful while browser authentication cookies remain.

A browser-level test is required to establish the exact behavior for deployed cookie domains.

## SU-GATEWAY-012 — SkillUp auth can bypass the gateway when fallback is enabled

Source: [Shared authentication proxy fallback](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L484-L541).

The shared proxy describes a gateway-only architecture, but its `proxyAuthRequest()` implementation can send requests directly to `fallbackApiBase` when the gateway fails and configuration permits fallback.

This is an actual alternate routing path, not merely a comment or unused helper.

Confirmed: The bypass path exists in code.

Conditional: Whether SkillUp uses it in production depends on `STRICT_GATEWAY`, `ENABLE_FALLBACK` and the configured fallback base URL.

Architectural concern: Authentication traffic should not silently switch trust boundaries during gateway failure.

## SU-GATEWAY-013 — Client-supplied identity headers are copied into the trusted upstream request

Source: [Header copying](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L134-L140) and [Internal secret injection](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L223-L266).

The proxy begins with all incoming request headers and removes only a small set.

It subsequently injects the internal gateway secret, but does not explicitly strip inbound `x-user-id`, `x-original-user-id`, `x-shadow-user-id` or `x-user-roles`.

This means client-controlled identity headers can accompany a server-supplied internal credential.

Confirmed: The header-forwarding trust boundary is not sanitized at this layer.

Not yet proven: Whether the gateway or final backend accepts those headers as authenticated user identity on any particular SkillUp endpoint.

Priority: P1 — trace downstream consumers and add negative tests.

# Expanded SkillUp Audit — 16 Files, Approximately 900 Lines

I have widened this review to cover an entire connected SkillUp workflow rather than just two or three files: authentication entry points, session management, learner APIs, tutorial progress, placement handoff, and the shared middleware that actually protects SkillUp.

One important correction to the previous audit: the current shared authentication configuration has `ENABLE_FALLBACK: false` and `STRICT_GATEWAY: true`. Therefore, although the proxy contains direct-API fallback code, that fallback is disabled in the reviewed source configuration. It should remain an architectural concern, not be reported as an active production bypass.

## Critical findings

### SU-AUTH-024 — Missing gateway secret disables gateway-secret enforcement

P1 — Fail-open security control

Source: [Shared SkillUp authentication middleware](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L101-L118).

The middleware's gateway-secret check contains:

```
if (typeof INTERNAL_GATEWAY_SECRET !== 'string' || INTERNAL_GATEWAY_SECRET.length === 0) {
  return true;
}
```

If the secret is not configured, the check accepts the request.

Confirmed: The check fails open when the environment variable is absent.

Scope: This check applies to API routes that the middleware classifies as requiring a gateway secret. Other authentication checks may still protect individual routes.

Architectural requirement: A missing mandatory security credential must not silently disable the control.

### SU-AUTH-025 — Authentication middleware and learner API disagree about required identity claims

Sources: [Middleware identity validation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L141-L152) and [Learner identity validation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L93-L112).

The middleware requires both `originalUserId` and `shadowUserId`.

But the learner API guard accepts a token with no `shadowUserId` if `userId` exists.

That creates two incompatible definitions of a valid SkillUp identity.

Confirmed: The authentication contracts disagree.

Priority: P1. They should share one explicit identity-validation contract, with the original and shadow IDs preserved as distinct values.

### SU-AUTH-026 — Test-session endpoint can operate under a production Node environment with a preview override

Source: [Test-fixture authorization gate](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/test-fixture-session/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L16-L40).

The test-only endpoint checks several environment flags and requires a long shared secret with timing-safe comparison. Those are positive controls.

However, the `NODE_ENV === 'production'` restriction can be overridden by `PROJECT_LLM_ISOLATED_VERIFICATION === 'true'`, provided the other production markers do not identify the deployment as production.

Confirmed: `NODE_ENV=production` is not, by itself, a hard prohibition.

Conditional risk: A misconfigured production-like environment could enable a route that issues signed access tokens.

Priority: P1. Test-session issuance should be restricted by a deployment identity that cannot be relaxed through ordinary feature flags.

## Tutorial and learner API findings

### SU-TUTORIAL-001 — Tutorial progress bypasses the shared gateway routing abstraction

Source: [Progress GET upstream request](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/progress/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L39-L53) and [Progress POST upstream request](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/progress/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L92-L109).

Both handlers select the upstream server in this order:

`INTERNAL_API_URL` → `GATEWAY_URL` → hardcoded public API URL.

They then call `fetch()` directly instead of using the established shared gateway-first proxy.

Confirmed: Tutorial progress has an independent upstream routing path.

Risk: It can bypass the intended gateway boundary depending on environment configuration. It also introduces a hardcoded fallback endpoint.

Priority: P1 — architecture consistency and service trust.

### SU-TUTORIAL-002 — Progress API authenticates users but sends identity through service headers

The same handlers verify the learner's access token locally, then forward `X-User-ID`, `X-Brand` and internal credentials to the upstream API.

They do not forward the verified access token itself.

This may be a legitimate trusted-service design, but its safety depends on the receiving API requiring the internal credential and rejecting forged identity headers from untrusted callers.

Confirmed: The upstream identity is header-based.

Pending verification: The receiving tutorial route's exact authentication and ownership checks.

Priority: P1 — cross-service authorization contract.

### SU-TUTORIAL-003 — Subtopic progress route lacks UUID validation

Source: [ILS subtopic progress route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/subtopic/%5BsubtopicId%5D/progress/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L12-L33).

The handler inserts the route parameter directly into an upstream URL:

```
const url = `${apiUrl}/api/tutorial/ils/subtopic/${params.subtopicId}/progress`;
```

Unlike the general tutorial progress endpoint, it does not validate the identifier as a UUID.

Confirmed: Validation is inconsistent.

Priority: P2. Validate the parameter and construct the URL using the expected route contract.

### SU-TUTORIAL-004 — Upstream error messages can reach the learner

In the same route, the catch block returns `error.message` to the client.

A failure involving upstream configuration or request processing could therefore disclose internal implementation details.

Priority: P2 — error handling.

### SU-DATA-008 — Student dashboard and attendance responses lack explicit private caching controls

Sources: [Student dashboard API](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/student/dashboard/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and [Student attendance API](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/student/attendance/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

Both routes authenticate the learner and return their data, but neither explicitly sets `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

This is particularly relevant because the previously reviewed SkillUp service worker caches certain successful application responses.

Confirmed: These two API handlers do not set an explicit private caching policy.

Not confirmed: That these particular JSON responses are actually cached by the service worker.

Priority: P2 — privacy hardening.

## Placement handoff and session management

### SU-PLACEMENT-001 — Placement handoff forwards unnecessary incoming headers

Source: [Placement handoff request](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L61-L76).

The handler forwards the entire header collection produced by `createForwardHeaders(request)` to `placement.skillhubcore.in`.

That collection begins with browser request headers and may include cookies, authorization headers and internal service credentials.

The placement handoff already sends the access token explicitly in the JSON body, so forwarding the broader header collection is unnecessary.

Confirmed: Broad header forwarding occurs across this service boundary.

Priority: P1 — credential minimization. A narrow, explicit header allowlist is preferable.

### SU-PLACEMENT-002 — Placement redirect validation is incomplete

Source: [Redirect normalization](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L17-L23).

The handler accepts any string starting with `/` except one starting with `//`.

This prevents the most obvious protocol-relative redirect form, but it does not enforce a list of permitted destination routes or reject all unusual path encodings.

Priority: P2 — validate against the placement service's redirect policy.

### SU-SESSION-010 — Session revocation delegates authorization entirely to the backend

Sources: [Session collection route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/sessions/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and [Individual session route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/sessions/%5BsessionId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

The SkillUp BFF forwards session-listing and revocation requests without independently checking session ownership.

This is not necessarily a defect: the backend should be the authoritative enforcement point.

However, the earlier audit found that a backend token-revocation repository permits unscoped revocation when its optional user ID is omitted.

Priority: P1 — end-to-end verification required. The BFF's delegation and backend ownership checks must be tested together.

## Additional review results

The SkillUp login, signup, forgot-password, verify-email and refresh routes are small wrappers around the shared authentication proxy. Their primary risk is inherited from that proxy rather than from their own route bodies.

The reset-password route supports both GET and POST and delegates both to the upstream. Whether GET is appropriate depends on the backend contract; the wrapper alone does not establish a defect.

The shared middleware contains positive controls worth preserving: it verifies signed access tokens, requires both identity-bridge claims, compares the token brand against the request hostname, and protects React Server Component requests through the application matcher.

The reviewed `auth/config.ts` explicitly disables direct API fallback and enables strict gateway mode. This narrows the earlier fallback finding.

## Principal Architect assessment

The expanded audit reveals three architectural themes that deserve priority before feature work:

1. Identity consistency: SkillUp middleware and learner APIs must agree on original versus shadow user IDs.
2. Gateway trust boundaries: Tutorial and placement APIs need explicit rules for which headers, credentials and identity claims may cross service boundaries.
3. Authentication lifecycle: Cookie deletion, session ownership and test-token issuance require end-to-end verification.

The next larger review tranche should cover SkillUp's complete learner API inventory, batch and enrollment services, tutorial content APIs, and the actual backend handlers receiving tutorial-progress requests. That will move the audit beyond authentication into business logic, data integrity and learner authorization.

No code was changed. No tests were executed. No commits, pull requests or deployments were made.

# SkillUp Audit — 10 Related Tutorial and ILS Files

10 files · 728 source lines · SkillUp web application · Read-only review

This tranche covers SkillUp's Intelligent Learning System (ILS) tracking endpoints and tutorial-content delivery. I reviewed the full source of all ten files, including authentication, input handling, upstream routing, response handling and error paths.

## Findings

### SU-ILS-001 — Eight ILS endpoints repeat an inconsistent upstream-routing pattern

P1 — Service boundary

Examples: [Visit tracking](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/visit/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L26-L49) and [Node completion](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/complete-node/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L26-L40).

The endpoints independently select an upstream server using:

```
process.env.INTERNAL_API_URL ||
process.env.GATEWAY_URL ||
'https://api.skillhubcore.in'
```

This repeats the routing concern previously found in the general tutorial-progress API.

There is also a path inconsistency:

| Endpoint group                                                            | Upstream prefix          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Active time, block time, block completion, block visit, navigation, visit | `/tutorial/ils/...`      |
| Complete node                                                             | `/api/tutorial/ils/...`  |
| General progress                                                          | `/api/tutorial/progress` |
| Sections                                                                  | `/tutorial/sections/...` |

The differences may reflect gateway rewrites, but the BFF code does not establish a single canonical contract.

Confirmed: Routing is duplicated and path conventions differ.

Not yet confirmed: Which paths fail at runtime.

Recommendation: Verify the receiving routes, then centralize upstream URL construction and service authentication.

### SU-ILS-002 — Tracking payloads are accepted without schema validation

P1 — Data integrity

Sources: [Active-time handler](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/active-time/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L19-L39) and [Block-completion handler](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/block-completion/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L19-L39).

Six POST tracking handlers parse the incoming JSON into `unknown`, but do not validate the resulting structure before forwarding it.

This includes active time, block active time, block completion, block visit, complete node and visit.

A learner can therefore submit malformed or unrealistic tracking values to the BFF. The downstream API may reject them, but that protection is not established by these files.

Confirmed: No BFF-level schema validation.

Priority: P1 for verifying end-to-end integrity; final severity depends on backend validation.

### SU-ILS-003 — Client-controlled learning-session identifiers are forwarded without verification

Sources: [Block visit](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/block-visit/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L76-L87) and [Visit](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/visit/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L38-L49).

Both handlers forward the browser's `x-session-id` header directly to the backend.

They do not verify that the learning session belongs to the authenticated learner.

Confirmed: The session identifier is untrusted at this boundary.

Potential impact: Incorrect session attribution or cross-session tracking if the backend also omits ownership enforcement.

Priority: P1 — verify backend ownership.

### SU-ILS-004 — Several routes return internal exception messages to learners

Source: [Navigation error handler](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/navigation/%5BnodeId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L61-L66).

Multiple handlers return:

```
{ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Internal server error' }
```

This can reveal internal endpoint URLs, parsing failures or implementation details.

Confirmed: Internal exception messages can become HTTP response content.

Priority: P2 — error disclosure.

### SU-ILS-005 — Navigation and content identifiers lack consistent validation

Source: [Navigation parameter handling](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/navigation/%5BnodeId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L25-L40) and [Tutorial sections parameter handling](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/sections/%5BsubtopicId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L25-L33).

Navigation requires a nonempty `subtopicId`, but does not validate its format or the `nodeId`.

The sections route similarly interpolates `subtopicId` into a URL without validating it.

Priority: P2 — consistent input contracts.

### SU-ILS-006 — Tracking APIs have inconsistent error and response contracts

The six POST tracking routes follow nearly identical workflows, yet their error responses differ. Some return the entire upstream error object, others return only its `error` field, and others expose exception messages.

The inconsistent contracts increase frontend complexity and make it harder to distinguish validation failures, authorization failures and service outages.

Priority: P2 — API consistency and maintainability.

### SU-TUTORIAL-005 — Deprecated content endpoint remains active

Source: [Legacy tutorial content declaration](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/content/%5BsubtopicId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L6-L20).

The file explicitly states that `/api/tutorial/content/*` uses an incomplete or abandoned content system, while production pages use `/api/tutorial/sections/*`.

Nevertheless, the deprecated endpoint remains operational and proxies requests to the old backend path.

Confirmed: Two tutorial-content paths remain available.

Priority: P2 — migration and technical debt. Removal should follow caller inventory and compatibility checks, not precede them.

### SU-PRIVACY-001 — Legacy content endpoint logs the authenticated learner ID

Source: [Legacy endpoint logging](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/content/%5BsubtopicId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L28-L44).

The route logs the learner's full user ID alongside requested content identifiers and upstream URLs.

This is unnecessary personally linkable diagnostic data for an ordinary content read.

Priority: P2 — data minimization.

## Positive controls

The reviewed files also demonstrate several sound practices:

- All ten routes call `requireStudentAuth()` before accessing learner-specific backend data.
- Invalid JSON is rejected with HTTP 400 in the six tracking POST handlers.
- Interaction types are explicitly allowlisted to `quiz`, `practice`, `code`, `visual` and `completion`.
- Upstream requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.
- The sections endpoint returns `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
- The deprecated content endpoint includes deprecation headers, which support a controlled migration.

## Principal Architect assessment

The main issue is not ten isolated mistakes. It is that SkillUp's ILS API layer repeats authentication, routing, input parsing, identity forwarding and error handling without one consistent contract.

Before proposing implementation, the next audit should follow these ten routes into their actual API-server handlers, request schemas, ownership checks and database writes. That is necessary to determine which concerns are merely missing BFF defense-in-depth and which can actually corrupt learner progress or cross user boundaries.

This completes the requested 10-file, 500+-line review tranche. All findings are from static inspection of the selected feature branch. No tests were executed, and no code, database records, commits or deployments were changed.

# SkillUp Principal Architect Audit — Backend ILS Verification

This tranche follows the ten SkillUp tutorial endpoints reviewed previously into their corresponding API-server handlers. The purpose is to distinguish actual backend defects from missing validation at the SkillUp BFF layer.

The first important result is positive: the backend does validate ILS request bodies using Zod schemas, and its ILS routes call `validateRequest(request, { requireInternalSecret: true })` before trusting forwarded identity.

That means the earlier finding about unvalidated BFF payloads should not be described as proof that malformed learning data reaches the database. The backend provides a second validation boundary.

## SU-ILS-007 — Completion requirements are resolved server-side

Source: [Complete-node validation and service call](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/complete-node/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L69-L88).

The backend validates the completion request and calls `LearningProgressService.completeNavigationNode()` without accepting a client-supplied `requiredBlocks` list.

This is an important protection against learners simply declaring that all required blocks are complete.

Assessment: Positive control. The next verification point is the service's implementation of the canonical completion policy.

## SU-ILS-008 — Backend uses inconsistent sources for learning-session identity

P1 — Session integrity review

The backend ILS handlers do not all obtain learning-session identity in the same way:

- `active-time`, `visit` and `navigation` read `x-session-id` from the request header.
- `block-completion` and `block-visit` also pass a `sessionId` from the validated request body into their service methods.
- `block-active-time` constructs an identity without a session ID.

Confirmed: Session attribution differs across handlers.

Not established: Whether the service validates ownership and resolves conflicting header/body session IDs safely.

The service and repository must establish a single rule: a learning session belongs to the authenticated learner and cannot be reassigned by supplying another identifier.

## SU-ILS-009 — Navigation endpoint contains hardcoded forensic logging

Source: [Navigation forensic logging](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/navigation/%5BnodeId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L88-L98).

The endpoint searches every navigation response for one hardcoded block UUID and logs its version, active time, expected time and completion timestamp.

Confirmed: Temporary diagnostic logic remains in a general-purpose learner API.

Priority: P2 — observability hygiene. This should be removed or converted into a controlled diagnostic facility after its investigation is complete.

## SU-ILS-010 — Learning-session IDs are format-checked, not ownership-checked at the HTTP boundary

Source: [Session ID schema](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/schemas/ils.schemas.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L26-L28).

The schema accepts any nonempty string of up to 100 characters as a session ID.

That is valid input validation, but it does not prove ownership.

For example, `block-visit` passes the validated body `sessionId` directly into `LearningProgressService.recordBlockVisit()`.

Confirmed: The HTTP layer does not establish session ownership.

Pending: Whether the service or database repository binds that ID to the authenticated learner.

Priority: P1 — authorization verification.

## SU-ILS-011 — Internal service authentication uses ordinary string comparison

Source: [Internal secret validation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/middleware/internal-auth.middleware.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L64-L78).

The middleware checks the configured secret and fails closed if it is missing, which is correct.

However, it compares the received secret using ordinary string inequality instead of a timing-safe comparison.

Priority: P2 — security hardening. This is not evidence of a practical remote timing attack.

## SU-ILS-012 — Legacy tutorial interaction progress is a placeholder

Source: [Legacy interaction progress helper](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/_shared.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L81-L90).

`updateProgressForSection()` ignores its user and section parameters and returns progress calculated from an empty completed-sections array.

Confirmed: The helper does not persist or calculate actual learner progress.

Potential impact: Any live interaction route still using it would produce misleading progress.

Priority: P1 if called by active routes; otherwise P2 migration debt. Caller verification remains necessary.

### Architectural conclusion

The backend is stronger than the SkillUp BFF in two important respects: it requires internal-service authentication and validates ILS payloads before invoking business logic.

The highest-value remaining audit work is now inside `LearningProgressService`, its repositories and the actual interaction handlers. Those determine whether progress, time, completion and session attribution are enforced against authoritative learner records.

Review status: 12 backend and shared-dependency files inspected, 1,658 source lines. Findings are static-code observations; runtime exploitability and database behavior remain unverified. No code was modified and no tests were run.

# SkillUp Audit — Tutorial Interactions and Progress Integrity

Feature branch: `feature/project-llm-linux-worker` · Read-only source review

This review continues from the ILS backend into the actual quiz, practice, code, visual and completion handlers, together with their telemetry repository.

## SU-INTERACTION-001 — Quiz and practice scoring correctly use server-side answers

The quiz and practice endpoints retrieve the correct answer from the stored tutorial section rather than trusting the answer submitted by the learner.

Sources: [Quiz scoring](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/quiz/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L33-L77) and [Practice scoring](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/practice/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L28-L72).

Positive control: A learner cannot simply supply a different `correctAnswer` to make an incorrect selection score as correct.

The comments at the top of these files are outdated, but the executable scoring logic is more secure than those comments suggest.

## SU-INTERACTION-002 — Every interaction endpoint returns placeholder progress

P1 — Learning progress integrity

The shared `updateProgressForSection()` helper returns a calculation based on an empty completed-section list.

All five interaction routes call that helper after recording their respective activities.

Confirmed: Their returned `progress` value is not derived from the learner's actual recorded completion history.

This affects quiz, practice, code, visual and section-completion responses.

Recommendation: Establish one canonical progress calculation in the learning-progress domain service and retire the placeholder response contract.

## SU-INTERACTION-003 — Section completion trusts submitted time and score

Source: [Section completion recording](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/completion/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L21-L69).

The completion handler accepts `timeSpent` and `score` from the validated request and inserts them into `sectionCompletions`.

It does not independently calculate the score or verify completion requirements in this handler.

Confirmed: Completion evidence is not established at this HTTP layer.

Conditional impact: If this legacy completion table feeds official learner progress, assessments or certificates, client-supplied completion metrics could be treated as authoritative.

Priority: P1 — verify downstream consumers and completion policy.

## SU-INTERACTION-004 — Quiz and practice attempt numbering is vulnerable to concurrency

Sources: [Quiz attempt calculation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/quiz/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L71-L93) and [Practice attempt calculation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/practice/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L66-L89).

Both endpoints count existing attempts, calculate `previousAnswers.length + 1`, and insert the next answer separately.

Two concurrent submissions can read the same count and calculate the same attempt number.

Confirmed: The calculation is not atomic in these handlers.

Potential impact: Duplicate attempt numbers and inaccurate attempt histories, depending on database constraints.

Priority: P1 — assessment data integrity.

## SU-INTERACTION-005 — Quiz and practice statistics can misrepresent learner performance

Sources: [Quiz statistics](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/quiz/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L146-L159) and [Practice statistics](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/practice/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L142-L157).

The handlers calculate:

```
score = Math.round((correctAnswers / totalAttempts) * 100)
```

This is an attempt-level correctness rate, not necessarily a quiz score.

For example, if a learner answers one question incorrectly nine times and correctly once, the reported score is 10%, even though their latest answer is correct.

The code also reports `totalQuestions` as the number of distinct questions attempted, not the total questions available in the assessment.

Confirmed: The statistics have these semantics.

Priority: P2 — product correctness. The API should distinguish attempt accuracy, latest-attempt score, best score and question coverage.

## SU-INTERACTION-006 — Section completion has a check-then-insert race

Source: [Completion deduplication](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/completion/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L33-L69).

The handler checks whether a completion exists and then inserts a record.

Without an appropriate database uniqueness constraint and conflict-safe insertion, concurrent requests could both observe no existing completion.

Confirmed: The handler uses a non-atomic check-then-insert sequence.

Not yet verified: Whether database constraints prevent duplicates.

Priority: P1 — verify schema and concurrency behavior.

## SU-INTERACTION-007 — Quiz and practice logging includes answer-key values

Sources: [Quiz mismatch logging](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/quiz/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L60-L67) and [Practice mismatch logging](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/practice/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L55-L62).

When a submitted answer key differs from the authoritative answer, the handlers log both the client value and the correct answer.

Confirmed: Correct answers can enter application logs.

Priority: P2 — assessment confidentiality. Logging question identifiers and mismatch counts is generally sufficient.

## SU-TELEMETRY-001 — Event claiming has a useful atomic idempotency mechanism

Source: [Atomic telemetry event claim](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/block-telemetry-event.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L40-L59).

The telemetry repository inserts an event using `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` against `eventId`.

This is a sound foundation for preventing duplicate processing of retried active-time events.

However, the repository itself does not compare a duplicate event's payload with the original. Its documentation explicitly assigns that responsibility to the caller.

Assessment: Positive database pattern, with payload-immutability enforcement still requiring service-level verification.

### Principal Architect conclusion

The strongest finding in this tranche is not an authentication bypass. It is a split between two progress models:

- The newer ILS system has dedicated learning-progress services, block state and telemetry.
- The legacy interaction endpoints still write their own records and return placeholder progress.

Before changing either model, we need to establish which records are authoritative for learner dashboards, assessments and certificates.

The next priority is to inspect `LearningProgressService` and the navigation-progress and block-state repositories, particularly their ownership checks, transaction boundaries, completion rules and idempotency behavior.

No files were edited, no tests were run, and no commits or deployments were made.

Yes. `FinalAechitecture.md` is our architectural audit baseline, not merely a reference document. The SkillUp audit must assess every relevant file against its applicable requirements—not just identify security bugs.

That includes SOLID, DRY, KISS, YAGNI, separation of concerns, modularity, bounded contexts, dependency direction, maintainability, testability, scalability, performance, security, privacy, data integrity, brand isolation, and operational reliability.

I will also distinguish three types of findings:

- Confirmed defect: The implementation demonstrably violates a contract or produces incorrect behavior.
- Architectural deviation: The code conflicts with an explicit principle or boundary in `FinalAechitecture.md`, even if it works today.
- Verification required: The outcome depends on another service, database constraint, deployment configuration, or runtime behavior.

One important nuance from your architecture document: DRY does not mean extracting every repeated line into a shared package, and SOLID should not force unnecessary object-oriented abstractions. We should prefer the simplest maintainable design that preserves domain boundaries.

I am continuing with SkillUp's actual learning-progress implementation and related repositories, where we can evaluate both business correctness and these architectural principles.

## Architectural findings from the learning-progress service and repositories

### SU-ILS-013 — Subtopic progress uses sequential per-node database operations

P2 — Scalability and performance

Source: [Subtopic progress aggregation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L213-L243).

`getSubtopicProgress()` first loads progress records, then loops through them. For each node, it separately resolves required blocks and fetches block states.

For \\(N\\) nodes, this produces approximately \\(1 + 2N\\) repository-level operations, excluding any additional queries performed inside requirement resolution.

Confirmed: The service uses sequential per-node calls.

Architecture assessment: This conflicts with the scalability and efficient data-access objectives in `FinalAechitecture.md`.

Recommendation: Introduce batch repository methods where justified, avoiding an unnecessary new abstraction layer.

### SU-ILS-014 — Completion eligibility and completion persistence are separate operations

P1 — Concurrency verification

Sources: [Completion decision](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L487-L526) and [Completion persistence](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/tutorial-navigation-progress.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L687-L727).

The service loads progress, resolves canonical requirements, evaluates eligibility, and subsequently calls `completeNode()`.

The repository's `completeNode()` method performs the status update but does not re-evaluate the completion requirements.

Confirmed: Eligibility and persistence are not visibly enclosed in a single transaction in these methods.

Conditional risk: If required content or completion records change between those operations, a stale decision could be persisted.

Recommendation: Verify the content-version and transaction contract before deciding whether optimistic concurrency, version pinning or a transactional completion command is appropriate.

### SU-ILS-015 — Write operations return calculated progress without block telemetry state

P2 — Response correctness

Sources: [Visit response](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L298-L306) and [Completion response](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L519-L526).

Several write methods call `toDTO(updated, requiredBlocks, [])`, deliberately omitting block-state records.

By contrast, `getNavigationProgress()` loads actual block states before constructing its DTO.

Confirmed: Read and write paths supply different inputs to the same DTO transformation.

Pending: Whether this changes any public DTO field or only omits optional telemetry. That requires checking `toDTO()` and its tests.

### SU-ILS-016 — Progress repository uses recursive conflict retries without a fixed retry limit

Source: [Time-tracking conflict retry](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/tutorial-navigation-progress.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L447-L453) and [Visit conflict retry](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/tutorial-navigation-progress.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L554-L562).

The repository retries by calling its own method recursively after an insert conflict. The reviewed paths do not impose an explicit retry bound.

Confirmed: These retry paths are unbounded at the method level.

Architectural impact: This makes failure behavior harder to predict under contention and is less consistent with KISS and operational reliability than a bounded retry policy.

Priority: P2.

## Positive architectural findings

The newer ILS implementation demonstrates meaningful alignment with `FinalAechitecture.md`:

| Principle                    | Observed implementation                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SRP / separation of concerns | Business rules live in `LearningProgressService`; SQL mutations live in repositories     |
| Dependency inversion         | Navigation progress is injected through `ITutorialNavigationProgressRepository`          |
| DRY                          | Aggregation, validation and hierarchy resolution are separated into reusable modules     |
| Security                     | Progress operations use authenticated identity rather than request-body user IDs         |
| Data integrity               | Visit counters, time increments and block completion use atomic database expressions     |
| KISS                         | Explicit methods distinguish visits, time tracking, block completion and node completion |

These strengths should be preserved during remediation.

### Principal Architect conclusion

The primary architectural concern is now the coexistence of two learning-progress models. The newer ILS implementation has substantially better separation of responsibilities and server-side completion policy. The older interaction implementation still exposes placeholder progress and client-supplied completion metrics.

I would not merge or replace these systems without first tracing their consumers and establishing the authoritative learner-progress contract.

The next verification should focus on the remaining ILS helper modules, database schema constraints and existing service tests, especially for concurrent completion, duplicate telemetry and session ownership.

# SkillUp Audit — ILS Validation, Aggregation, SQL Helpers and Database Schemas

7 complete files · 848 source lines · Read-only review

This tranche checks the lower-level contracts supporting the previously reviewed learning-progress service.

## SU-ILS-017 — Missing canonical content is treated as zero required blocks

P1 — Completion integrity

Source: [Required-block resolution](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.hierarchy-resolution.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L47-L62).

The resolver returns an empty required-block list when the section is missing, its content is missing, or its blocks are missing.

Meanwhile, the aggregation policy defines zero required blocks as 100% progress, and the service permits completion when all required blocks are complete.

Confirmed: Missing content and intentionally empty content are represented by the same empty array.

Risk: If content disappears or becomes unavailable after hierarchy validation, the completion path may interpret that failure as a legitimately requirement-free page.

Recommendation: Distinguish “valid page with zero required blocks” from “canonical content unavailable.” This preserves KISS while making the domain contract explicit.

## SU-ILS-018 — Content-version and progress-version relationships need explicit enforcement

Source: [Navigation progress schema](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/tutorial-navigation-progress.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L53-L76).

The progress record stores completed block IDs and versions inside JSONB, plus a numeric row version.

However, the schema does not record the canonical content publication or revision against which the overall node-completion decision was made.

Confirmed: The reviewed table has no explicit content-revision reference.

Conditional risk: A completed node may retain a completion state after its required instructional blocks change.

Architecture principles: Data integrity, explicit version contracts, bounded-context consistency.

Recommendation: First determine the intended policy for content updates—grandfather completion, require revision, or recompute eligibility—then enforce it consistently.

## SU-ILS-019 — Learning-session validation checks presence, not authenticity

Source: [Session validation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.validation.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L47-L63).

`validateSessionId()` accepts any nonempty string. It does not establish whether the identifier belongs to the authenticated learner.

This confirms the contract gap noted in earlier ILS reviews.

Priority: P1 — end-to-end ownership verification. The proper fix is not simply requiring UUID syntax; the session must be tied to authenticated identity or issued by a trusted server.

## SU-ILS-020 — Event UUID validation is stronger than session ID validation

Source: [Telemetry event validation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.validation.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L115-L139).

Telemetry event IDs are validated against a UUID-shaped pattern. Learning-session IDs receive only a nonempty-string check.

That difference may be intentional because the identifiers have different origins. It should nevertheless be documented as part of the public ILS contract rather than left implicit.

Priority: P2 — API contract clarity.

## SU-ILS-021 — Telemetry and progress counters lack database-level nonnegative constraints

Sources: [Block telemetry counters](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/block-learning-state.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L47-L56) and [Navigation progress counters](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/tutorial-navigation-progress.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L59-L65).

The reviewed schemas define integer counters but no `CHECK` constraints enforcing nonnegative values.

The service and repository perform some validation, which is useful. Database constraints would provide an additional invariant if another writer or maintenance script bypasses those services.

Confirmed: These Drizzle schema definitions do not declare nonnegative checks.

Not yet verified: Whether SQL migrations add those constraints separately.

Priority: P2 — defense in depth.

## SU-ILS-022 — Progress percentage calculation repeatedly scans completed blocks

Source: [Progress percentage calculation](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.aggregation.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L110-L130).

For each required block, the calculation calls `.some()` on the completed-block array.

Its complexity is approximately \\(O(R \times C)\\), where \\(R\\) is required blocks and \\(C\\) is completed blocks.

For ordinary tutorial pages, this may be perfectly acceptable. If pages can contain large block histories, a `Set` of completed block/version pairs would reduce repeated scanning.

Priority: P3 — performance optimization only if profiling warrants it. KISS and YAGNI argue against changing this without evidence.

## SU-ILS-023 — Atomic database helpers correctly prevent several concurrency defects

Source: [Atomic JSONB completion](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/tutorial-navigation-progress-sql.helpers.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L33-L50).

The SQL helper checks whether a block/version pair already exists inside the current database row and appends it only if absent.

Other helpers calculate session transitions, revision increments and time accumulation inside database expressions.

Assessment: Positive control. These patterns are substantially stronger than the legacy quiz/practice attempt-numbering logic previously reviewed.

## SU-ILS-024 — Partial unique indexes protect active learner records

Sources: [Navigation progress unique index](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/tutorial-navigation-progress.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L77-L82) and [Block learning-state unique index](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/block-learning-state.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L68-L72).

Both schemas declare unique indexes that apply only to non-deleted records.

This is a sound way to support soft deletion while preventing duplicate active progress records.

The telemetry-events schema also enforces global uniqueness of `eventId`, which supports retry-safe event delivery.

Assessment: Positive control.

## 1. Findings

### SU-TEST-007 — Genuine concurrent duplicate-event testing exists

Positive control

The [D2-6 concurrency test](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/__tests__/d2-idempotent-delivery.integration.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L382-L431) submits two simultaneous `recordBlockActiveTime()` calls using the same event ID.

It asserts that exactly one event is processed, the other is identified as a duplicate, PostgreSQL contains one event row, and the block's active time increases only once.

Assessment: This is a meaningful integration test of idempotency and concurrent delivery, substantially stronger than the single-call mocked concurrency tests identified earlier.

Limit: The test has not been executed in this audit, so its current passing status is unknown.

### SU-TEST-008 — Rollback test proves database rollback, but not the full service transaction

P2 — Test coverage

Source: [D2-5 rollback test](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/__tests__/d2-idempotent-delivery.integration.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L323-L376).

The test opens a PostgreSQL transaction, inserts a telemetry event directly, deliberately throws an error and verifies the inserted event was rolled back.

That correctly proves transaction rollback at the database layer.

However, it does not force a failure inside the actual `LearningProgressService.recordBlockActiveTime()` transaction after the event claim but before the block-state update.

Confirmed gap: This particular test does not prove that the service's two related writes roll back together when the second operation fails.

Recommendation: Add a fault-injection integration test at the service transaction boundary. Preserve the existing database rollback test.
