## 1. Critical and high-priority findings

### SU-PROFILE-001 — Direct API bypass contradicts gateway-first design

P1 · Confirmed architectural inconsistency

File: [auth/bffProfileHandler.ts, lines 35–44 and 88–96](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/bffProfileHandler.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L35-L44)

The shared profile handler directly calls:

```
const res = await unifiedFetch(`${INTERNAL_API_URL}/auth/profile`, {
  method: 'GET',
  headers,
  cache: 'no-store',
});
```

The module explicitly describes this as bypassing the gateway.

Yet the previously reviewed `authBffRoute.ts` states that all authentication requests must go through the shared gateway.

Impact: Profile and onboarding-related identity requests can travel through different trust paths, creating inconsistent routing, observability, service authorization and deployment behavior.

Recommendation: Choose one authoritative internal communication contract. If direct authenticated service calls are a supported exception, document and verify that exception explicitly rather than contradicting the gateway-first rule.

### SU-PROFILE-002 — Full internal user identity appears in PATCH logs

P1/P2 · Confirmed logging issue

File: [auth/bffProfileHandler.ts, PATCH handler](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/bffProfileHandler.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The PATCH handler logs:

```
sendingUserId: headers['x-user-id']
```

It also logs the upstream API URL and authentication metadata.

The complete user ID should not be included in routine request diagnostics. The GET handler already uses partial identifiers, although even partial identifiers require an appropriate logging policy.

Recommendation: Centralize structured logging, use correlation IDs, remove full user IDs from ordinary log events, and restrict detailed authentication diagnostics to controlled debug environments.

### SU-ONBOARD-004 — Onboarding navigates to dashboard after persistence failure

P1 · Confirmed application logic defect

File: [OnboardingPage.tsx, lines 70–115](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/OnboardingEngine/components/OnboardingPage.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L70-L115)

Both `handleSkip()` and `handleComplete()` have this pattern:

```
try {
  await persistOnboarding(data, 'completed');
  router.replace('/dashboard');
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Onboarding completion failed:', error);
  router.replace('/dashboard');
}
```

The route therefore navigates to the dashboard whether onboarding persistence succeeds or fails.

The server may subsequently redirect the learner back to onboarding. That creates a potential redirect loop or confusing failure experience.

Recommendation: Preserve the current step, show a recoverable error, allow retry, and transition only after the authoritative backend confirms the requested state change.

### SU-ONBOARD-005 — Initialization animation controls business completion

P2 · Confirmed design defect

File: [InitializationStep.tsx, lines 15–51](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/OnboardingEngine/components/InitializationStep.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L15-L51)

The component increments progress using an interval and calls `onComplete()` after the visual progress reaches 100%.

This means onboarding persistence is triggered by an animation, rather than the animation representing actual persistence progress.

The effect also depends on an `onComplete` function created during the parent render, which can cause the effect to restart when the callback identity changes.

Recommendation: Start persistence as an explicit action, let the animation reflect its state, and make completion or failure depend on the actual API response.

### SU-AUTH-011 — Login redirect target is used without local validation

P1/P2 · Security investigation

File: [AuthPage.tsx, login submission handler](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/AuthPage.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The login handler reads:

```
const redirectTarget = searchParams.get('redirect');
const destination = sessionState.onboardingCompleted === true
  ? redirectTarget || '/dashboard'
  : '/onboarding';

window.location.assign(destination);
```

There is no visible validation requiring a same-origin, application-relative redirect destination.

Impact: A manipulated redirect parameter could steer a newly authenticated user to an external destination.

Recommendation: Accept only approved relative paths and reject external schemes, protocol-relative URLs, backslashes and other ambiguous forms.

This is a potential open-redirect exposure; it has not been tested in a browser.

### SU-AUTH-012 — Client session-state retrieval treats unavailable auth as incomplete onboarding

P2 · Confirmed behavioral issue

File: [auth/authLoader.ts, lines 57–85](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/authLoader.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L57-L85)

`fetchCurrentUserState()` returns `{ onboardingCompleted: false }` when `validateAuthState()` returns no authenticated state.

This combines two different conditions: an authenticated learner who has not completed onboarding, and an unsuccessful or unavailable session-state check.

Recommendation: Use distinct states for authenticated/incomplete, authenticated/complete, unauthenticated and temporarily unavailable. Do not infer onboarding status from a failed authentication-state lookup.

## 4. Architectural decisions

The review supports keeping shared components and brand configuration. The structural problem is not that UI is shared; it is that shared UI sometimes owns authentication transitions, business workflow completion and synthetic performance interpretation.

Recommended boundaries:

```
SkillUp-web UI
   |
   +-- Authentication state presentation
   |       |
   |       +-- Shared auth BFF / gateway
   |
   +-- Onboarding form presentation
   |       |
   |       +-- Validated onboarding command
   |                |
   |                +-- Authoritative user service
   |
   +-- Dashboard visualization
           |
           +-- Learner dashboard read model
                    |
                    +-- Authoritative progress
                    +-- Authoritative assessments
                    +-- Authoritative attendance
                    +-- Authoritative sessions
```

The UI should not infer business completion from timers, invent mastery scores, or silently turn failed persistence into successful navigation.

## 5. Verification and acceptance criteria

Before closing this portion of the audit, I would require automated coverage for successful and failed onboarding persistence, redirect URL validation, session-state outages, profile BFF authorization and upstream failures, dashboard action behavior, zero-goal progress handling and accessible form controls.

Audit conclusion: The 28-file tranche is reviewed at the source level, with 12 actionable findings documented. A production-ready approval remains blocked by onboarding workflow correctness, profile routing inconsistency, authentication redirect handling and the broader learner-data integrity issues already identified.

No commits, pull requests, code edits, migrations, builds or tests were performed.

Repository: `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`\
Branch: `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`\
Scope: Learner-facing application, tutorial BFF routes, shared branding, authentication, and student APIs.

Files verified

New findings

Code changes

All 40 files were fetched successfully from the feature branch. Several were deliberately revisited to verify cross-file behavior. The 1,186-line landing page received focused inspection rather than exhaustive line-by-line certification.

## 1. New findings

### SU-BRAND-002 — Missing dashboard provider silently selects another brand

P1 · Confirmed

Two separate brand context implementations use incompatible fallback policies.

In [OnboardingEngine/context/BrandContext.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/OnboardingEngine/context/BrandContext.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1-L19), a missing provider throws an error.

In [PostLandingPage/app/context/BrandContext.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/PostLandingPage/app/context/BrandContext.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1-L20), it silently returns `rthConfig`:

```
if (!brand) {
  return rthConfig;
}
```

This second context is used by SkillUp's dashboard components.

Risk: A missing or incorrectly composed provider can render RealTutorialHub branding inside a SkillUp experience without exposing a configuration error.

This is a confirmed brand-isolation defect in the fallback behavior, not evidence of a cross-brand database leak.

Remediation: Make the brand context strict, enforce one explicit provider contract, and test SkillUp dashboard rendering without and with its provider.

### SU-AUTH-013 — Authentication response mapper reports success for missing payloads

P2 · Confirmed

File: [auth/authMapper.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/authMapper.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1-L31)

The mapper returns:

```
return {
  success: true,
  user: response?.user,
  expiresAt: response?.expiresAt ?? null,
};
```

It does not validate that a successful upstream response contains the expected authenticated-session data.

The caller checks HTTP status, but a malformed successful JSON payload can still be mapped as success.

Remediation: Validate the successful authentication response against a schema before creating a successful view model.

### SU-PAYMENT-003 — Paid installments can be visually treated as overdue

P2 · Confirmed

File: [student/payments/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/student/payments/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The page computes:

```
const overdue =
  installment.status === 'overdue' ||
  isPastDue(installment.dueDate);
```

A paid installment with an old due date therefore receives the overdue background styling, even while its status badge says paid.

Remediation: Derive overdue presentation only for unpaid installments. The payment domain should own the authoritative overdue state; the UI can use dates for supplementary explanations.

### SU-ONBOARD-008 — Onboarding field mappings and selectable values are not fully normalized

P2 · Confirmed mapping inconsistency

File: [constants/fieldMappings.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/constants/fieldMappings.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The onboarding model uses IDs such as `learn-skills` and `web-dev`, while the shared field mappings recognize different forms for some goals, including underscore-separated variants.

The code does not establish one universally accepted representation across every UI selection, cookie, and database mapping.

Remediation: Establish canonical domain IDs and goal IDs and make mappings explicit at boundaries. Add round-trip tests for every selectable option.

### SU-ILS-017 — Several learner-event BFFs lack consistent runtime request schemas

P2 · Confirmed

The reviewed ILS handlers for active time, block completion, block visits, node completion and general visits parse JSON but generally do not validate the parsed object before forwarding it.

The legacy tutorial-progress handler, by contrast, uses Zod schemas.

Backend validation may already reject malformed records. Therefore this is a BFF contract-consistency finding, not proof of unauthorized writes.

Remediation: Standardize request validation without duplicating the backend's authoritative business rules.

### SU-CACHE-004 — Offline cache policy applies to all successful navigations

P1 · Reconfirmed with full source

File: [app/sw.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/sw.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L37-L67)

The service worker caches successful navigation responses regardless of whether the route is authenticated:

```
if (
  response.ok &&
  (request.mode === 'navigate' || url.pathname.startsWith('/_next/'))
) {
  await cache.put(request, response.clone());
}
```

No privacy-header, logout or account-isolation check is visible.

Required action: Restrict caching to explicitly public, safe assets and implement tests covering account switching, logout and offline behavior.

## 2. Cross-file review: tutorial delivery and identity

The tutorial BFF group was revisited together. This confirms that the SkillUp app has multiple independent request-building patterns:

| API family                 | Authentication       | Validation                       | Caching             |
| -------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| Legacy tutorial progress   | `requireStudentAuth` | Zod UUID/body schemas            | `no-cache`          |
| Tutorial sections          | `requireStudentAuth` | No visible local UUID validation | `private, no-store` |
| ILS visit/block visit      | `requireStudentAuth` | JSON parse, no visible schema    | `fetch` no-store    |
| ILS active-time/completion | `requireStudentAuth` | JSON parse, no visible schema    | `fetch` no-store    |
| Interaction proxy          | `requireStudentAuth` | Interaction-type allowlist       | `fetch` no-store    |

A `fetch` configured with `cache: 'no-store'` does not by itself guarantee the browser-facing API response will have `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

The routes also do not consistently normalize `/api` prefixes or forward the same service credentials.

Architectural decision: These handlers should share a focused authenticated internal client responsible for URL construction, brand context, identity propagation, credentials, timeouts, cache policy and error translation.

## 4. Principal Architect decision

The 40-file tranche confirms that the largest architectural risks are not caused by React component structure. They arise where presentation and platform boundaries meet:

1. Brand context must never silently switch tenant identity.
2. User-specific API responses must have consistent privacy guarantees.
3. Learning events must have consistent identity, validation and ownership rules.
4. Payments and assessments must display authoritative states rather than derived or static substitutes.
5. The real learner UI must connect to authoritative course and assessment data.

The positive patterns—thin protected student routes, central authentication verification, schema validation in progress APIs and accessible calendar controls—should be retained.

Audit status: 40 files verified in this round, with previously reviewed defects rechecked and new source findings recorded. This is not a declaration of full application coverage or production security certification. The long landing page and downstream service/database contracts remain incompletely verified.

No code was changed. No tests, builds, migrations or deployments were executed.

This tranche covers 40 verified source files, mostly previously unreviewed backend dependencies. I inspected line-indexed implementation details and traced key calls between the API, service, repository and schema layers. For large files, this was a targeted source inspection rather than a claim that every line received independent certification.

## 1. Highest-priority findings

### SU-PROGRESS-006 — Legacy progress endpoint trusts an identity header locally

Priority: P1 investigation

File: [apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/progress/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/progress/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Lines 46–49 extract `x-user-id` directly:

```
function extractUserId(request: NextRequest): string | null {
  return request.headers.get('x-user-id');
}
```

Both GET and POST use that value to select or update learner progress. Unlike the newer ILS routes, this handler does not visibly call `validateRequest()`.

Confirmed: This route contains no local verification that the supplied user ID came from an authenticated, trusted service.

Not yet proven: Whether an external caller can reach it without gateway enforcement. That depends on the deployed upstream boundary and routing controls.

Required correction: Apply the common trusted-authentication contract at this endpoint, or establish and test an equivalent enforced upstream guard.

### SU-PROGRESS-007 — Legacy progress updates are vulnerable to lost updates

Priority: P1/P2, depending on usage

File: [packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/tutorial-progress.repository.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/tutorial-progress.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Lines 61–116 follow a read-modify-write sequence:

1. Read existing progress.
2. Merge a newly completed block into the previously read JSON array.
3. Write the merged array back.
4. Increment the version number.

The update does not compare the previously read version in its `WHERE` clause.

Two concurrent completions may therefore calculate different snapshots from the same old record, and the last writer can overwrite the other completion.

The newer navigation-progress implementation has atomic SQL helpers, so the architecture already contains a better approach.

Recommendation: Retire this write path when possible. Otherwise, use atomic JSONB updates or optimistic concurrency with compare-and-swap and bounded retries.

### SU-PROGRESS-008 — Missing tutorial content can be interpreted as 100% complete

Priority: P1/P2 investigation

Files:

- [learning-progress.hierarchy-resolution.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.hierarchy-resolution.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [learning-progress.aggregation.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/learning-progress.aggregation.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The hierarchy resolver returns an empty required-block list when a section or its blocks are missing:

```
if (!section || !section.content || !section.content.blocks) {
  return [];
}
```

The aggregation function considers zero required blocks fully complete:

```
if (requiredBlocks.length === 0) {
  return 100;
}
```

These two rules create an important semantic ambiguity.

An intentionally informational page with no mandatory learning blocks may legitimately be considered complete. But a missing, malformed or unpublished section must not automatically receive the same interpretation.

Recommendation: Distinguish content unavailable from valid content with zero instructional requirements. Check the complete service call path before classifying this as an exploitable completion bypass.

### SU-TUTORIAL-V2-003 — Brand-specific tutorial precedence is not deterministic

Priority: P2, previously suspected and corroborated

Files:

- [tutorial-delivery.service.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/services/tutorial-delivery.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [tutorial-section.repository.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/tutorial-section.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The retrieval logic accepts both shared and requested-brand content, but the inspected lookup does not consistently establish that brand-specific content takes precedence over shared content.

This matters because these may be distinct instructional variants, not interchangeable records.

Recommended invariant: Exact brand match first, explicitly shared fallback second, with deterministic version/publication selection.

### SU-CACHE-005 — Personalized legacy progress responses permit storage

Priority: P1/P2, reconfirmed

The API's legacy progress GET and POST routes return:

```
Cache-Control: no-cache
```

That is weaker than `private, no-store` for learner-specific progress responses.

The learner application's service worker was previously found to cache successful navigations without a privacy-aware policy.

Recommendation: Enforce a single no-store response policy for personalized tutorial progress at every API and BFF boundary.

## 2. Positive architectural findings

The review also confirmed several useful safeguards that should be retained.

Internal authentication: The newer ILS API routes call `validateRequest(request, { requireInternalSecret: true })` before constructing the learner identity. The middleware rejects missing or invalid internal secrets in this mode. This is substantially stronger than relying on identity headers alone.

Self-scoped learning operations: The new Learning Progress Service receives an `AuthenticatedIdentity` and generally uses `identity.userId` for progress operations rather than accepting a target user ID from the request body.

Database concurrency: The block-learning repository uses PostgreSQL conflict handling, while navigation-progress SQL helpers provide atomic increments and JSONB updates. These are appropriate building blocks for event-driven progress tracking.

Database uniqueness: The schemas define partial unique indexes for active learner/navigation records and block-learning identities. Telemetry events also have a unique event ID for deduplication.

API validation: The ILS routes use Zod request schemas and return explicit validation failures. The newer API layer is materially more structured than the legacy progress route.

## 5. Principal Architect decision

The backend review strengthens the case for making the new ILS progress engine the authoritative learner-progress implementation, subject to closure of its remaining correctness and isolation questions.

The immediate order of engineering work should be:

1. Verify and enforce the authentication boundary on the legacy progress endpoint.
2. Resolve the global-user versus brand-local-user identity contract.
3. Eliminate concurrent lost-update behavior in any remaining active legacy progress writes.
4. Separate unavailable content from legitimately zero-requirement content.
5. Make shared versus brand-specific tutorial delivery deterministic.
6. Establish integration tests for concurrent events, session ownership, cross-brand isolation and caching.

These are recommendations only; no implementation was performed.

Final status for this tranche: 40 source files retrieved and reviewed at the architecture and implementation level. Security-sensitive branches and data-integrity paths received targeted scrutiny; exhaustive line-by-line certification of the largest files is still pending. Several findings are source-confirmed, while exploitation and runtime effects remain unverified.

Repository unchanged. No builds, tests, migrations, deployments, commits or pull requests.

Yes, correct. As Principal Architect, I should review the actual source code line by line, file by file, and page by page, including the backend and database dependencies of each page.

That means more than fetching files and identifying suspicious patterns. For every relevant file, I need to understand its complete implementation, trace its callers and dependencies, verify its architectural responsibilities, and document issues with precise line references.

## How many more audit rounds?

My current planning estimate is 6–8 additional rounds of approximately 40 files each, followed by a final consolidation and verification round.

That is a planning estimate, not a verified count of remaining unread files. The previous audits contain repeated file reviews, and some large files received targeted inspections rather than complete line-by-line examination. Counting those as fully completed would overstate our progress.

## What remains before I can sign off?

| Audit stage                         | Remaining work                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Source inventory                 | Establish the exact file list on the authoritative branch, excluding generated and irrelevant files |
| 2. SkillUp frontend                 | Certify each route, page, component, state transition and user action                               |
| 3. Authentication and authorization | Trace JWT, gateway, brand identity, cookies, headers and permissions end to end                     |
| 4. Backend services                 | Review controller-to-service-to-repository logic                                                    |

| 6. Tutorial and assessments         | Validate content delivery, ILS, completion, event tracking and assessment correctness               |
| 7. Quality and security             | Review tests, PWA caching, configuration, error handling and operational safeguards                 |
| 8. Final certification              | Reconcile findings with the architecture, identify unresolved blockers and issue a final verdict    |

For each file, I will record its path, line count, review status, findings, severity, architectural compliance and any dependencies requiring further inspection.

There is one important distinction: a completed code audit is not the same as production certification. Because we are operating read-only, I can assess source correctness and test coverage, but runtime security and database behavior that require executing tests must remain unverified until explicitly authorized.

## My completion criteria

I will not declare the audit complete until:

- Every in-scope file has been accounted for.
- Large files have been read completely, not merely sampled.
- Each learner-facing page has been traced to its real data source.
- Critical authentication and database flows have been checked end to end.
- Existing findings have been deduplicated and revalidated.
- Remaining risks are documented with exact evidence.
- A final architecture compliance report and prioritized remediation plan are ready.

My recommendation: Plan for 6–8 more substantial audit rounds, plus one final consolidation round, and adjust that number after establishing an exact unique-file coverage ledger.

I will prioritize completeness and accuracy over meeting an arbitrary round count.

# Round 1 — SkillUp-web Principal Architect Audit

Scope: Learner-facing pages and their execution paths\
Branch: `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`\
Review mode: Read-only, with source-level evidence and no tests or code changes.

The first part of Round 1 has revealed a significant architectural distinction: some pages explicitly validate the learner's session, while others delegate directly to shared components without a visible route-level authentication check. That does not establish an authorization bypass, because middleware and downstream services may still enforce access. It does mean the authorization contract must be traced through every layer.

### Finding R1-001 — Inconsistent authentication at exam entry points

P1 investigation

[launch-exam/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/launch-exam/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com) calls `validateAuthState()` and redirects unauthenticated users.

However, [exam/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/exam/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com) directly calls `loadExamSessionData(examId)` and renders the exam engine. [result/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/result/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com) likewise delegates to a shared result component.

Required verification: Confirm that exam-session loading, result retrieval and all related mutation endpoints enforce the authenticated learner's ownership of the requested exam. A page-level check alone is insufficient, but the absence of one requires verifying the downstream boundary.

### Finding R1-002 — Learning-path page is hardwired to Python Lists

P2 · Confirmed

[learning-path/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/learning-path/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com) uses static metadata specifically describing Python Lists — Part 1 and renders a generic `TutorialPage` without a course or subtopic identifier.

That makes this route unsuitable as a genuinely personalized learning-path entry point without additional selection logic inside the shared component.

Recommendation: Define whether `/learning-path` represents a general learner path or a specific lesson. If general, it needs dynamic learner context and appropriate metadata.

### Finding R1-003 — Dashboard and onboarding use different auth-state readers

P2 · Confirmed architectural inconsistency

[dashboard/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com) uses `validateAuthState()`, whereas [onboarding/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/onboarding/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com) uses `fetchBackendAuthState()`.

Those shared functions were previously found to construct upstream requests differently.

Risk: When gateway configuration, forwarding headers or profile-service availability differ, a learner could pass one page's authentication check but fail the other's.

Recommendation: Consolidate the authenticated-session read model and use a separate, explicitly scoped service to load optional profile data.

## 2. Further confirmed findings

### R1-004 — Tutorial dashboard displays fabricated learner achievements

P1 · Confirmed

File: [tutorialDashboardData.ts, lines 106–145 and 222–251](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/tutorialDashboardData.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L106-L145)

The tutorial dashboard assigns a fixed learner name, 16-day streak, 2,450 XP, level 12, assessment scores, assignments, projects and career statistics.

These are not retrieved from authenticated learner records.

Required action: Replace the static dashboard dataset with an authenticated read model. Until then, identify the page as a demonstration rather than a genuine learner-progress dashboard.

### R1-005 — Exam route silently loads a demo examination

P1/P2 · Confirmed

File: [examSessionLoader.ts, lines 305–310](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/ExamEngine/components/examSessionLoader.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L305-L310)

When `examId` is missing, `loadExamSessionData()` returns a hardcoded demo examination containing a fictional student identity and questions.

```
if (typeof examId === 'string' && examId.trim() !== '') {
  return loadRealExamSessionData(examId.trim());
}

return mapExamApiToSessionData(demoExamApiResponse);
```

A demo is acceptable as an explicit demonstration mode, but it should not silently replace a missing real examination.

Required action: Separate `/exam/demo` from authenticated examination sessions and return a controlled error or redirect when an actual examination ID is missing.

### R1-006 — Program discovery has conflicting public-access assumptions

P1/P2 · Confirmed contract inconsistency

Files:

- [programs/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/programs/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [api/programs/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/programs/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [programs/\[slug\]/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/programs/%5Bslug%5D/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The page and site navigation treat the program catalog as public. The API, however, rejects unauthenticated requests.

The previously reviewed `fetchSkillupApi()` then falls back to direct database helpers for program requests that fail.

Risk: The same public page has different access and data-loading semantics depending on which backend path succeeds.

Required action: Make a deliberate product decision about public program visibility, then apply it consistently to the API, frontend, database access and search indexing.

### R1-007 — Email verification trusts an upstream redirect destination

P1 investigation

File: [verify-email/page.tsx, lines 17–55](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/verify-email/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L17-L55)

After successful verification, the client follows `payload.redirectUrl` using `window.location.assign()` without validating its origin.

Because this value comes from the authenticated verification API response, exploitability depends on whether that backend strictly controls it.

Required action: Validate redirect destinations against approved application origins or use a server-defined destination.

### R1-008 — Placement redirect validation accepts ambiguous paths

P2 · Confirmed

File: [placement/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/placement/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The redirect validator checks for a leading `/` and excludes `//`, but does not enforce a canonical destination path or reject all potentially ambiguous path representations.

The placement client subsequently concatenates the accepted path to the placement-service origin.

Required action: Parse and normalize the destination using the target service's URL contract and allow only approved placement routes.

### R1-009 — Public sitemap depends on fallback-capable program data

P2 · Confirmed

File: [sitemap.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/sitemap.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The sitemap calls `getSkillupPrograms()` directly to publish program URLs.

That data helper has previously been confirmed to return fallback programs when normal retrieval fails.

Risk: Search engines can receive URLs for demonstration or unavailable programs.

Required action: Generate the sitemap exclusively from the authoritative published program catalog.

### R1-010 — Brand theme settings disagree

P3 · Confirmed

## 4. Round 1 assessment

Architecture acceptance

Not approved

Acceptance is blocked by unresolved exam authorization, fabricated operational data and inconsistent authentication and catalog contracts.

Round 2 examined 40 files on the feature branch. Smaller handlers and components were inspected fully; several large shared modules received focused call-chain and branch analysis. Consequently, this is 40 files assessed, not yet 40 files exhaustively certified line by line.

## 1. Key findings

### R2-001 — Exam result display invents performance metrics

P1 · Confirmed

File: [ExamSummaryReport.tsx, lines 105–254](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/ExamSummaryReport.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L105-L254)

The result component substitutes fixed values when real metrics are absent or zero.

Examples include:

```
const correctCount =
  answeredQuestions.filter((q) => q.isCorrect === true).length
  || (result.score ?? 12);

const percentile = result.percentile || 76;
```

It also fabricates concept counts, a completion date, skill scores, total time and fastest/slowest question metrics.

Impact: A learner with zero correct answers can be presented with a positive score derived from fallback data. Missing results can appear as measured achievement.

Required action: Remove fabricated operational metrics. Treat zero as a legitimate value, distinguish unavailable metrics from real results, and show explicit empty states.

### R2-002 — Result page can remain indefinitely in a loading state after an error

P1/P2 · Confirmed

File: [ExamSummaryReport.tsx, lines 71–85](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/ExamSummaryReport.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L71-L85)

The code evaluates:

```
if (loading || !result) {
  return /* loading spinner */;
}

if (error || result.status === 'processing') {
  return /* error / processing view */;
}
```

When a fetch fails, it sets `error` and clears `loading`, but `result` remains `null`.

The first condition still succeeds, displaying the loading spinner rather than the error message.

Required action: Handle errors before the missing-result loading condition and provide an explicit retry action.

### R2-003 — Exam timer uses client-local countdown state

P1/P2 · Confirmed design risk

File: [ExamEngine.tsx, lines 37–80](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/ExamEngine/components/ExamEngine.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L37-L80)

The exam timer parses the server-provided time label into seconds, then decrements local state every second.

It also calls exam submission when that countdown reaches zero.

Problems include:

- Timer accuracy depends on browser scheduling.
- A suspended tab can cause the visual countdown to drift.
- The code does not derive the remaining time from an authoritative server expiration timestamp.
- Auto-submission is initiated from a React state update callback.

Required action: Use an immutable server-defined examination deadline. The backend must independently reject late answers and enforce expiration.

This review confirms the client-side design weakness; server-side deadline enforcement remains to be verified in the exam engine and command handlers.

### R2-004 — Previous-question navigation can bypass answer persistence

P2 · Confirmed

File: [ExamEngine.tsx, lines 105–157](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/ExamEngine/components/ExamEngine.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L105-L157)

`handleNext()` attempts to save the current answer before navigating, but `handlePrev()` changes the question index without saving.

The selected answer remains in local React state, so normal backward navigation need not immediately lose it. However, a reload or unexpected interruption can lose unsaved answers.

Required action: Define one answer-persistence policy for every navigation path, including question jumps, previous/next controls, tab closure and submission.

### R2-005 — Mark-for-review state is not visibly persisted

P2 · Confirmed frontend behavior

File: [ExamEngine.tsx, lines 297–307](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/ExamEngine/components/ExamEngine.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L297-L307)

The mark-for-review button only updates `markedQuestionIds` in local React state.

No corresponding server request is visible in that action.

Impact: A reload or resumed exam can lose marks created during the current session.

Required action: Persist review flags to the authoritative exam session.

### R2-006 — Backend result ownership verification is present

Positive finding · Source confirmed

File: [api-server quiz/result/route.ts, lines 20–47](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/quiz/result/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L20-L47)

The backend verifies the user access token, fetches the requested examination and explicitly checks that its `userId` matches the authenticated token identity.

Similarly, [quiz/state/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/quiz/state/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) calls `SessionService.resumePayload(examId, payload.userId)`.

Conclusion: Round 1's concern about absent page-level auth is partially resolved. The result endpoint has an explicit ownership guard; the state service still requires inspection to verify its internal ownership handling.

### R2-007 — The result/report API can perform scoring during a GET

P2 investigation

File: [quiz/result/route.ts, lines 55–80](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/quiz/result/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L55-L80)

A result GET may invoke `ScoringEngine.calculateExamResults()` when processing is pending or a completed exam contains unevaluated answers.

This makes an otherwise read-oriented endpoint capable of changing grading state.

Risk: Concurrent result requests may initiate overlapping scoring operations unless the scoring service enforces idempotency and locking.

Required verification: Inspect the scoring engine's transaction and concurrency behavior. Ideally scoring should occur in a controlled job or command flow.

### R2-008 — Report subcomponents also contain hardcoded statistics

P2 · Confirmed

Files:

- [DifficultyPerformanceCard.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/components/report/DifficultyPerformanceCard.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [ConceptPerformanceCard.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/components/report/ConceptPerformanceCard.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [MetricsSummaryBar.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/components/report/MetricsSummaryBar.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The difficulty card creates invented scores when metric groups are missing.

The concept card renders fixed progress bar widths of 85%, 55%, and 35%, regardless of actual concept counts.

The metrics summary always displays `totalQuestions / totalQuestions` as questions attempted, even when some questions were skipped.

Required action: Make report cards pure renderers of validated server metrics, with explicit absence states.

### R2-009 — The launch configuration includes static catalog data

P2 investigation

File: [launchExamPageData.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/launchExamPageData.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The launch view model includes hardcoded domain, subject, topic and subtopic configuration data.

The active exam-start backend uses authenticated commands and schema validation, but the configuration interface must be checked against live catalog identity and availability.

Required action: Verify that every selectable configuration ID corresponds to an authorized, existing, published scope.

## 3. Principal Architect verdict

Round 2: Source review completed for 40 files; production acceptance not approved.

I recommend addressing these areas in order:

1. Remove synthetic scores and misleading report fallbacks.
2. Fix result-error state handling.
3. Verify deadline and answer-ownership enforcement inside exam commands and services.
4. Make saving, navigation and review marks resilient to reloads.
5. Verify scoring concurrency and idempotency.
6. Connect launch configuration to an authoritative, validated exam catalog.

The next audit tranche should concentrate on `SessionService`, `ExamEngine.completeExam`, `SubmitAnswerCommand`, scoring, report generation and database constraints. Those are the remaining dependencies needed to resolve the highest-severity Round 2 investigations.

No repository changes, tests, builds or deployments were performed.

Repository: `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`\

Round 3 traced the actual backend implementation behind the exam routes from Round 2. I reviewed all 40 files at source level, inspected critical logic with line numbers, and read selected execution paths in depth. Several large files, including the 768-line report engine, still require further full-line certification. I will not present their targeted inspection as a complete line-by-line sign-off.

## 1. High-priority findings

### R3-001 — Answer endpoint can acknowledge an answer that was not saved

P1 · Confirmed

File: [exam.engine.ts, lines 305–330](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L305-L330)

The `submitAnswer()` method fetches the exam-question record. If no matching record exists, it logs an error but does not throw.

Execution then continues toward updating the examination timestamp and completing the command.

This creates a path where an answer request can return success without persisting an answer to an actual question.

Correction: Treat a missing exam-question record as an explicit not-found or invalid-question failure. Add an API test asserting that success is impossible without a corresponding stored answer.

### R3-002 — Scoring logs answer keys and user responses

P1 · Confirmed information exposure to logs

File: [scoring.engine.ts, lines 269–279](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/scoring-engine/scoring.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L269-L279)

The scoring engine logs both:

```
rawUserAnswer,
resolvedScoringAnswer: scoringAnswer,
resolvedCorrectAnswer: scoringCorrectAnswer,
```

This exposes assessment answer keys and learner responses to application logs.

Correction: Remove answer contents and answer keys from production diagnostics. Log opaque question identifiers, evaluation outcome, durations and correlation IDs instead.

### R3-003 — Submission transaction does not visibly lock exam state

P1 investigation · Concurrency

File: [exam.engine.ts, lines 490–545](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L490-L545)

Inside `completeExam()`, the transaction reads the current status and later updates the exam to `processing`.

The inspected code does not use a row lock or a conditional status transition from `started` to `processing`.

Two concurrent submit requests may both observe a started examination before either commits.

Required verification: Run a real PostgreSQL concurrency test. The source supports a race-condition concern; it does not establish the precise production outcome.

Correction: Enforce an atomic status transition and make subsequent submission attempts idempotently return the existing result.

### R3-004 — Session recovery can trigger repeated scoring operations

P1/P2 investigation

File: [session.service.ts, lines 63–80](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/session.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L63-L80)

For an expired examination, `syncSession()` directly changes its status to `processing` and launches scoring asynchronously.

The update is based on the exam state already read, potentially from a two-minute cache, without an explicit status condition.

Repeated recovery requests could therefore attempt scoring again.

Correction: Expiration processing should claim the examination atomically, then dispatch one durable scoring job.

### R3-005 — Scoring failure updates state outside the declared transition contract

P2 · Confirmed

Files:

- [scoring.engine.ts, lines 364–380](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/scoring-engine/scoring.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L364-L380)
- [exam.state-machine.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.state-machine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The state machine says exam statuses should be changed through its transition logic.

However, the scoring error handler first directly writes `status = 'failed'`, then attempts a state-machine transition.

This bypasses the intended legal-transition validation on the first write.

Correction: Establish a single transition service for all state changes, including expiration, submission, scoring success and failure.

### R3-006 — Report-engine percentile silently substitutes an unmeasured value

P2 · Confirmed

File: [report.engine.ts, lines 240–291](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/report.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L240-L291)

When cohort information is insufficient or percentile calculation fails, the reporting engine returns `50`.

A neutral-looking numerical fallback is still presented as a percentile, even though it was not calculated from a reliable comparison cohort.

Correction: Use `null` or an explicit insufficient-data status. Only display a percentile when backed by an actual eligible cohort.

### R3-007 — Report creation uses a check-then-insert pattern

P2 investigation

File: [report-repository.ts, lines 30–44](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/report-repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L30-L44)

`createReportIfNotExists()` checks for a prior report before inserting one.

This may race when multiple scoring or report jobs target the same attempt.

Correction: Verify the database uniqueness constraint and adopt conflict-safe creation where required.

### R3-008 — Queue-service implementation is a placeholder

P1/P2 · Confirmed implementation issue

File: [core/queue.service.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/core/queue.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The complete six-line module contains:

```
export const queueService = {
  async enqueue() {
    return { success: true };
  },
};
```

This function does not enqueue a message.

Risk: Any caller treating `{ success: true }` as proof of durable queue delivery can lose work if it relies on this implementation without an alternative dispatcher.

The actual deployment impact depends on the surrounding QStash and local-runner configuration.

Correction: Replace the placeholder with a real queue adapter or make its nonproduction status explicit.

## 2. Important positive findings

Several Round 2 questions now have stronger answers.

The backend does enforce an exam ownership check during session recovery, including when the exam metadata came from cache. `ExamEngine.submitAnswer()` also checks the exam owner and examination status, and `checkExamTimeLimit()` rejects answers after the configured duration.

The exam repository creates examinations and associated questions inside a transaction. The scoring engine uses a scoring-strategy registry and persists dimension scores and final examination metadata inside a transaction.

There are also tests for examination startup races, state-machine transitions, queue branches and submission-flush failures.

These are meaningful safeguards. The unresolved concerns are primarily atomicity, consistent state transitions, durability and the correctness of success/error responses.

## 4. Principal Architect verdict

Round 3 assessment: Not approved for final acceptance.

The highest-priority corrective work is answer-persistence correctness, removal of assessment secrets from logs, durable scoring dispatch and atomic examination state transitions.

The strongest architectural direction is to establish one authoritative exam lifecycle:

```
Start exam
    ↓
Persist session and questions
    ↓
Accept authenticated answers
    ↓
Enforce server deadline
    ↓
Atomically claim submission
    ↓
Durably dispatch scoring
    ↓
Persist final score and dimensions
    ↓
Publish authoritative result
```

Each transition should be idempotent, ownership-checked and recoverable after process failure.

Recommended Round 4 focus: The answer-evaluation engine, exam-selection service, question database schemas, idempotency tables, durable job orchestration and retry behavior, followed by the unreviewed sections of the larger Round 3 files.

Round 3 completed at source-inspection level. Full line-by-line certification is still in progress. No repository files were modified, and no tests or builds were executed.

## 1. Critical and high-priority findings

### R4-001 — Alternative QuizEngine uses a placeholder selection service in production

P1 · Confirmed source defect

File: [quiz.engine.ts, lines 24–36](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/quiz-engine/quiz.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L24-L36)

The service resolves a mock selection implementation when running in test mode. Outside test mode, it also returns an implementation that produces empty questions and an empty blueprint.

```
return {
  composeExam: async () => ({
    questions: [],
    blueprint: {},
  }),
};
```

Impact: Any production flow invoking this alternative `QuizEngine.startQuiz()` implementation will not obtain real selected questions from the underlying selection service.

This is a confirmed defect in the implementation. Whether the implementation is used by a live entry point still requires a caller audit.

Required correction: Inject the real `SelectionService` in production and restrict mock implementations to explicit test setup.

### R4-002 — Unknown question types silently use exact-string comparison

P1/P2 · Confirmed

File: [evaluator.factory.ts, lines 17–37](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/answer-engine/evaluators/evaluator.factory.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L17-L37)

The factory registers evaluators for MCQ, code MCQ and multiple-selection questions.

However, unknown question types silently fall back to `DefaultEvaluator`.

That evaluator awards a full score when the two strings are equal.

This can conceal unsupported question types or data-contract defects instead of rejecting them.

The database schema currently limits question types to the three explicitly supported values, which mitigates this risk for correctly constrained records. The fallback remains problematic for other callers and malformed input.

Required correction: Reject unsupported types explicitly. Use a default evaluator only where the domain contract intentionally supports one.

### R4-003 — Multi-selection grading mixes partial credit with binary correctness

P2 · Confirmed contract inconsistency

Files:

- [multi-select.evaluator.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/answer-engine/evaluators/multi-select.evaluator.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [answer.engine.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/answer-engine/answer.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The multi-selection evaluator computes fractional credit based on correct and incorrect selections. `AnswerEvaluationEngine.evaluate()` then turns that score into a boolean using a threshold of `0.8`.

As a result, sufficiently high partial credit can be treated as a fully correct answer when consumed through the boolean evaluation interface.

Required architectural decision: Should an examination award all-or-nothing marks, partial marks, or weighted marks for multiple-selection questions?

Once defined, scoring, `isCorrect`, dimensional analytics and result reporting must consistently implement that policy.

### R4-004 — Report repository uniqueness resolves part of the Round 3 race concern

Positive finding · Previous risk narrowed

File: [packages/db/src/schema/reports.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db/src/schema/reports.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The report schema declares `attemptId` as unique.

Therefore, the earlier check-then-insert concern does not imply that two committed report rows can exist for the same attempt when the database constraint is present.

The remaining problem is that concurrent insert attempts may produce a uniqueness error instead of a clean idempotent response.

Revised recommendation: Use conflict-safe insertion and return the existing report on conflict. Verify that the deployed database migration actually contains the unique constraint.

## 2. Job-processing and reliability findings

### R4-005 — Background jobs may be represented without durable persistence

P1 investigation

File: [jobs.service.ts, lines 25–49](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/system/jobs.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L25-L49)

When `QUEUE_ENABLED` is not set to `true` outside test mode, `createJob()` returns an in-memory representation rather than inserting the job into the database.

That can be a deliberate direct-execution design, but it means the returned job ID is not necessarily recoverable from persistent job storage.

Required verification: Trace all callers under queue-disabled deployment configuration and prove that every returned job is either durably recorded or immediately and reliably processed.

### R4-006 — Job execution needs an atomic worker-claim contract

P1 investigation

File: [job-orchestrator.ts, lines 35–105](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/system/job-orchestrator.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L35-L105)

The orchestrator retrieves the job, checks whether it is pending, then moves it into processing.

That sequence requires a database-level atomic claim to prevent two workers from executing the same pending job concurrently.

The inspected code did not establish a complete atomic claim or distributed lease contract.

Required correction: Verify and enforce conditional status changes, worker claims, retries, expiration recovery and idempotent job effects.

### R4-007 — Question-selection implementation needs explicit brand isolation

P1 architectural investigation

Files:

- [selection.service.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/selection-engine/selection.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [schema/question.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db/src/schema/question.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [schema/domain.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db/src/schema/domain.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The selection engine filters by question status, difficulty and selected curriculum hierarchy.

The inspected schema and selection paths do not demonstrate an explicit brand identifier as part of the question-selection contract.

This is a significant architectural question for the shared SkillUp/RTH assessment platform.

Not proven: That data actually crosses brands. Separate databases or constrained deployment boundaries may provide isolation elsewhere.

Required verification: Trace the database connection, authenticated brand context, blueprint ownership and curriculum hierarchy before approving tenant isolation.

### R4-008 — Question selection tests do not establish full integration correctness

P2 · Confirmed test-coverage limitation

The reviewed selection tests cover specific branches such as empty question pools, invalid selection identifiers, difficulty defaults and batching.

Several tests use mocks or replace the selection service itself.

These tests are useful, but they do not independently establish that the real database queries select only authorized, active and correctly scoped questions.

Required tests: Real database integration coverage for multiple brands, overlapping curricula, inactive questions, insufficient question supply and concurrent exam creation.

### R4-009 — Existing job tests do not prove exactly-once processing

P2 · Confirmed coverage limitation

The reviewed orchestrator tests check successful scoring, failed scoring and skipping jobs already marked as processing.

Those are positive cases.

However, source-level unit tests do not establish exactly-once execution across two independently running workers.

Required tests: Competing-worker integration tests, crash-after-claim recovery and duplicate-delivery handling. The practical target should be at-least-once delivery with idempotent effects, rather than assuming a queue provides exactly-once execution.

## 4. Principal Architect verdict

Round 4: Not approved for production sign-off.

The most important conclusion from this round is that the platform has reasonably structured examination schemas and a scoring-strategy architecture, but its execution and reliability contracts are not yet uniformly enforced.

The next engineering decisions should establish one authoritative question-type contract, one grading policy, one production question-selection implementation, and one durable, concurrency-safe processing mechanism.

For Round 5, the audit should target the deployed API gateway and token-to-database identity contracts, alongside the remaining complete-line reviews of large selection and orchestration modules. That is particularly important because the source includes both shared identity tables and brand-specific learner experiences.

Round 4 source inspection is complete for the 40-file tranche; exhaustive line-by-line certification remains open for the larger modules. No code, tests, builds, migrations, deployments, commits or pull requests were changed or executed.

## 1. Principal findings

### R5-001 — Session revocation omits the authenticated user ID

P1 · Confirmed

[global-logout.service.ts, lines 104–124](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/global-logout.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L104-L124) receives both `userId` and `sessionId`, but calls:

```
await brandTokenRepo.revokeById(sessionId);
```

The repository's `revokeById()` method accepts an optional `userId`. When omitted, the database update is constrained only by the session ID.

Confirmed risk: The service does not enforce ownership of the target session during revocation.

Whether this is externally exploitable depends on the route's authorization and whether an attacker can obtain another user's session ID.

Required correction: Make `userId` mandatory in `revokeById()`, and include both the session ID and authenticated user ID in the database condition.

### R5-002 — Different SkillUp components use different user identities

P1 · Confirmed architectural inconsistency

[unifiedBffAuth.ts, lines 199–207](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/unifiedBffAuth.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L199-L207) constructs internal headers using `originalUserId` as the database identity.

[identityGuard.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/identityGuard.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) explicitly defines the same rule.

However, [student-auth.ts, lines 94–100](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L94-L100) prefers `shadowUserId`.

The auth proxy also uses the shadow identity in its `x-user-id` response header.

Impact: The same authenticated learner can be represented by different database identifiers in different code paths.

That can produce missing records or incorrect ownership checks if the downstream database expects the brand-local user ID.

Required correction: Define separate typed `BrandUserId` and `GlobalIdentityId` contracts and make the database target explicit at every service boundary.

### R5-003 — Authentication and gateway trust contracts are inconsistent

P1 investigation

The inspected code uses multiple authentication mechanisms:

| Component                     | Trust mechanism                                            |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gateway-auth.middleware.ts`  | Internal or gateway secret                                 |
| `internal-auth.middleware.ts` | Explicit secret validation with identity headers           |
| `unifiedBffAuth.ts`           | JWT verification plus brand matching                       |
| `authProxy.ts`                | JWT verification and injected identity headers             |
| `authBffRoute.ts`             | Forwarded request headers and internal service credentials |
| `student-auth.ts`             | User JWT plus SkillUp brand check                          |

Each can be legitimate in its own context, but they should implement one consistent trust contract.

The previously identified fail-open condition in `authProxy.ts` when a gateway secret is not configured remains important.

Required action: Establish a trust-boundary matrix for browser, BFF, gateway and API-server calls. Make production configuration validation fail closed.

### R5-004 — Forwarded request headers require stricter trust separation

P2 · Confirmed design concern

[authBffRoute.ts, lines 134–266](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L134-L266) creates upstream headers by copying the incoming request headers and then rewriting selected fields.

It does not begin with a strict allowlist.

Risk: Caller-controlled headers that are not explicitly removed may be propagated into an environment where internal headers carry stronger trust.

The exact consequences depend on gateway sanitization and downstream middleware.

Required correction: Construct upstream headers from an allowlist. Always replace sensitive identity, brand and internal-authentication headers with verified server-derived values.

### R5-005 — Refresh-token rotation is transactional, but session-risk handling needs review

P2 · Mixed finding

[token-refresh.service.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/token-refresh.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) validates the existing refresh token and performs old-token revocation and new-token creation inside a transaction.

That is a positive architectural pattern.

However, the service treats an IP mismatch as a warning and continues. The source explicitly leaves aggressive revocation disabled.

IP changes alone should not automatically invalidate legitimate users, so this is not inherently a defect. It does require a documented risk policy that accounts for device identity, refresh-token reuse and session revocation.

### R5-006 — SHC authentication and token storage need end-to-end consistency

P1/P2 investigation

[shc-auth.service.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/shc-auth.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) contains a comment stating refresh tokens are not stored in `people_db`.

Its logout implementation nevertheless attempts to revoke refresh tokens through the token repository.

Risk: The login and logout contracts may disagree about whether refresh tokens are persistently tracked and revocable.

Required verification: Inspect the actual token-generation and storage path, the database binding of `TokenRepository`, and the SHC logout API. Comments alone are insufficient evidence of runtime behavior.

### R5-007 — Two separate rate-limit implementations have different trust assumptions

P2 · Confirmed

The authentication rate limiter and general API rate-limit middleware both derive client IP addresses from forwarding headers.

They differ in preferred header order and implementation details.

The general middleware also returns the wrapped handler when the limiter throws an exception, allowing a request to proceed despite failure to enforce rate limits.

Required correction: Centralize trusted client-address resolution and define explicit fail-open versus fail-closed policies for security-sensitive routes.

### R5-008 — Brand-specific database routing is present, but not universally applied

P2 · Architectural investigation

[brand-db.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/brand-db.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) explicitly selects different authentication database contexts for SkillUp, RealTutorialHub and SkillHubCore.

This is a positive isolation mechanism.

However, the shared identity system, token repositories, some legacy authentication helpers and examination database operations do not all visibly use that same brand-binding contract.

Required verification: Trace each authenticated user ID to the database that owns the associated record. A brand-specific login database does not, by itself, prove downstream data isolation.

## 3. Principal Architect assessment

Round 5 is complete at source-inspection level, but not approved for security certification.

The highest-priority issue is the absence of mandatory user ownership in the session-revocation repository call. The broader structural concern is that `originalUserId`, `shadowUserId` and generic `userId` do not have one uniformly enforced meaning across the platform.

Before accepting the identity architecture, I would require a complete request trace demonstrating:

`Browser → SkillUp BFF → API gateway → API server → brand-specific database → learner-owned record`

That trace must use the correct user identity, trusted brand context and authenticated principal at every boundary.

Recommended Round 6 focus: The actual token-service implementation, identity-bridge repositories, API gateway middleware, brand database connection factories, session-revocation routes, and end-to-end security tests.

No source files were changed. No tests, builds, migrations, commits, pull requests or deployments were executed.

## 1. Critical and high-priority findings

### R6-001 — JWT secrets have hardcoded fallback values

P1 · Confirmed implementation defect

File: [packages/auth/src/token.service.ts, lines 81–93](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/auth/src/token.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L81-L93)

The signing and verification keys are initialized using environment variables, but missing values fall back to fixed strings such as `test-access-secret`, `test-refresh-secret` and `test-admin-secret`.

Risk: If production environment configuration is missing, predictable keys could be used instead of failing startup.

Required correction: Restrict test secrets to explicit test environments. In production, reject missing or invalid secrets before accepting requests.

Actual production configuration was not inspected, so use of these fallback keys in a live deployment is not established.

### R6-002 — Cross-user session revocation risk is confirmed end to end

P1 · Confirmed source-level authorization gap

The Round 5 issue is now traced through the endpoint, service and repository:

DELETE `/api/auth/sessions/[sessionId]`

Verifies the caller's access token

`GlobalLogoutService.revokeSession(userId, sessionId)`

Passes only `sessionId` to the repository

`TokenRepository.revokeById(id, userId?)`

Optional user constraint is omitted

Files:

- [sessions/\[sessionId\]/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/auth/sessions/%5BsessionId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [token.repository.ts, lines 59–70](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/repositories/token.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L59-L70)

The endpoint authenticates a user, but the database mutation does not enforce that the target session belongs to that user.

Required correction: Make the user ID mandatory and execute the update with both session ID and authenticated user ID in the `WHERE` clause. Return not-found if no owned session matches.

### R6-003 — Session validation middleware contains an unfinished implementation

P1/P2 · Confirmed

File: [packages/auth/src/middleware/auth.middleware.ts, lines 71–77](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/auth/src/middleware/auth.middleware.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L71-L77)

The middleware has an option to require session validation, but the associated refresh-token extraction and repository validation logic is commented out and marked TODO.

Risk: A caller may believe it is enforcing live session validity while actually relying only on access-token verification.

Required correction: Implement the requested session verification or remove the unsupported option. Add a test proving that revocation changes access behavior when session validation is required.

### R6-004 — Generic authentication context can fall back to the wrong brand

P1/P2 · Confirmed architectural inconsistency

File: [apps/api-server/src/lib/auth-context.ts, lines 105–151](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/auth-context.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L105-L151)

In the JWT fallback path, the authentication context constructs its brand with:

```
brand: (payload.brand as RequestBrand) || 'realtutorialhub'
```

This means the helper can return an RTH authentication context for a token lacking a brand claim, subject to what the token verifier permits.

Required correction: Require a valid brand claim, and validate it against the trusted request context before producing an authenticated principal.

This is inconsistent with the stricter brand validation elsewhere in the application.

### R6-005 — Original and shadow user identity contracts remain inconsistent

P1 · Confirmed across layers

The new evidence is particularly important:

- [packages/db-skillup/src/schema/users.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/db-skillup/src/schema/users.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) defines a brand-local primary user ID and a separate `shadowUserId`.
- [packages/identity-bridge/src/UserIdentityBridgeService.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/identity-bridge/src/UserIdentityBridgeService.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) links brand users to cross-platform shadow identities.
- [apps/api-server/src/lib/request-auth.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/request-auth.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) returns only the `x-shadow-user-id` when callers ask for the effective user ID.
- The shared BFF identity guard defines the original user ID as the brand-database key.

Conclusion: The system has distinct identities by design, but some utilities collapse them into one ambiguous `userId`.

Required correction: Make `brandUserId` and `globalIdentityId` distinct validated types and prohibit untyped identity substitution in repository calls.

### R6-006 — Brand-specific token queries are not consistently table-bound

P1/P2 investigation

File: [apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/repositories/user.repository.ts, lines 313–354](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/repositories/user.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L313-L354)

Methods such as `findToken()` and `findResetToken()` use the configured database client's relational query API.

The repository also supports custom brand tables through its `withDb()` operation.

Concern: The correctness of these relational queries depends on whether the database client is initialized with the matching brand schema. Selecting a brand-specific database client does not automatically prove that its relational schema mapping matches the repository.

Required verification: Check the actual Drizzle schema supplied by every database factory and test SkillUp versus RTH verification/reset token operations.

### R6-007 — Shared session IDs are not a sufficient authorization boundary

P2 · Architectural finding

File: [packages/auth/src/session.service.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/auth/src/session.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The package-level session interface supports `revoke(sessionId)` and `getSession(sessionId)` without an authenticated user argument.

These low-level methods are not necessarily exposed directly to end users, but they require an authorization layer above them.

Required correction: Keep authenticated session-management interfaces user-scoped and reserve unrestricted session operations for explicitly privileged internal services.

## 3. Positive findings

There are also important safeguards worth preserving.

Token verification: `verifyUserAccessToken()` uses signed JWT verification, checks the requested audience, validates identity claims and requires a user token type.

Identity bridge: The bridge explicitly associates original brand-user records with cross-platform shadow users.

Brand middleware: The brand-validator middleware rejects mismatches between JWT identity, hostname-derived brand and explicit brand headers.

Database initialization: The SkillUp database factory requires `DATABASE_URL_SKILLUP` outside its test fallback. The people database factory likewise rejects missing configuration outside test conditions.

Session storage: Refresh tokens are represented in a brand-specific schema with ownership fields, revocation state and relevant indexes.

These controls mitigate several risks. They do not cancel the inconsistencies identified above.

# Round 7 — Principal Architect Deep Audit

Focus: Closing previously incomplete line-by-line reviews, with priority on authentication, session ownership, examination state and scoring.

Repository: `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`\
Branch: `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`\
Mode: Read-only
