## 1. Confirmed findings

### R7-001 — Unauthenticated ownership of session revocation remains unresolved

P1 · Confirmed

The complete source review confirms the Round 5 and Round 6 finding.

[GlobalLogoutService, line 113](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/global-logout.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L104-L124) calls `revokeById(sessionId)` without passing the authenticated user's ID.

[TokenRepository, lines 62–69](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/repositories/token.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L62-L69) only adds the user constraint when the optional parameter is supplied.

Consequence: Knowing another user's valid session identifier is sufficient to target its revocation through this service path, provided the caller can reach the corresponding authenticated endpoint. This is an authorization flaw, not merely a coding-style inconsistency.

Required fix: Make `userId` mandatory in the repository operation, require both identifiers in the update condition, and check the affected-row count.

### R7-002 — Gateway authentication logs fragments of configured secrets

P1/P2 · Confirmed

[Gateway middleware, lines 74–78 and 106–110](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/middleware/gateway-auth.middleware.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L74-L110) logs the first ten characters of both received and expected authentication secrets when validation fails.

Even truncated credential values should not be recorded in application logs.

Required fix: Log the authentication mode, request correlation ID and a generic failure reason—never portions of secret values.

### R7-003 — Expired examination recovery can overwrite an existing processing or failed state

P1/P2 · Confirmed

[SessionService, lines 61–80](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/session.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L61-L80) returns immediately only for `completed` status.

When the deadline has passed, it updates the exam to `processing` without restricting the previous status.

Thus an exam already marked `failed`, `abandoned` or `processing` can enter the expiration-processing branch again.

Required fix: Use an atomic, permitted transition from `started` only. Treat other statuses according to the state machine and return their authoritative status without launching duplicate scoring.

### R7-004 — Role normalization contradicts its declared contract

P2 · Confirmed

[auth-context.ts, lines 8–42](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/auth-context.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L8-L42) describes a strict single-role contract, but the implementation maps `user` to `student` and preserves all other supplied roles.

For example, `["user", "admin"]` becomes `["student", "admin"]` rather than one canonical role.

This is not inherently an authorization bypass. It is a security-contract and documentation mismatch that can cause different services to interpret roles differently.

Required fix: Define the intended canonical role model once, including whether multiple roles are legal, and enforce it consistently.

### R7-005 — Job locks are not protected against stale-owner release

P2 · Confirmed design defect

File: [job-lock.ts, lines 3–13](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/job-lock.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L3-L13)

The Redis lock uses `SET NX EX`, which is a reasonable starting point.

However, it stores the same value (`'1'`) for every lock owner. Release simply deletes the key.

If worker A's lock expires, worker B acquires the same lock, and worker A subsequently calls `releaseJobLock()`, A can delete B's valid lock.

Required fix: Use a unique owner token and release through an atomic compare-and-delete operation.

### R7-006 — Effective-user utility always chooses the shadow identity

P2 · Confirmed contract conflict

File: [request-auth.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/request-auth.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

`getEffectiveUserId()` returns only `x-shadow-user-id`.

This is valid when the consuming service uses the global identity database. It conflicts with the shared BFF contract when the consuming service needs the brand-local user ID.

Required fix: Replace the ambiguous utility with explicit brand-local and global-identity accessors. Validate the caller's trust context before either identifier is used.

## 1. Critical findings

### R8-001 — Question-selection random-number calculation can produce invalid array indexes

P1 · Confirmed

File: [selection.service.ts, lines 450–476](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/selection-engine/selection.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L450-L476)

The selection engine uses:

```
return (h >>> 0) / 2147483647;
```

`h >>> 0` is an unsigned 32-bit integer that can reach `4294967295`. Dividing it by `2147483647` can produce a value approaching 2, not a value strictly between 0 and 1.

That result is subsequently multiplied by `localPool.length` to select an array index.

Impact: The index can exceed the available pool. `splice()` then removes nothing and returns an empty array; its first element is `undefined`. That invalid value can enter the selected-question ID collection.

Required correction: Use a properly bounded deterministic random generator and validate every selected index. Add tests across many seeds, including boundary conditions.

This is a newly confirmed mathematical defect, not merely a performance concern.

### R8-002 — Onboarding preferences are marked complete regardless of caller-supplied status

P1/P2 · Confirmed

File: [user.repository.ts, lines 451–489](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/repositories/user.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L451-L489)

The `saveUserPreferences()` method accepts `journeyStatus` in its input but constructs the persisted onboarding object with:

```
journeyStatus: 'completed',
```

Impact: Saving partial preferences through this method can mark the onboarding journey complete even when the learner has not finished it.

Required correction: Preserve an explicitly validated incoming status and allow completion only through the authorized onboarding transition.

### R8-003 — Completed scoring can subsequently be marked failed if analytics refresh fails

P1 · Confirmed control-flow defect

File: [scoring.engine.ts, lines 333–375](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/scoring-engine/scoring.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L333-L375)

The engine commits the final score and transitions the exam to `completed` within a database transaction.

It then awaits:

```
await this.performanceService!.refreshAnalytics();
```

If analytics refresh throws, the outer catch block executes and directly updates the examination status to `failed`.

Impact: An examination can have a committed score and completion timestamp while its status is later changed to failed because a downstream analytics operation failed.

Required correction: Separate core scoring completion from post-processing. An analytics refresh failure should affect analytics-job status, not reverse the result of a successful examination.

### R8-004 — Exam status can become stale during answer submission

P1 investigation · Concurrency

File: [exam.engine.ts, lines 276–340 and 378–408](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L276-L408)

The method validates an exam's `started` status using a cached exam header with a two-minute TTL, then writes the answer to the database.

The answer update does not visibly reassert that the examination is still `started` at the point of mutation.

Risk: An answer request racing with submission or expiration may write after the examination has transitioned to processing.

Required correction: Make answer persistence conditional on authoritative examination status and deadline within an appropriate database transaction.

The race is supported by source inspection; reproducing its timing requires an integration test.

## 2. Additional findings

### R8-005 — Static exam blueprints can return fewer questions than configured

P2 · Confirmed

File: [selection.service.ts, lines 288–305](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/selection-engine/selection.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L288-L305)

Static selection rejects an empty result but does not check that the number of active returned questions matches the blueprint's required question IDs.

Risk: A configured assessment can launch with an incomplete question set.

Required correction: Compare the returned question IDs against the blueprint's expected IDs, rejecting incomplete or mismatched blueprints.

### R8-006 — Invalid database reads are treated as absent onboarding profiles

P2 · Confirmed

File: [user.repository.ts, lines 235–275](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/repositories/user.repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L235-L275)

`upsertOnboardingProfile()` catches database errors while checking whether a profile exists, treats the result as `null`, and proceeds to attempt an insert.

Risk: A transient read failure or schema error may be converted into a conflicting insert or misleading downstream error.

Required correction: Distinguish not-found from query failure. Use a database-native, conflict-safe upsert where appropriate.

### R8-007 — Token verification does not uniformly enforce issuer and identity contracts

P2 · Confirmed inconsistency

File: [token.service.ts, lines 378–480](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/packages/auth/src/token.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L378-L480)

User and admin access-token verification checks signatures, token types, relevant audiences and identity claims.

However, the standard verification methods do not specify an expected issuer in their JWT verification calls, while the SkillHubCore-specific verification method does.

The generic refresh-token verification method also does not apply the same identity-claim validation as user access-token verification.

Required correction: Define explicit token profiles covering issuer, audience, token type, brand, required identity claims and permitted signing keys.

### R8-008 — The exam's idempotency check is not bound to the requested examination

P2 · Confirmed behavioral risk

File: [exam.engine.ts, lines 421–430](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L421-L430)

During completion, a matching idempotency key can replace `targetExamId` with the exam ID stored against that key.

The code subsequently checks ownership, which is a useful safeguard. But a caller reusing a key with a different exam request may be redirected to the previously associated examination rather than receiving an explicit mismatch error.

Required correction: Bind idempotency keys to the user, operation and original exam target, and reject conflicting reuse.

### R8-009 — Scoring implementation disables TypeScript checking for the entire file

P2 · Confirmed maintainability weakness

File: [scoring.engine.ts, lines 1–2](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/scoring-engine/scoring.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L1-L2)

The module begins with `@ts-nocheck`.

That disables TypeScript diagnostics across the central scoring implementation, including database result shapes and state-transition interactions.

Required correction: Restore type checking incrementally using validated DTOs, typed query results and explicit service interfaces.

Branch: `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`\
Scope: Report generation, examination saga, background orchestration, PDF creation, and report interpretation.

Round 9 is a read-only source audit. I have retrieved the five primary modules and reviewed their control flow, including the report SQL, job dispatch, saga checkpoints, and report output contracts.

## 1. Confirmed findings

### R9-001 — Exam completion notification uses a placeholder recipient

P1 — Confirmed

File: [exam.saga.ts, lines 160–175](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.saga.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L160-L175)

The notification step sends to a fixed placeholder address rather than resolving the examination owner's verified email.

Impact: A legitimate learner may never receive the examination-completion notification. The code also treats successful delivery to that placeholder as successful completion of the notification step.

Required correction: Resolve the recipient through the authenticated examination owner, enforce brand-specific email configuration, and record delivery status independently.

### R9-002 — Saga progress checkpoints are not visibly persisted

P1 — Confirmed

File: [exam.saga.ts, lines 291–302](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.saga.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L291-L302)

The saga claims to support resumable execution by tracking completed steps.

However, `updateProgress()` changes `data.metadata` in memory and only updates the job's status to `PROCESSING`.

It does not visibly persist the updated `processedSteps` collection to the job record.

Impact: Retries that reconstruct the saga input from stored job data cannot rely on the latest completed-step checkpoints. Scoring, notifications, exports, or PDF generation may run again.

Required correction: Persist each checkpoint atomically and reload it from durable job storage at the start of every retry.

### R9-003 — Premium reports expose answer keys in their data contract

P1 — Confirmed data exposure; authorization impact requires endpoint review

File: [report.engine.ts, lines 618–642 and 725–738](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/report.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L618-L738)

The premium report fetches question-level records including `correct_answer` and `explanation`, then includes them in its returned `questions` array.

The standard report has an explicit `includeCorrectAnswers` option, but the premium report does not expose the same restriction.

Impact: Any consumer receiving a premium report receives answer-key information. Whether that is intended for a completed assessment depends on the product's review policy.

Required correction: Define an explicit question-disclosure policy covering completion state, learner ownership, reusable question banks, and privileged report consumers.

### R9-004 — Job orchestration does not atomically claim pending jobs

P1 — Concurrency investigation

File: [job-orchestrator.ts, lines 35–63](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/system/job-orchestrator.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L35-L63)

The orchestrator retrieves the job, checks for `pending`, and then updates its status to `PROCESSING`.

No atomic claim is visible in that sequence.

Risk: Two workers may both observe a pending job and begin processing.

Required correction: Enforce an atomic pending-to-processing claim, returning whether the worker acquired the job, plus lease-based recovery and idempotent effects.

### R9-005 — Report interpretation uses unverified fallback percentile data

P2 — Confirmed

File: [report.engine.ts, lines 240–291 and 675–685](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/report.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L240-L291)

Both the standard and premium report paths can substitute a numerical percentile of `50` when the required cohort statistics are unavailable.

The interpreter then generates a learner-facing statement describing that number as a cohort ranking.

Impact: A missing measurement can be presented as a measured result.

Required correction: Preserve missing percentile as `null` and generate an insufficient-cohort-data explanation instead.

### R9-006 — PDF generation places an internal API credential in the URL

P1 — Confirmed

File: [report-pdf.service.ts, lines 43–44 and 145–170](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/report-pdf.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L43-L170)

The service constructs a report URL containing:

```
internalKey=${encodeURIComponent(internalKey)}
```

It also logs the resulting URL when navigating to the print view.

Impact: An internal credential can appear in browser history, request logs, monitoring systems and navigation diagnostics. The source also supplies a fixed development fallback when the environment variable is absent.

Required correction: Never transmit internal API credentials in query parameters. Use a short-lived, narrowly scoped report-rendering token or a trusted server-side authentication channel. Redact existing diagnostic URLs.

### R9-007 — Queue-disabled saga startup can return a job without executing it

P1 — Confirmed

File: [exam.saga.ts, lines 51–67](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.saga.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L51-L67)

When `QUEUE_ENABLED` is false outside the test environment, `ExamSaga.start()` creates a job and immediately returns its identifier.

It does not execute the saga in that branch.

Impact: If this branch is reached without an independent worker consuming the job, scoring and report post-processing may never occur.

Required correction: Make queue-disabled operation an explicitly supported execution mode with a durable dispatcher, or reject the configuration before accepting examinations.

### R9-008 — PDF rendering diagnostics may record learner information

P2 — Confirmed logging exposure

File: [report-pdf.service.ts, lines 217–258](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/report-pdf.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L217-L258)

On a rendering failure, diagnostics include page HTML snippets, console messages, request URLs and browser errors.

These may contain learner details, examination content or internal credentials.

Required correction: Use structured, redacted diagnostics rather than raw page content and full URLs.

### R9-009 — Report completion statistics include unfinished examinations

P2 — Confirmed

File: [report.engine.ts, lines 206–238](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/report.engine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L206-L238)

`getUserPerformance()` queries all examinations for a user, without filtering by `completed` status, and then uses the resulting count for `examsCompleted`.

It also includes incomplete examinations when computing `averageScore`, substituting zero for missing scores.

Impact: Learner dashboards can overcount completed examinations and understate average performance.

Required correction: Apply explicit completion-state filtering for these measures.

## 3. Principal Architect verdict

Round 9: Not approved for production sign-off.

The most urgent newly confirmed issues are the internal credential placed in report URLs, non-durable saga checkpoints, the placeholder notification recipient and the queue-disabled execution path.

These findings also reinforce a broader architectural concern: examination scoring may complete successfully while report generation, exports and notifications remain unfinished, yet the current lifecycle does not consistently expose those as distinct states.

The next audit priority should be `JobsService`, `ReportRepository`, `PerformanceService`, `ReportMaterializer`, storage/upload adapters and the actual workflow endpoint. Those components determine whether the observed risks can be recovered automatically or cause permanent incomplete results.

No repository changes, tests, builds, migrations, commits or deployments were performed.

Focus: Job persistence, examination workflows, report materialization, PDF delivery, Cloudflare R2 storage, and recovery.

# 10

Repository changes

Round 10 confirms important problems not only in individual modules but also in the way these modules interact. All 12 files listed below were retrieved and their complete source read. No runtime tests or deployment configuration checks were performed.

## 1. High-priority findings

### R10-001 — Jobs can be reported as created without database persistence

P1 · Confirmed

File: [jobs.service.ts, lines 25–42](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/system/jobs.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L25-L42)

When queues are disabled outside tests, `createJob()` returns a generated job object without inserting it into `backgroundJobs`.

Downstream `getJob()` reads only the database.

Impact: The returned job identifier cannot be found through normal job-status lookup. In paths relying on that identifier, work can remain permanently unprocessed.

Required correction: Persist jobs regardless of dispatch mode, or execute synchronously without pretending to create a durable job.

### R10-002 — Analytics refresh failures are swallowed

P1 · Confirmed

File: [performance.service.ts, lines 38–49](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/performance.service.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L38-L49)

`refreshAnalytics()` catches database refresh errors, logs them and returns normally.

The saga and workflow both await this method before generating reports.

Impact: Workflow execution can continue after failed analytics refreshes and treat stale materialized views as current.

Required correction: Propagate refresh failures or return an explicit typed result that callers must check.

This finding also refines Round 8: the refresh method itself suppresses ordinary refresh exceptions, so those exceptions alone would not trigger the scoring engine's outer catch. Other errors after score commit can still produce the Round 8 status-reversal problem.

### R10-003 — Report job is marked complete before the final exam status write

P1/P2 · Confirmed sequencing defect

File: [HierarchicalReportService.ts, lines 112–137](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/services/reports/HierarchicalReportService.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L112-L137)

The service marks a report job as `completed` before performing its final examination status update.

Impact: If the final database operation fails, the report job has already been marked complete and must subsequently be corrected to failed.

More significantly, the reporting service directly sets the examination status to `completed`, bypassing the centralized exam state machine.

Required correction: Report processing should not own examination scoring status. Keep report-job completion separate and make finalization atomic where necessary.

### R10-004 — Durable workflow and local saga implement different workflows

P1/P2 · Confirmed architectural inconsistency

Files:

- [exam-report/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/workflows/exam-report/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [exam.saga.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/exam-engine/exam.saga.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The Upstash workflow runs scoring, analytics, notification and finalization.

The local saga additionally generates JSON/CSV exports and the student-insight PDF.

Impact: Two valid execution modes can produce different user-visible artifacts from the same examination lifecycle.

Required correction: Define one canonical workflow specification, with equivalent steps and completion criteria across all execution adapters.

### R10-005 — Workflow marks notification successful after sending to a system address

P2 · Confirmed

File: [exam-report/route.ts, lines 78–95](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/workflows/exam-report/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L78-L95)

The workflow sends the completion message to a fixed system address rather than the examination owner.

This corroborates the placeholder-recipient defect identified in Round 9's local saga.

Required correction: Resolve the correct brand-local user and verified email address. Record notification completion separately from report readiness.

## 2. Additional defects and reliability concerns

### R10-006 — Report materializer can produce invalid accuracy for an empty exam

P2 · Confirmed

File: [ReportMaterializer.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/services/reports/ReportMaterializer.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The report's domain accuracy calculation divides the number of correct questions by the total question count without a zero denominator guard.

If an exam contains zero resolved questions, the result can become `NaN`, which is unsuitable for report persistence.

Required correction: Handle empty examinations explicitly before constructing analytics.

### R10-007 — Report recovery SQL interpolates a duration as raw SQL text

P2 · Confirmed input-handling weakness

File: [ReportJobService.ts, stale-job recovery](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/services/reports/ReportJobService.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The stale-job recovery statement embeds `ageMinutes` inside a SQL interval literal using string interpolation.

This is not evidence of a remotely exploitable injection path—the function's default argument is numeric and its callers need further analysis—but it is an avoidable raw SQL construction.

Required correction: Validate the numeric range and use parameterized interval arithmetic.

### R10-008 — Report record creation is vulnerable to duplicate-insert errors under concurrency

P2 · Confirmed race pattern

File: [report-repository.ts, lines 30–44](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/modules/report-engine/report-repository.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L30-L44)

The repository checks for an existing record, then inserts one.

The uniqueness constraint found in Round 4 prevents duplicate committed reports for one attempt, but concurrent calls can still produce a uniqueness exception.

Required correction: Use `ON CONFLICT` handling and load the existing record after a conflict.

### R10-009 — Report persistence can succeed before all related records are updated

P2 · Confirmed partial-failure risk

File: [HierarchicalReportService.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/services/reports/HierarchicalReportService.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The report-processing flow uploads the PDF, updates the report record, updates examination export URLs, then updates the report job status.

These operations do not share one transaction or reconciliation mechanism.

Impact: A failure between stages can leave the PDF uploaded while database metadata is incomplete.

Required correction: Make upload operations idempotent and introduce a recoverable finalization sequence with reconciliation.

### R10-010 — Storage adapter uses deterministic keys that can overwrite existing reports

P2 · Confirmed

File: [r2.ts, lines 29–41](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/storage/r2.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L29-L41)

Uploaded reports use keys derived from `userId` and a report basename.

Reprocessing the same attempt and basename can overwrite an existing object.

This may be intentional for replacement semantics, but requires versioning or a documented immutability policy if historical reports must remain reproducible.

One positive finding is worth emphasizing: `ReportJobService.getNextJob()` uses a PostgreSQL `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim strategy. Unlike the general job orchestrator, it establishes an atomic database claim for queued report work.

## 4. Principal Architect verdict

Round 10: Not approved for production sign-off.

The highest-impact findings concern durable job creation, unreliable analytics-refresh error handling, divergent execution workflows and incomplete report finalization.

The architectural correction is to separate three states cleanly:

- Exam state: started → processing → completed or failed.
- Report state: pending → generating → ready or failed.
- Delivery state: queued → sent or failed, independently for each output.

These must be recoverable and idempotent without one subsystem rewriting the authoritative state of another.

Round 10 completed: 12 files inspected in full, 10 finding groups documented, and no repository changes, tests, builds, migrations, commits or deployments performed.

The most significant new result is a source-confirmed missing ownership check at the export initiation endpoint. Unlike the previously identified internal helper concern, this is a reachable API path that accepts an examination ID from an authenticated caller without verifying that the examination belongs to that caller.

## 1. Principal findings

### R11-001 — Export trigger authenticates the user but does not authorize the examination

P1 · Confirmed authorization defect

[export/trigger/route.ts, lines 35–89](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/trigger/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L35-L89)

The endpoint correctly derives `userId` from the verified JWT rather than trusting a user-supplied ID. However, it accepts `examId` from the request body and immediately launches the export.

There is no database ownership check between validation of the input and the export dispatch.

The downstream [ExportQueryBuilder](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/export/exportQueryBuilder.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) fetches examination records using that ID, including learner email, answers and correct answers, without independently enforcing ownership.

Impact: An authenticated user who knows another examination ID may be able to initiate generation of an export containing another learner's information. Whether the generated artifact can be retrieved depends on the execution and download paths; the unauthorized export initiation itself is confirmed.

Required correction: Verify `exam.userId === authenticatedUserId` before dispatch. Repeat the ownership assertion inside `ExportEngine.processExport()` and the workflow before reading sensitive data.

### R11-002 — The export engine trusts independently supplied exam and user identifiers

P1/P2 · Confirmed trust-boundary defect

[exportEngine.ts, lines 26–45 and 100–115](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/export/exportEngine.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L26-L115)

`processExport(examId, userId, format)` assumes the examination ID and user ID refer to the same owner.

The former controls which exam records are extracted; the latter controls historical records, cache keys and storage paths.

Impact: A mismatched pair can result in an export containing one learner's assessment data but stored or tracked under another learner's identity.

Required correction: Resolve the examination's owner from the database, reject mismatches, and derive storage and cache ownership from that verified record.

### R11-003 — Unsupported `pdf` format is accepted by the export trigger

P2 · Confirmed API-contract defect

[export/trigger/route.ts, lines 124–138](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/trigger/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L124-L138)

The input validator accepts:

`pdf`, `json`, `csv`, and `student-insight-pdf`.

However, the reviewed export engine explicitly processes `json`, `csv`, and `student-insight-pdf`, throwing for unsupported values.

The workflow also treats formats other than CSV and the special student-insight PDF case as JSON.

Impact: A request for `pdf` can fail or produce JSON content, depending on the path.

Required correction: Centralize supported-format validation and reject unsupported formats before creating any job.

### R11-004 — PDF workflow does not validate that the provided user owns the attempt

P1/P2 · Boundary investigation

[pdf-report/route.ts, lines 20–89](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/workflows/pdf-report/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L20-L89)

The workflow receives `attemptId` and `userId` in its payload, checks that both are nonempty strings, then generates and uploads the report under the supplied `userId`.

It does not compare the submitted user ID against `exams.userId`.

The endpoint verifies the Upstash signature, which protects against ordinary unsigned requests. That is an important mitigation, but a signed message can still contain mismatched identifiers because of an upstream programming defect.

Required correction: Query the exam owner and reject mismatches before rendering or uploading.

### R11-005 — Export workflow does not consistently preserve its output in exam metadata

P2 · Confirmed implementation inconsistency

[export/workflow/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/workflow/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The JSON/CSV workflow uploads the generated artifact, stores the resulting reference in the job result and caches it.

Unlike `ExportEngine.processExport()`, this workflow does not update `exams.exportUrls` with the resulting JSON/CSV reference.

Impact: Job-based downloads may work while exam-based export lookups have no corresponding saved reference. Redis expiration and job-record retention make these paths behave differently over time.

Required correction: Define one canonical export-artifact record and persist it consistently across both local and workflow execution.

### R11-006 — PDF workflow's idempotency check trusts metadata without checking storage existence

P2 · Confirmed

[pdf-report/route.ts, lines 34–58](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/workflows/pdf-report/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L34-L58)

The PDF workflow exits early when an existing report is marked ready with a nonempty file reference or when the exam has an `analytics_pdf` reference.

It does not verify that the referenced object is still present in storage.

Impact: A deleted or stale object can prevent automatic regeneration.

Required correction: Validate object existence, or make the download pathway invalidate and recover stale references.

### R11-007 — Export download permissions are stronger than export initiation permissions

P2 · Confirmed architectural inconsistency

Files:

- [export/download/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/download/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [export/trigger/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/trigger/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The download endpoint enforces either job ownership or exam ownership before fetching the storage object.

The trigger endpoint does not enforce exam ownership.

This is a positive download safeguard, but the inconsistency creates a fragmented security model: unauthorized processing can begin even when the final direct download would be denied.

Required correction: Apply authorization before any sensitive processing, not only at the final delivery step.

### R11-008 — Report endpoints need a unified answer-disclosure policy

P2 · Confirmed policy gap

[reports/route.ts, lines 85–113](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/reports/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L85-L113)

The standard report is requested with `includeCorrectAnswers: false`.

The premium report path does not use an equivalent restriction, and the premium report engine includes correct answers.

The route blocks `started` and `processing` exam states but does not require `completed` for every report type.

Required correction: Enforce explicit completion-state and answer-disclosure rules for all report tiers. Decide separately whether failed or abandoned exams may reveal question-bank answers.

## 2. Positive findings

The review also verified safeguards that should be preserved.

- The export trigger obtains the authenticated user ID from the JWT, not from request-body input.
- The report-download route checks examination ownership.
- The export-download route checks job ownership or examination ownership before accessing the stored artifact.
- The PDF workflow verifies Upstash signatures before invoking the workflow handler.
- Storage access uses private object references and signed read URLs rather than automatically exposing an entire storage bucket.

These protections are real, but they do not replace authorization inside export creation and processing.

## 4. Principal Architect verdict

Round 11: Not approved for security or export-delivery sign-off.

The immediate priority is closing the ownership-check gap before export generation. The fix must apply at both the API entry point and the core export operation, because relying exclusively on route-level authorization leaves internal and background callers unprotected.

Next, unify export format validation, persisted artifact metadata, workflow idempotency and completed-exam answer disclosure.

Recommended Round 12 focus: Export status and URL endpoints, report access on the SkillUp BFF, workflow-trigger authorization, shared export formatters, and integration tests for cross-user access.

No code was modified. No tests, builds, migrations, commits or deployments were executed.

Important: Round 12 found a significant authorization issue in export-status recovery. The endpoint authenticates the caller but does not consistently verify ownership of the job before reading it or updating its status.

## 1. Principal findings

### R12-001 — Export-status endpoint lacks job ownership enforcement

P1 · Confirmed

File: [export/status/\[jobId\]/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/status/%5BjobId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The endpoint verifies the caller's JWT and derives `userId`.

However, after retrieving the job through:

```
const job = await JobsService.getJobStatus(jobId);
```

there is no immediate check that `job.userId === authenticatedUserId`.

The endpoint subsequently returns job status, error information, and potentially a download URL derived from the job's stored artifact.

Impact: An authenticated user who knows another user's job ID can potentially inspect that job's status and associated information.

The actual download endpoint has a separate ownership check, which limits direct artifact retrieval, but does not eliminate the status-information exposure.

Required correction: Check ownership immediately after retrieving the job and before any recovery, storage lookup or response construction.

### R12-002 — Export-status polling can mutate another user's job

P1 · Confirmed authorization defect

File: [export/status/\[jobId\]/route.ts, stale-job recovery](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/status/%5BjobId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The status endpoint is a `GET` handler, but it can call `JobsService.updateJobStatus()`.

When a job appears stale, the handler may mark it completed or failed.

Because the current request path does not first enforce job ownership, an authenticated caller who supplies another user's job ID may trigger these state changes.

Impact: Status polling can become an unauthorized job-state mutation, potentially disrupting an export still being processed.

Required correction: Separate status retrieval from recovery mutations. Recovery should run through a trusted worker using atomic job-state transitions, not an ordinary user-facing GET request.

### R12-003 — CSV export can return non-ZIP data labeled as ZIP

P1 · Confirmed

File: [csvFormatter.ts, lines 57–71](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/export/formatters/csvFormatter.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L57-L71)

The formatter normally uses JSZip to create an archive.

If ZIP generation fails, it catches the error and returns a plain CSV buffer instead.

However, the callers continue treating the result as a ZIP archive, using an `.zip` extension and `application/zip` content type.

Impact: The export job can report success while delivering a corrupt or unreadable ZIP file.

Required correction: Do not silently substitute another file format. Either fail the ZIP generation or return an explicitly typed CSV fallback whose extension and content type are correct.

### R12-004 — Export status uses workflow step names that differ from the producer

P2 · Confirmed

File: [export/status/\[jobId\]/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/status/%5BjobId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The status mapper recognizes `upload-to-blob`.

The export workflow reviewed in Round 11 writes `upload-to-storage`.

Impact: During the storage-upload stage, the status endpoint can return an unknown progress value rather than the intended finalization progress.

Required correction: Define shared workflow-step constants used by both producer and status API.

### R12-005 — Export-status fallback can use the job owner's identity instead of the caller's

P1/P2 · Confirmed trust-boundary flaw

File: [export/status/\[jobId\]/route.ts, ](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/status/%5BjobId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[`resolveReadyExportArtifact()`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/status/%5BjobId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The fallback lookup passes:

```
userId: job?.userId ?? requestUserId
```

This makes the job's stored owner ID authoritative when a job exists, instead of consistently requiring the authenticated caller to own that job.

The fallback can therefore inspect another user's exam artifact metadata if a foreign job ID is supplied.

Required correction: Authorize the job first, then pass the authenticated and verified owner identity through all recovery functions.

### R12-006 — Export URL lookup can return stale responses despite a valid database artifact

P2 · Confirmed

File: [export/urls/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/app/api/export/urls/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

When Redis contains an invalid or missing artifact reference, the endpoint clears the cache key and immediately returns `{ url: null, source: 'stale' }`.

It does not continue to check whether `exams.exportUrls` contains a valid reference.

Impact: A stale cache entry can temporarily hide an otherwise available export.

Required correction: On cache validation failure, invalidate Redis and continue to the database lookup instead of immediately returning.

### R12-007 — CSV formatter lacks spreadsheet-formula injection protection

P2 · Confirmed

File: [csvFormatter.ts, lines 4–20](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/api-server/src/lib/export/formatters/csvFormatter.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L4-L20)

The formatter escapes commas, quotation marks and newlines.

However, it does not neutralize values beginning with spreadsheet-formula characters such as `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`.

Impact: Untrusted question text, learner names or other exported strings may be interpreted as formulas when the CSV is opened in spreadsheet software.

Required correction: Apply spreadsheet-safe cell encoding to untrusted strings and add tests for formula-prefixed content.

### R12-008 — Existing tests do not prove security and artifact correctness

P2 · Confirmed test gap

The inspected tests establish only narrow expectations.

The CSV formatter test verifies that the result is a `Buffer`, but does not establish that it is a valid ZIP archive containing the expected CSV files.

The export-status test verifies happy-path responses and stale-job recovery, but does not test requests using a foreign user's job ID.

The legacy export-cache test is skipped entirely.

Required correction: Add negative authorization tests, ZIP signature and content validation, stale-cache recovery tests, and concurrency cases.

## 2. Positive findings

The export URL endpoint verifies a user token and enforces examination ownership before returning an artifact link.

It also checks whether stored objects exist, rather than trusting nonempty storage references blindly.

The student-insight formatter separates behavioral metrics, knowledge gaps, skills, priorities, progress and recommended next steps into a well-defined output structure.

These are useful foundations. They do not compensate for the authorization gaps in the status endpoint.

All paths are relative to `apps/api-server/src/`. The correct ledger total is 893 source lines; the initial summary figure understated this count. Source lines were read; tests were not executed.

The SkillUp BFF did not contain the initially expected `/api/reports` or `/api/export` directories at the inspected paths, so those specific BFF implementations could not be included in this tranche. I have not substituted unrelated files to inflate the file count.

## 4. Principal Architect verdict

Round 12: Not approved for security sign-off.

The most urgent work is enforcing authorization in export-status retrieval and eliminating state mutations from ordinary polling requests. These issues are more serious than cosmetic progress-display defects because they affect cross-user job boundaries.

The next priority is making exported artifacts trustworthy: correct ZIP generation, consistent workflow status names, safe CSV output, and tests that prove ownership and file integrity.

No repository files were modified. No tests, builds, migrations, commits or deployments were performed.

I retrieved and inspected the complete source of 14 files. This round concentrates on actual SkillUp functionality rather than shared examination infrastructure.

## 1. High-priority findings

### R13-001 — Students without batch enrollment receive a fabricated batch

P1 · Confirmed

File: [skillup-data.ts, lines 88–107 and 312–319](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L88-L107)

`getSkillupMyBatch()` returns `FALLBACK_BATCH` when no active enrollment is found.

This is not an empty-state placeholder. The returned object includes a batch name, faculty, schedule, session history and recording URLs.

Impact: A learner without an actual enrollment can see a seemingly real assigned batch.

Required correction: Return an explicit `not_enrolled` state with no fabricated sessions. Keep demonstration data exclusively in isolated demo or test environments.

### R13-002 — Programs and faculty can silently switch to sample records

P1/P2 · Confirmed

File: [skillup-data.ts, lines 209–245 and 548–589](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L209-L245)

The programs query returns predefined programs if the database is empty or throws an error.

Faculty retrieval similarly substitutes predefined faculty and statistics when records are missing or queries fail.

Impact: A database outage can be hidden behind realistic-looking catalog content. Users may believe an unavailable or fictional course or mentor is genuinely offered.

Required correction: Distinguish database failure, no data and demo mode; never silently turn production failures into sample content.

### R13-003 — Placement profile contains invented interview counts and match percentages

P1/P2 · Confirmed

File: [skillup-data.ts, lines 419–507](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L419-L507)

The student placement response calculates interview count from readiness score rather than actual interview records:

```
interviewCount: Math.max(1, Math.round(readinessScore / 20))
```

If a placement profile is missing, the code supplies predefined profile statistics. In fallback ranking paths, it also assigns synthetic job-match percentages.

Impact: Students can receive misleading placement progress and confidence indicators.

Required correction: Derive interview counts from real interview records; expose match scores only when produced by a validated matching algorithm; otherwise return unavailable or unranked status.

### R13-004 — Student dashboard attendance can exceed the actual batch scope

P2 · Confirmed calculation defect

File: [skillup-data.ts, lines 248–280](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L248-L280)

The dashboard calculates attendance percentage using all matching attendance records for the user as the numerator, but only the selected batch's sessions as the denominator.

The query does not restrict attendance records to that batch.

Impact: Learners who attended sessions across multiple batches may receive inflated attendance percentages, potentially above 100%.

Required correction: Restrict attendance and session counts to the same batch, define whether canceled sessions are included, and count distinct eligible sessions.

### R13-005 — Payment data sources are inconsistent

P2 · Confirmed

File: [skillup-data.ts, lines 248–274 and 374–417](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L248-L417)

The dashboard computes `paymentDue` from payment installments obtained through the people database.

The dedicated payments endpoint uses a separate payment-database connection and queries installments via payment plans.

Risk: The dashboard and payments page may disagree when the two sources differ or are not synchronized.

Additionally, when the payment database is not configured, the dedicated payments endpoint returns an empty installment list instead of a configuration error.

Required correction: Establish the payment system of record and use a single validated projection across both experiences.

## 2. Additional findings

### R13-006 — Onboarding session cookie accepts user-supplied completion state

P2 · Trust-boundary investigation

Files:

- [onboarding/session/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/onboarding/session/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [onboardingSessionCookie.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/onboardingSessionCookie.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The session endpoint accepts an onboarding object, including `journeyStatus`, and serializes it into an HTTP-only cookie.

The endpoint itself does not authenticate the user or establish completion against a database record.

Risk: If another part of the application treats this cookie as proof of onboarding completion, client-provided state could bypass the actual onboarding process.

Required correction: Treat the cookie as display or draft state only. Completion must be verified using server-side persisted onboarding status.

The downstream authorization impact remains to be traced.

### R13-007 — Program detail includes a synthesized curriculum

P2 · Confirmed

File: [skillup-data.ts, lines 594–624](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L594-L624)

`getSkillupProgramDetail()` constructs generic curriculum sections using highlight strings and standard interview-preparation descriptions.

The sections are not fetched from a verified curriculum or module table.

Impact: Course details may be presented as official curriculum despite being programmatically synthesized.

Required correction: Use a canonical course, module and lesson data model.

### R13-008 — Shared profile BFF bypasses the gateway used by onboarding

P2 · Architectural inconsistency

Files:

- [bffProfileHandler.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/src/share-branding/auth/bffProfileHandler.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [onboarding/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/onboarding/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The onboarding BFF forwards through a configured gateway URL.

The shared profile BFF calls an internal API URL directly and falls back to a fixed API hostname when configuration is missing.

Risk: These routes may apply different network and authorization controls despite using shared authentication helpers.

Required correction: Define the permitted topology for each endpoint and ensure equivalent authentication, brand validation and observability across both paths.

### R13-009 — Student dashboard reports global open jobs as personalized placement matches

P2 · Confirmed semantic mismatch

File: [skillup-data.ts, lines 294–300](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com#L294-L300)

The dashboard's `placementMatches` field counts all open, non-deleted job listings.

It does not calculate matches for the current student.

Impact: A learner may see the number of available jobs represented as the number of personally relevant placement matches.

Required correction: Use a per-student matching query or rename the measure to accurately describe the total number of open positions.

## 3. Positive findings

The five student API routes use a shared `requireStudentAuth()` guard and pass the derived user ID into their data functions.

Program-list and program-detail endpoints explicitly invoke authentication and brand validation.

The onboarding BFF also uses shared authentication and centralized internal-header construction.

These are useful protections, although the underlying auth implementation still needs complete contract verification for original versus shadow user IDs.

## Round 14 findings

### R14-001 — Tutorial progress requests use manually assembled internal credentials

P2 — Confirmed design inconsistency

Source: [tutorial/progress/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/progress/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Both GET and POST handlers correctly call `requireStudentAuth()` before proxying requests.

However, they independently construct privileged service headers and use a fallback API hostname. This differs from the shared header-construction pattern elsewhere in the application.

Required correction: Centralize authenticated internal request creation, require valid server configuration and make original-versus-shadow user identity selection explicit.

### R14-002 — Tutorial progress proxy configuration can silently switch endpoints

P2 — Confirmed

The route selects:

```
process.env.INTERNAL_API_URL
  || process.env.GATEWAY_URL
  || 'https://api.skillhubcore.in'
```

A missing or incorrect configuration can therefore cause traffic to reach an unintended fallback destination.

Required correction: Validate the destination and required credentials at startup. In production, fail explicitly when the intended upstream is unavailable.

### R14-003 — Tutorial progress tests do not cover user isolation

P2 — Confirmed test gap

Source: [tutorial/progress/route.test.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/progress/route.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The tests cover URL normalization, forwarding of internal authentication and rejection of unauthenticated calls.

They do not establish that one student cannot read or alter another student's tutorial progress through the upstream API.

Required correction: Add tests for identity mismatch, missing service secrets, brand mismatch and cross-user progress attempts.

### R14-004 — Faculty listing correctly requires authentication and brand validation

Positive verification

Source: [faculty/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/faculty/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

This is a sensible separation of learner-facing and administrative responsibilities.

### R14-006 — Active-time and completion APIs forward unvalidated request bodies

P2 · Confirmed validation gap

Sources: [active-time/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/active-time/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and [block-completion/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/block-completion/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

Both routes authenticate the learner but accept any syntactically valid JSON body and forward it upstream.

### R14-007 — SkillUp server-side API helper has inconsistent identity forwarding

P2 · Investigation required

Source: [skillup-api.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-api.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

The helper forwards `x-shadow-user-id` as `x-user-id`, while the learner authentication tests establish that the shadow identity represents the SkillUp-local user ID.

The naming and identity contract remain inconsistent with other shared service integrations.

Required correction: Use explicitly named identity fields throughout the chain and verify their mapping against database ownership rules.

The helper also falls back to direct data access for programs and faculty after an API request fails. That fallback can conceal the reason the original protected request failed.

### R14-008 — Learner authorization tests establish useful protections, but remain incomplete

Positive verification with test gaps

Source: [student-auth.test.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

The test suite checks rejection of forged identity headers, wrong-brand requests and unauthenticated access. It also checks that personalized tutorial responses are not publicly cached.

These are useful regression protections.

Remaining gaps include multi-user progress mutation, upstream token/header mismatches, authorization across the database boundary and concurrent progress updates.

## 1. Principal findings

### R15-001 — SkillUp examinations page presents nonfunctional assessment actions

P1/P2 · Confirmed

[student/exams/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/student/exams/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### R15-002 — Payments page contains nonfunctional payment and receipt buttons

P1/P2 · Confirmed

[student/payments/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/student/payments/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The page renders `Pay overdue installment` and `Download receipt` buttons without event handlers or navigation actions.

Impact: Learners may believe these financial actions are available when the interface does not implement them.

Required correction: Integrate authorized payment initiation and receipt retrieval, or visibly disable and label unavailable functionality.

### R15-003 — Learner dashboard uses fixed visual progress-bar percentages

P2 · Confirmed

[student/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/student/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Although the dashboard receives actual values for attendance, learning progress, upcoming sessions and job matches, the visual bars use fixed Tailwind widths:

`86%`, `68%`, `54%` and `62%`.

Impact: The graphic indicator can contradict the adjacent actual metric.

Required correction: Derive chart widths from the corresponding data values with proper clamping and accessible labels.

### R15-004 — Tutorial API routes have inconsistent upstream paths and authentication headers

P2 · Confirmed contract inconsistency

Reviewed routes include:

- [ILS complete-node](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/complete-node/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [ILS block-visit](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/block-visit/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Tutorial content](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/content/%5BsubtopicId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Tutorial sections](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/sections/%5BsubtopicId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Some routes call upstream paths beginning with `/api/tutorial/...`, while others use `/tutorial/...`.

Some forward both internal authentication headers, while others forward only `X-Internal-Secret`.

Impact: Behavior depends on the exact upstream base URL, route configuration and authentication middleware.

Required correction: Centralize upstream URL construction and internal authentication into one typed service client, then validate the complete route matrix.

### R15-005 — Tutorial navigation accepts identifiers without schema validation

P2 · Confirmed BFF validation gap

[ILS navigation route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/navigation/%5BnodeId%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The handler checks only that `subtopicId` is present. It also interpolates `nodeId` into the upstream path without explicit parameter-schema validation.

Required correction: Validate identifiers using the expected database identifier contract, encode path parameters and enforce node-to-subtopic membership upstream.

### R15-006 — Tutorial interaction proxy forwards arbitrary client-provided query parameters

P2 · Investigation

[tutorial/interactions/\[type\]/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/interactions/%5Btype%5D/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The route correctly restricts interaction types to an allowlist and requires learner authentication.

However, it forwards all incoming query parameters and the POST request body without validating their contents.

Risk: If upstream handlers trust client-supplied ownership or completion fields, inconsistent access checks may result.

Required correction: Validate each interaction's request schema and enforce authoritative ownership at the API server.

### R15-007 — Attendance page may display duplicate calendar-day keys

P2 · Confirmed UI risk

[student/attendance/page.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/student/attendance/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The attendance history uses formatted date strings as React keys.

Multiple attendance records on the same calendar day could therefore share a key.

Required correction: Return stable attendance-record identifiers and use them for rendering.

## 2. Positive findings

The tutorial proxy routes consistently perform `requireStudentAuth()` before forwarding protected learner requests.

The interaction endpoint uses an explicit allowlist for supported interaction types.

The server-side SkillUp API helper also avoids silently falling back to direct database access for protected student dashboard, attendance, batch, payment and placement requests.

These protections should be preserved when consolidating the BFF implementation.

# Round 16 — SkillUp-Web Principal Architect Audit

Repository: `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`\
Branch: `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`\
Mode: Read-only

## Initial security findings

### R16-001 — Placement handoff forwards an access token to another service

P1 — Security-sensitive integration requiring verification

[Placement handoff route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The endpoint retrieves the access token from a cookie or refresh response and sends it in the JSON body to the placement service.

This is a deliberate cross-service credential handoff, but the inspected route does not independently verify the token's audience or replace it with a placement-specific, single-use exchange credential.

Risk: A general-purpose user token may be exposed beyond the service for which it was issued.

Recommendation: Use short-lived, single-use handoff tokens with explicit audience, brand, destination and expiry restrictions. Verify the placement receiver's implementation before determining exploitability.

### R16-002 — Test-fixture session endpoint can mint access tokens in specially configured production builds

P1/P2 — Deployment-sensitive security risk

[Test fixture session route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/test-fixture-session/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The fixture route normally blocks production, but an isolated-verification environment flag permits operation when `NODE_ENV` is `production`, provided other production indicators are absent and the required secret and fixture settings are present.

The route has meaningful safeguards, including secret verification, an allowlist and short token lifetime. Nevertheless, its availability depends on several environment variables being configured correctly.

Recommendation: Enforce a deployment-level restriction that is independent of user-configurable environment flags, and keep fixture token issuance inaccessible from public production infrastructure.

### R16-003 — Profile page logs personally identifiable information

P2 — Confirmed

[Dashboard profile page](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/dashboard/profile/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The page logs the authenticated user's complete ID and email address while loading profile information.

Recommendation: Remove personal identifiers from routine logs, retain correlation IDs and apply structured redaction.

### R16-004 — Tutorial subtopic progress uses inconsistent proxy authentication

P2 — Confirmed

[Subtopic progress route](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/subtopic/%5BsubtopicId%5D/progress/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The route uses the same manually assembled upstream URL and identity-header pattern identified in earlier ILS routes. It forwards only one of the internal credential headers used elsewhere.

Recommendation: Consolidate tutorial endpoints behind one authenticated, typed upstream client and validate the path parameters.

### R16-005 — Service worker can cache authenticated pages

P1 — Confirmed caching risk

[SkillUp service worker](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/sw.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The service worker caches successful same-origin navigation responses without excluding authenticated student pages.

It also reads cached responses when network requests fail.

Impact: Previously rendered learner pages may remain available through the browser's offline cache after logout or account switching on the same device.

Required correction: Cache only explicitly public pages and static assets. Exclude authenticated routes and API responses, and clear user-specific cached content when a session ends.

### R16-006 — Proxy test contradicts the intended RSC authentication boundary

P2 — Confirmed test-contract inconsistency

[Proxy test](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/__tests__/proxy.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The proxy configuration comments state that React Server Component requests must pass through authentication.

However, one test expects an unauthenticated dashboard RSC request to return HTTP 200 without calling token verification.

The test also imports `isPublicAuthRoute` from the local proxy module, although that symbol is not visibly exported by the inspected `proxy.ts`.

Required correction: Reconcile the expected RSC behavior with the shared proxy implementation and repair the tests to reflect the actual security contract.

### R16-007 — Password recovery and session routes rely on shared proxy authorization

Architecture dependency

The login, signup, logout, refresh, password recovery and session routes are thin wrappers around `proxyAuthRequest()`.

This reduces duplication, but final security approval depends on the shared proxy's handling of request headers, cookies, credentials, token rotation and forwarded session identifiers.

A complete wrapper review alone cannot certify those mechanisms.

## Round 16 coverage

I inspected 34 files, including authentication routes, fixture-session controls, certificate verification, profile pages, student UI components, browser caching, and proxy tests.

The remaining target of 50–60 was not achieved in this round. I am recording 34 rather than claiming 50–60 without having retrieved and inspected those files.

Some longer UI files were examined through selected source lines rather than all their implementation details, so their coverage must remain classified as targeted until completed.

## Principal Architect verdict

Round 16: Not approved for production sign-off.

The most important issues identified are the authenticated-page caching risk, placement-token handoff design, test fixture deployment controls, and inconsistent RSC authentication expectations.

For Round 17, the audit should prioritize the remaining large SkillUp-web components, tutorial-v2 learning routes, payment and placement integrations, and the shared authentication proxy contracts.

My recommendation remains to use 50–60 files as the target where the source sizes permit, while preserving exact evidence and a truthful completion ledger.

No code was changed, and no tests, builds, migrations, commits or deployments were performed.

Repository: `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`\

## 1. Findings

### R17-001 — SkillUp BFF route tests are inconsistent with the actual authorization requirements

P1/P2 · Confirmed test-design defect

Source: [app/api/tests/routes.test.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/__tests__/routes.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The test suite mocks student authentication and data services, then verifies successful responses from dashboard, payments, attendance, placement and batch routes.

However, the program and faculty endpoints have their own authentication and brand-validation requirements. The suite calls those handlers without verifying that the requirements are satisfied.

Impact: The tests do not establish that program and faculty authorization works correctly. They may also fail under the real route contracts, depending on the remaining mocks.

Required correction: Test authenticated, unauthenticated, wrong-brand and authorized requests separately. Preserve actual route authorization behavior instead of mocking it away.

### R17-002 — Tutorial V2 depends on identity headers supplied by the shared proxy

P2 · Security contract requiring integration verification

Source: [Tutorial V2 navigation page](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/tutorial-v2/%5BdomainSlug%5D/%5BsubjectSlug%5D/%5BtopicSlug%5D/%5BsubtopicSlug%5D/%5BnavigationNodeId%5D/page.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The page checks for an access-token cookie, then obtains the learner identity from request headers.

It relies on the shared proxy having validated the token and inserted trustworthy identity headers.

Risk: The security of this page depends on the proxy correctly replacing or rejecting caller-supplied identity headers.

The current page does not independently verify the token.

Required correction: Add an integration test covering the proxy, headers, runtime resolver, tenant identity and learner ownership as one end-to-end authorization boundary.

### R17-003 — Placement bridge needs a verified cross-domain session contract

P2 · Integration investigation

Sources:

- [PlacementBridgeClient.tsx](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/placement/PlacementBridgeClient.tsx?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [placement-handoff/route.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The client sends a handoff request and, after an HTTP-success response, navigates the browser to the placement domain.

The handoff route forwards the learner's access token to that service.

Risk: Successful HTTP delivery does not independently prove that the destination accepted and established the correct brand-local placement session.

Required correction: Verify the placement-side handoff handler, the session cookie domain, replay protection and identity mapping.

### R17-004 — API test fixtures reinforce synthetic dashboard expectations

P2 · Confirmed coverage weakness

Source: [routes.test.ts](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/feature/project-llm-linux-worker/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/__tests__/routes.test.ts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The tests configure populated fictional batch, payment, placement and faculty records as successful responses.

Test fixtures themselves are appropriate. The concern is that these tests predominantly assert the presence of populated data, without covering legitimate empty states.

This compounds the Round 13 finding that production helpers can return similar fabricated data.

Required correction: Add explicit cases for unenrolled students, absent payment records, empty placement profiles, empty faculty lists and backend failures.

## 2. Positive findings

The Tutorial V2 page rejects requests without a token cookie or a resolved learner ID.

The placement bridge handles an unsuccessful handoff by redirecting toward login rather than proceeding to the placement application.

The root layout uses a consistent SkillUp brand configuration, and the landing page delegates its implementation to a shared component rather than duplicating its UI logic.

# Round 18 — Principal Architect Audit: SkillUp Learning, Onboarding and Shared Authentication

Repository: `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`\
Branch: `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`\
Scope: Shared code used by SkillUp-web

Files inspected

# 52
