# SkillUp-Web — Phase 02 Authentication and Security Audit

**Report date:** 1 November 2026
**Repository:** `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`
**Branch:** `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`
**Pinned revision:** `e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c`
**Audit mode:** Read-only static source review, cross-referencing preceding audit rounds. No live deployment access, exploits, tests, fixes, commits, or build execution.

## Executive decision

**PHASE 02 SECURITY SIGN-OFF: NOT APPROVED.** The core browser → SkillUp proxy → BFF → gateway/API → persistent identity contract is not demonstrably consistent. Some defects are confirmed at source level; other concerns are contingent on deployment or downstream middleware. This report is a substantive static assessment, **not** a claim of exhaustive line-by-line certification of every reachable backend/shared package. Closing that distinction requires the verification checklist below.

## Scope and evidence

Source traced at the pinned revision:

- `apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts` (154 lines)
- `apps/skillup-web/src/proxy.ts` (17 lines; earlier full review)
- `src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts` (429 lines; principal authorization branches and full ranges examined)
- `src/share-branding/auth/unifiedBffAuth.ts` (250 lines; identity and internal-header branches)
- `src/share-branding/auth/identityGuard.ts` (239 lines; ID semantics)
- `src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts` (566 lines; forwarding, cookie rewriting, gateway routing)
- `src/share-branding/auth/validateAuthState.ts` (311 lines; auth-state forwarding)
- `apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts` (97 lines)
- `apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/test-fixture-session/route.ts` (106 lines)
- previously fully read SkillUp authentication route wrappers, session handlers and the tests for learner authorization, proxy, and fixture sessions.

Note: File lengths include trailing newline when present. Complete-source retrieval and focused line-by-line tracing are distinguished from execution-backed validation. Previously reported findings from Rounds 5–18 remain unresolved unless proven fixed at the pinned revision.

## Findings register

### P02-001 — P1 — Contradictory brand-local identity mapping (confirmed source inconsistency)

**Evidence:** [`student-auth.ts#L94-L100`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts#L94-L100) chooses `shadowUserId` for learner operations; [`authProxy.ts#L398-L403`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts#L398-L403) propagates the shadow ID as `x-user-id`; [`unifiedBffAuth.ts#L150-L159`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/auth/unifiedBffAuth.ts#L150-L159) also returns shadow as the generic user ID, **but** [`unifiedBffAuth.ts#L199-L209`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/auth/unifiedBffAuth.ts#L199-L209) sets `x-user-id` to `originalUserId`. [`identityGuard.ts#L52-L67`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/auth/identityGuard.ts#L52-L67) asserts that `originalUserId` is always the database ID.

**Impact:** Data lookup divergence, invisible learner records, and potential cross-identity authorization errors. This does not by itself establish a user-to-user IDOR.

**Resolution:** Specify for *each backing database* whether its primary key is original/global, shadow/brand-local, or bridged. Use an explicit typed identity context at every BFF → API hop; reject ambiguous `x-user-id` in security-sensitive operations; add multi-brand and multi-user integration tests.

### P02-002 — P1/P2 — Default-allow route classification for unlisted pages and APIs (confirmed control-flow design)

**Evidence:** [`authProxy.ts#L12-L47`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts#L12-L47) defines explicit public and protected route lists. [`authProxy.ts#L296-L316`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts#L296-L316) applies the gateway-secret gate only to API routes outside an allowlist of BFF internals. [`authProxy.ts#L398-L428`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts#L398-L428) ends with `NextResponse.next()` for paths not covered by protected checks.

**Impact:** Security depends on each unlisted route implementing its own guard. A future sensitive route can be introduced without adding it to the list; the proxy does not fail closed. No direct exploitable unguarded API established here.

**Resolution:** Adopt a default-deny policy for authenticated application namespaces and a narrowly documented public allowlist. Generate routing coverage tests from the source route inventory.

### P02-003 — P1/P2 — User token sent as JSON to the placement service (confirmed token-transfer design)

**Evidence:** [`placement-handoff/route.ts#L37-L81`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts#L37-L81). A normal access token is extracted or refreshed and posted in the handoff body. The caller's `redirectTo` is restricted to leading `/` excluding `//`, but still allows arbitrary relative destinations.

**Impact:** A general access token crosses application-service boundaries. Security hinges on the placement receiver's audience/nonce/replay behavior. No intercepted credential or placement-side exploit demonstrated.

**Resolution:** Exchange a signed one-time, placement-audience handoff grant with a short TTL and replay protection. Verify destination, callback, session cookie and token rotation behavior end to end.

### P02-004 — P1/P2 — Development fixture-session issuer permits special production-mode builds (confirmed gate logic; deployment contingent)

**Evidence:** [`test-fixture-session/route.ts#L17-L39`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/test-fixture-session/route.ts#L17-L39) explicitly accepts `NODE_ENV=production` if isolation flags and other production indicators permit it, provided a 32-character secret and allowlisted IDs are configured. [`route.test.ts`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/test-fixture-session/route.test.ts) tests that acceptance.

**Impact:** Environment misclassification can expose a token-minting endpoint. Safeguards do exist, including timing-safe secret comparison, configured fixtures and 15-minute tokens.

**Resolution:** Remove test-credential issuance from Internet-facing production artifacts, or hard-block it independently at ingress with dedicated isolated infrastructure and rotating credentials.

### P02-005 — P2 — Forwarding starts from arbitrary request headers and incompletely strips privileged headers (confirmed code design; receiving service matters)

**Evidence:** [`authBffRoute.ts#L134-L266`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts#L134-L266) constructs `new Headers(request.headers)` and deletes only `host`, `content-length`, and `expect` before conditionally overwriting selected brand and internal headers. It passes along client-supplied `x-forwarded-for`, device headers and possibly client-controlled identity headers.

**Impact:** If a receiving system trusts an unsanitized forwarded field, a forged identity, IP, or gateway context can influence decisions. The BFF itself does overwrite some brand context on recognized hosts, which partially mitigates this.

**Resolution:** Build a strict allowlisted header set from server-owned context; remove inbound `x-user-id`, `x-shadow-user-id`, `x-original-user-id`, internal credentials and trusted proxy identity fields, then populate them from a verified context.

### P02-006 — P2 — Placement-handoff cookie host resolution trusts `x-forwarded-host` (confirmed divergence)

**Evidence:** [`placement-handoff/route.ts#L25-L33`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts#L25-L33) prefers `x-forwarded-host`. Shared [`authBffRoute.ts#L87-L106`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts#L87-L106) intentionally chooses `host` for rewritten cookie domains.

**Impact:** A deployment accepting untrusted forwarded-host values can rewrite refreshed cookie domains incorrectly or cause errors. Browser cookie-domain restrictions may block some misuse; real exploitability requires ingress testing.

**Resolution:** Use one trusted host resolver derived from ingress-controlled headers; validate against allowed SkillUp domains before setting cookies.

### P02-007 — P2 — Learner authentication accepts `admin`, `super_admin`, and `faculty` in a student auth guard (confirmed authorization semantics)

**Evidence:** [`student-auth.ts#L5-L7`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts#L5-L7) and [`student-auth.ts#L120-L140`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts#L120-L140).

**Impact:** A request with a valid SkillUp admin/faculty claim can access student-facing functions. This may be intentional support access, but without a student enrollment check and explicit target-user authorization, semantics are ambiguous.

**Resolution:** Distinguish learner access from administrative impersonation and enforce audited, scoped staff workflows.

### P02-008 — P2 — Security test contradictions and gaps (confirmed)

**Evidence:** [`apps/skillup-web/src/__tests__/proxy.test.ts`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/apps/skillup-web/src/__tests__/proxy.test.ts) expects RSC dashboard requests to bypass verification while [`authProxy.ts#L269-L280`](https://github.com/skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC/blob/e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c/src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts#L269-L280) explicitly says they must not. The app-local proxy file also does not visibly re-export the test-imported `isPublicAuthRoute`.

**Impact:** Tests are not a reliable proof of the active authentication boundary.

**Resolution:** Update proxy tests; add a generated route matrix, cross-brand tests, cookie/session integration, token replay, and backend ownership tests.

## Prior-round security findings requiring carry-forward

- Session revoke-by-ID ownership (R7-001): review the API handler + token repository together; API-side object ownership must be mandatory.
- JWT secret fallback and token verification policy (R6, R8): prove strong secrets, issuer/audience and revocation in production configurations.
- User ID ownership inconsistencies (R6, R7, R18): require mapping proof per database.
- Export trigger and status ownership gaps (R11–R12): distinct shared API concerns; not cleared by this SkillUp BFF review.
- Private response and offline cache (R16): service worker must not retain authenticated pages after logout.

## Confirmed strengths

- `requireStudentAuth` verifies tokens with `audience: 'user'`, requires the `skillup` brand, and rejects missing roles/identity.
- Proxy compares JWT brand with the resolved request hostname for authenticated routes.
- Fixture endpoint uses constant-time secret comparison, fixture allowlisting and a short token lifetime.
- Shared `createInternalHeaders` requires a configured internal secret rather than silently sending an empty one.
- The placement callback redirect blocks protocol-relative URLs, though deeper destination policy remains desirable.

## Phase 02 exit criteria and evidence status

| Exit criterion | Assessment |
|---|---|
| SkillUp JWT verification and brand scope reviewed | Static review performed; runtime issuer/revocation tests outstanding |
| Browser → proxy → BFF identity agreement | **Failed — conflicting original/shadow user ID contracts** |
| Every protected route listed and default-deny enforced | **Failed — explicit protected-prefix model and default continuation** |
| Session revoke and placement handoff bounded to user/brand | **Unverified end-to-end** |
| Cross-brand/IDOR/CSRF/cookie tests executed | **Not executed** |
| Security findings resolved and independently regression-tested | **Not demonstrated** |

**Phase 02 disposition:** Source assessment report delivered; **security certification rejected**. This is not a passing completed security phase. The highest priority remediation order is: (1) ID contract, (2) route default-deny coverage, (3) privilege/header forwarding controls, (4) placement token exchange, (5) fixture endpoint isolation, and (6) end-to-end tests.

## Scope limitations

The request was to complete Phase 02. The current review produces a defensible static report for the principal SkillUp boundaries, but it does not establish exhaustive, full-range review of every backend handler, session repository, migration, auth test, gateway policy or production environment. Claims about practical exploitation require the described tests. The repo was not changed.

# Phase A — Principal Architect Audit Report

**Date:** 2026-11-01
**Repository:** `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`
**Reviewed branch reference:** `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`
**Mode:** Read-only static source audit and cross-file reconciliation. No code changes, tests, builds, migration execution or live deployment verification.
**Decision:** **STATIC REVIEW RECONCILED; PHASE A CERTIFICATION NOT PASSED.**

## Executive decision

Phase A covers the Round 2–4 backend backlog: ILS learner progress, canonical content resolution, tutorial composer and delivery, API authentication, cross-brand behavior, and corresponding tests. The previously unfinished *identified core source-range backlog* has now been closed across the composer, section repository, learning-progress service, navigation repository, block-state repository, and learning-progress service test. Other dependencies and 749-line ILS authentication tests were previously retrieved and screened, not exhaustively certified in this completion pass. This report therefore concludes the **available Phase A static assessment**, not repository-wide or runtime approval.

Architecture requirements in `FinalAechitecture.md` include secure authenticated brand boundaries, single authority over business rules, private treatment of personalized responses, deterministic data access, and resilience under concurrency. Earlier `ProjectAuditReport.md` and `ResolveProjectAuditReport.md` concern historical work, including `main` and other changes; they are contextual leads, not evidence that the target branch's defects are fixed.

## Findings — risk-prioritized

| ID | Priority | Evidence (branch source path, lines) | Finding / impact | Required action |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The wrong brand variant may be returned when both exist. | Explicitly order exact brand before shared; PostgreSQL test with both rows. |
| A-02 | **High** | `packages/db-tutorial/src/services/tutorial-composer.service.ts:269–319,456–522`; `.../repositories/tutorial-section.repository.ts:389–441` | Composer update and append call unconditional `updateTutorialContent`, although `updateTutorialContentWithVersion` exists. Concurrent editors can lose blocks/edits. | Require expectedVersion, conditional update and 409 conflict semantics; concurrency integration tests. |
| A-03 | **High** | `packages/db-tutorial/src/services/tutorial-composer.service.ts:322–355,367–414`; `.../repositories/tutorial-section.repository.ts:450–481` | Generic status update lacks transition-policy enforcement; repository can set `deployed`/`publishedAt` outside publish validation. | Centralize a controlled status transition state machine; block direct deployment except through validated publish operation. |
| A-04 | **High / caller-dependent** | `tutorial-composer.service.ts:280–283,332–335,372–375,431–434,466–469` | Service-level authorization checks are TODOs. The *reviewed SHC publish route* explicitly checks admin/subtopic/brand; this does not establish public exploitation of that route. Other callers and alternate entry points remain to be traced. | Enforce authorization in a shared domain policy or prove every caller's non-bypassable boundary; deny cross-brand mutation tests. |

Suitable for **valid informational content**; unsafe if empty requirements also mean missing/unpublished/broken canonical content. | Distinguish valid no-assessment page from canonical document missing, invalid or unpublished; fail closed for missing source. |

| A-16 | **Medium / interoperability** | `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/app/api/tutorial/progress/mark-complete/route.ts:9–19`; `.../lib/ai-tutor-progress.ts` | API accepts several instructional block types but forwards completion to AI-tutor-only helper, ignoring parsed type. | Block-type-aware completion route, cross-type endpoint tests. |

## Security boundary adjudication

- **Positive:** `apps/api-server/src/middleware/internal-auth.middleware.ts:51–199` strictly rejects missing/mismatching internal secrets when required and validates gateway trust-secret for gateway-mode identities. `apps/api-server/src/app/api/tutorial/ils/block-completion/route.ts:28–51` and `.../complete-node/route.ts:33–56` use `{requireInternalSecret: true}` and derive identity from validated context. The SHC publish route (`.../sections/[sectionId]/publish/route.ts:94–124`) has admin, subtopic and brand guards.
- **Not proven:** Those controls do not certify every consumer, middleware path, endpoint, service caller, or deployment-level ingress. Internal-secret authentication is also not equivalent to checking a learner's enrollment/entitlement for the requested resource.
- **RTH:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/lib/assignment-auth.ts` checks token/brand/role; it checks full subtopic completion for assignment access. Because assignment completion may itself participate in the wider mastery denominator, the intended unlock policy needs a dedicated content-only predicate; learner deadlock is conditional on the active mastery rules.

## Recommended remediation order

1. **P0 correctness and security:** Canonical completion ingestion; fail closed for unavailable content; brand-specific content precedence; block status bypass; classify all composer callers and scope checks.
2. **P1 data integrity:** Composer OCC, navigation completion transactionality, reliable pagination, cache invalidation and revision consistency.
3. **P1 verification:** Real PostgreSQL integration for concurrent visits, completion/reset, exact/shared brand collision, invalid block/version, duplicate/soft-deleted state, telemetry idempotency; API security test execution.
4. **P2 operational:** Remove diagnostic logging; avoid exposure via caching, preserve timestamps under old data, ensure error mapping and rate limits.

## Mandatory correction and verification sequence

1. **Trust boundaries:** specify intended admin/author brand and subtopic permissions, implement checks in central policy (A-17/18), enumerate service callers, verify role/origin tests and prove public ingress cannot forge internal identity.
2. **Canonical learner progress:** reject missing/unpublished content and arbitrary block completions, define informational pages, atomically protect completion/reset and versioned state.
3. **Content authoring:** lock down deployed status, enforce expected-version writes for content and append, make exact-brand fallback deterministic, reconcile list filters.
4. **Operations:** fix personalized cache policy, make invalidation reliable, remove forensic logging and validate brand-scoped user mapping.
5. **Executable evidence:** run unit, PostgreSQL integration and API security tests; inspect migration/index state, typecheck, lint, build, and ingress/CDN configuration; record actual results and failing logs.
6. **Audit loop closure:** obtain correction commit and test output, re-read modified files, compare to requirements, mark each finding FIXED / STILL OPEN / NOT VERIFIED with immutable SHA. **Only then** issue Phase A PASS and unblock Phase B.

These are **positive authenticated-route protections**. They do not make `requireBrandAccess` or `requireSubtopicAccess` resource-specific. Further, the full call graph outside these known routes remains an enumeration task, not a certified negative result.

# SkillUp-Web — Phase 02 Security Audit, Re-audit 2

**Date:** 2026-11-01
**Repository:** `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`
**Branch:** `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`
**Pinned commit:** `e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c`
**Method:** Read-only static code review and cross-layer tracing. No code changes or test execution.

## Executive disposition

**Phase 02 security exit: FAILED — not eligible for sign-off. Phase 03 remains on hold.**

This re-audit expanded the earlier eight-finding assessment into the actual API session handlers, the logout service, token repository, internal-auth middleware and API auth-context helper. It confirmed a cross-user session-revocation defect and an authentication-mode downgrade concern. A fully completed *static source investigation* is not equivalent to an independently verified secure system: production configuration, integration tests and remediation evidence are absent.

## Architecture and trust-boundary trace

1. Browser presents `accessToken` cookie or (for learner BFF) `Authorization: Bearer` to `apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts`.
2. SkillUp proxy (`apps/skillup-web/src/proxy.ts` and `src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts`) classifies routes, verifies a user-audience token on protected paths, validates the JWT brand against host, and injects `x-user-id` from `shadowUserId`.
3. Shared profile BFF (`src/share-branding/auth/unifiedBffAuth.ts`) extracts `userId` from `shadowUserId` but creates upstream `x-user-id` from `originalUserId`.
4. Auth BFF (`src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts`) copies incoming headers and conditionally overwrites select trust headers before gateway forwarding.
5. API server (`apps/api-server/src/middleware/internal-auth.middleware.ts` and `src/lib/auth-context.ts`) accepts internal-secret, gateway-secret, or user JWT modes; authoritative identity semantics differ by mode.
6. Session routes delegate to `GlobalLogoutService`; `revokeSession` invokes token-repository `revokeById(sessionId)` without scoping by the verified user ID.
7. Placement handoff sends the regular access token in a cross-origin JSON POST to the placement service; destination receiver and cookie trust policy not verified.

## Findings register (confirmed vs contingent)

### P02-001 — P1 — Contradictory brand-local user identity semantics (confirmed source inconsistency)

`apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts` L94–100 favors `shadowUserId`; `src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts` L398–403 injects shadow as `x-user-id`; `src/share-branding/auth/unifiedBffAuth.ts` L150–159 uses shadow for generic `userId` but L199–209 selects original for `x-user-id`; `src/share-branding/auth/identityGuard.ts` L52–67 insists original is the database identifier. The exact brand-specific database ownership must be demonstrated by a schema/data mapping. **Do not treat cross-user disclosure as proven solely from this mismatch.** Fix by establishing a typed, database-specific identity contract and end-to-end integration tests.

### P02-002 — P1/P2 — Default-allow proxy route classification (confirmed control flow; exploit contingent on route)

`src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts` L12–47 uses public and protected lists; L269–429 ultimately returns `NextResponse.next()` for unlisted routes. Public authentication routes return early. This makes endpoint-local guards essential; the proxy is not a universal authentication wall. Fix with route inventory and default-deny for protected namespaces, while retaining explicitly public paths.

### P02-003 — P1/P2 — Cross-service general access-token handoff (confirmed design)

`apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts` L37–81 sends `accessToken` in JSON to `https://placement.skillhubcore.in/api/auth/handoff`. Receiver-side audience, replay and cookie validation have not been verified. Replace with single-use, audience-limited exchange grants and test receiver-side enforcement.

### P02-004 — P1/P2 — Test fixture minting can be enabled for selected NODE_ENV=production builds (confirmed gate, deployment contingent)

`apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/test-fixture-session/route.ts` L17–39 allows isolation mode with configured flags, secret and fixture list even when `NODE_ENV=production`, provided other production indicators are not production. The route enforces a timing-safe secret comparison and 15-minute token, but must not be internet-accessible in real production. Its bundled tests intentionally exercise isolation mode.

### P02-005 — P2 — Forwarding user-supplied headers into privileged network context (confirmed design, downstream dependency)

`src/share-branding/auth/authBffRoute.ts` L134–266 starts from `new Headers(request.headers)` and removes only a few headers before setting trusted host/brand/internal credentials. Identity, forwarding and device headers can persist if not overwritten. Prefer strict allowlist and explicit reconstruction of security-relevant headers from verified server context.

### P02-006 — P2 — Placement cookie host derived from x-forwarded-host (confirmed difference)

`apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/auth/placement-handoff/route.ts` L25–33 prioritizes `x-forwarded-host`, while shared `authBffRoute.ts` L87–106 uses the `host` header. Host trust must be enforced at the ingress; centralize cookie-domain validation against allowlisted domains.

### P02-007 — P2 — Learner guard accepts staff roles (confirmed policy behavior)

`apps/skillup-web/src/lib/student-auth.ts` L5–7 and L120–140 permits `student`, `admin`, `super_admin`, `faculty`. This may be legitimate support access but must not be mistaken for proof of learner enrollment. Explicitly define staff acting-as-learner policy and scoped audit logging.

### P02-008 — P2 — Security tests contradict active proxy contract (confirmed)

`apps/skillup-web/src/__tests__/proxy.test.ts` expects dashboard RSC requests to bypass auth, contrary to `src/share-branding/middleware/authProxy.ts` L269–280. The test imports an auth-route symbol not visibly re-exported by `apps/skillup-web/src/proxy.ts`. Update tests before relying on any passing suite as evidence.

### P02-009 — P1 — Unauthorized cross-user revocation of session IDs (confirmed)

`apps/api-server/src/app/api/auth/sessions/[sessionId]/route.ts` L30–93 verifies the caller and passes `userId` to the service. **However**, `apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/global-logout.service.ts` L105–126 invokes `brandTokenRepo.revokeById(sessionId)` with no `userId`. In `apps/api-server/src/modules/auth/repositories/token.repository.ts` L59–69, `revokeById(id, userId?)` includes the user ownership predicate **only when userId is supplied**. A caller with an accessible/known foreign session UUID may therefore revoke a different user's session in the selected token database. The route returns success regardless of affected-row count. **Fix:** Make `userId` mandatory at the repository API, use `WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?`, return affected rows / 404 for no ownership match, and add cross-user + brand-boundary tests. This confirms and strengthens Round 7 finding R7-001; it is not an entirely new discovery.

### P02-010 — P1/P2 — Failed privileged-auth validation can fall through to JWT mode (confirmed control flow; exploit contingent)

`apps/api-server/src/middleware/internal-auth.middleware.ts` L54–198 returns an error for invalid internal/gateway credentials. `apps/api-server/src/lib/auth-context.ts` L67–153 calls `validateRequest(req)` but checks only `authResult.context` and otherwise attempts JWT validation without first honoring `authResult.error`. If a request contains bad internal/gateway credentials **and** a valid user JWT, this helper may authenticate under JWT rather than treating the invalid privileged context as a terminal rejection. Exploitability depends on the calling route's required mode and downstream authorization. **Fix:** Return `null` or propagate the explicit error on failed privileged-mode validation; never downgrade. Add mixed-header and mode-confusion tests.

### P02-011 — P2 — API JWT fallback silently assigns default brand (confirmed)

`apps/api-server/src/lib/auth-context.ts` JWT branch returns `brand: payload.brand || 'realtutorialhub'` without resolving the inbound host or requiring a valid brand claim in that function. Token verification may enforce brand elsewhere; the fallback still weakens the local brand-contract clarity. Require a validated brand claim and match to trusted request context where appropriate.

### P02-012 — P2 — API session routes inconsistently derive brand (confirmed)

`apps/api-server/src/app/api/auth/sessions/route.ts` GET L34–38 uses token brand; DELETE L115–120 infers brand from hostname, while `apps/api-server/src/app/api/auth/sessions/[sessionId]/route.ts` L30–42 uses hostname substring logic defaulting to `realtutorialhub`. This can select different token database contexts for the same identity under different routes. Adopt one canonical validated request-brand strategy and test SkillUp, RTH, and SkillHubCore routing.

## Positive controls verified in source

- Learner token verification requests `audience: 'user'` and enforces token brand `skillup` (`student-auth.ts` L70–140).
- Shared BFF header generation rejects missing internal API secret (`unifiedBffAuth.ts` L178–209).
- Internal-auth middleware requires a matching configured secret for privileged modes (`internal-auth.middleware.ts` L54–198).
- Fixture endpoint enforces a strong configured secret, timing-safe comparison, fixture allowlist and short expiration.
- Session listing and revoke-all operations are scoped to user ID in token repository; **single-session revocation is not**.

## Phase 02 exit criteria

| Criterion | Outcome | Required evidence before passing |
|---|---|---|
| Full trust-path source review | **Partial** | Examine all relevant gateway/placement receiver, token/session issuance, CSRF, and auth middleware paths with full line coverage |
| Canonical identity contract | **Fail** | Written mapping of original/shadow ID to each user table; integration tests |
| Protected route isolation | **Fail** | Generated route matrix, default-deny or explicit per-route ownership evidence |
| Session access/revocation | **Fail** | Fix P02-009; unauthorized-ID tests; affected-row assertions |
| Auth-mode fail-closed behavior | **Fail** | Fix P02-010; mixed-header tests |
| Handoff and cookie boundary | **Unverified** | Placement receiver review, one-time exchange or explicitly bounded credential protocol |
| Production fixture isolation | **Unverified** | Deployment/ingress proof fixture route is unreachable or disabled |
| Security regression validation | **Not run** | Tests, typecheck, build and relevant staging security cases |

## Remaining work to close Phase 02 — concrete ordered gate

1. **P1 remediation:** P02-009 ownership-scoped single-session revocation; P02-010 no authentication-mode downgrade.
2. **Identity and route design:** P02-001/P02-002 typed ID contract, full route matrix and default-deny/per-handler audit.
3. **Handoff and deployment evidence:** review placement receiver and gateway auth; verify production fixture blocking and cookie/host policy.
4. **Test evidence:** run authenticated/unauthenticated, wrong-brand, cross-user IDOR, RSC, JWT issuer/audience, refresh/logout and CSRF scenarios.
5. **Re-audit fixed revision:** compare commit SHA and confirm each failing exit item with source and runtime evidence.

## Decision

**The Phase 02 assessment/re-audit report is complete as a static snapshot, but Phase 02 itself is NOT COMPLETE because its mandatory security exit criteria fail. No Phase 03 sign-off should follow until remediation and evidence exist.** Repeating a static read of unchanged vulnerable source cannot legitimately turn this failed gate into a pass. Repository was not modified; tests were not run.

**Date:** 2026-11-01

**Scope:** `packages/marketing-site/src/` only

**Phase:** 01 — Inventory and coverage reconciliation
**Decision:** **INVENTORY PASS; COVERAGE-CERTIFICATION GATE NOT PASSED**

## Executive assessment

Phase 01 establishes an exact inventory of **290 Git blobs** and assigns **one documented evidence classification to every relative path** in the accompanying CSV ledger. It **does not** establish that all 290 files have been completely audited line by line. No code was changed, and no build, lint, typecheck, tests, browser, deployed endpoint, or service traffic was executed.

### Evidence classification (mutually exclusive)

| Classification | Files | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `PINNED_SOURCE_RETRIEVED` | 106 | Whole source fetched at the pinned SHA in known audit rounds; depth differs, **not** automatically certified |
| `HISTORICAL_REPORT_MENTION` | 45 | Explicitly mentioned by an available local historical tranche report, not independently pinned-verified in this conservative ledger |
| `NO_PATH_LEVEL_EVIDENCE` | 139 | Not represented in the two narrower proof classes; **not proof it was never reviewed** |
| **TOTAL** | **290** | All files accounted for; none can be signed off as fully line-reviewed based on standardized evidence alone |

The ledger gives the highest proven evidence classification for each file. The categories measure **evidence quality**, **not** a count of previously unreviewed source files. For example, Round 11 fetched 50 files, but only selected high-risk files were deeply inspected; all 50 are marked retrieved, not conclusively reviewed.

## Input evidence and provenance

- Immutable Git subtree listing retrieved in the audit conversation on 2026-11-01: exactly 290 blob paths, unique, sorted. File path inventory was expanded from a prefix-compressed transfer and validated to 290 distinct paths.
- `SkillUp_Marketing_Audit_Tranche_01.md` through `...05.md`: local prior findings and named file histories. Tranche 01 states it is partial; Tranches 03–05 contain mutable `main` fetch caveats; lack of a full historical manifest prevents certification.
- Closure Rounds 4–11: explicit immutable-ref code retrievals with cited paths, including a 50-file analytics/event/privacy batch in Round 11.
- `FinalAechitecture.md`, `ProjectAuditReport.md`, and `ResolveProjectAuditReport.md` consulted as project context, **not substituted for file-specific marketing-source review evidence**.

## Method and evidence reliability

1. Fix the branch-independent commit and source subtree.
2. Enumerate every blob. Exclude other applications, wrappers, server configurations, public assets, tests outside this subtree, and dependency/package locks from this **290-file inventory**. Those require separate integration scope gates.
3. Match paths to explicit local review reports and pinned source fetch records; give priority to immutable SHA evidence.
4. Preserve an explicit distinction between retrieved source, reported historical review, comprehensive semantic review, and executed tests.
5. Assign review depth `NO` until a complete reviewer record supports file-level certification. **No 100% completeness inference from round count.**

## Findings and gaps of Phase 01

**P01-EVID-01 (High, process):** No complete historical 290-row review manifest with immutable source SHA, reviewer, reviewed line coverage, results and finding cross-references is available. Historical audit summaries cannot prove unique-file completeness.

**P01-EVID-02 (High, process):** Some early tranche code was fetched from `main`. Without blob comparison, conclusions are not automatically valid for commit `5efd1129d905d05c912acfef66e52df9ca15120b`.

**P01-EVID-03 (Medium, process):** The cumulative MKT-001–MKT-286 IDs are historical *findings recorded*, not independently verified open defects. They require deduplication, remediation state and change-aware retesting.

**P01-EVID-04 (Medium, process):** The 290-source-blob scope does not include the Next.js app wrapper, marketing public assets, build config, CI, infrastructure or runtime tests. Completeness of the marketing site overall needs a separate system boundary assessment.

These are **Phase 01 evidence/control findings**, not new `MKT-287+` code defects. Phase 01 is an audit-plan closure phase, not a claim of whole-project risk remediation.

## Phase 01 exit criteria

| Criterion | Outcome |

## Phase 02 operational handoff

Process `NO_PATH_LEVEL_EVIDENCE` first, then `HISTORICAL_REPORT_MENTION`, then recheck `PINNED_SOURCE_RETRIEVED` for missing semantic review and adverse interactions. For each file, record:

Use batches of up to 50–60 **small/moderate** files, but cap batch size for large or security-critical modules. No file may be marked fully certified solely because its source was fetched. All new code findings join a separate MKT ledger, with deduplication against MKT-001–286.

## Priority risk streams for subsequent phases

3. Accessibility and interaction state across navigation, forms, filter drawers and certificates.

**Date:** 2026-11-01
**Repository:** `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`
**Immutable commit:** `5efd1129d905d05c912acfef66e52df9ca15120b`

**Evidence:** Placement, placement statistics, prerequisites and success stories mapper files all return an explicit fallback for unknown names. The separate curriculum mapper's omissions remain MKT-275; do not incorrectly extend that finding to these fallback-safe mappings.

# Phase B — Principal Architect Source Audit Report

**Date:** 2026-11-01
**Repository:** `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`
**Ref:** `feature/project-llm-linux-worker`
**Mode:** Read-only static inspection of GitHub repository sources. No commits, migrations, test runs, build, production verification or deployment access.

## Executive decision

**Phase B source audit: report issued; technical acceptance FAILED.** The reviewed code exposes confirmed authorization-policy, state-machine, durability, event-contract, and data-integrity gaps. Do not classify the learner achievement pipeline as production-certified. **Phase C is held** pending acceptance decision; any decision to work on the next phase does not waive these blockers.

This document distinguishes directly verified code behavior from concerns whose practical exploitation or runtime consequence needs test execution. It is a *source audit*, not evidence that a build passes or that all repository files have been exhaustively examined. It consolidates current-turn GitHub source inspections and preceding line-by-line Phase B investigation in the same conversation. A complete repository-wide inventory, migration inspection, test execution, and production configuration inspection are still prerequisites for unconditional certification.

## Findings — confirmed from code

Severity measures plausible business impact; it is not a production exploit claim.

### B-01 — High — Assignment tier completion bypasses prerequisites
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/assignment.service.ts:114–136`; `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/app/api/tutorial/assignments/[subtopicId]/complete/route.ts:43–51`; `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/__tests__/assignment.service.test.ts:123–143`.

`startTier` checks content flow and prior tier, but `completeTier` only rejects already-completed status. The API requires content-complete subtopic access, but does not enforce prerequisite tier completion or a started state. The test explicitly permits completing with absent progress. **Fix:** one atomic, shared transition policy for `not_started → in_progress → self_completed` with prerequisite eligibility. **Test:** direct completion of mixed/intermediate/expert without prior tier, absent progress, and concurrent requests.

### B-02 — High — Unpublished assignments are returned to learner calls
**Evidence:** `packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/assignment.repository.ts:44–51`; `packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/tutorial-assignments.ts:19`; `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/assignment.service.ts:58–78`.

`getAssignments` does not filter `isPublished`. **Fix:** learner-facing published-only query, separate admin draft queries. **Test:** published + draft rows in a real database query.

### B-03 — High — Assignment progress write lacks conditional lifecycle/version enforcement
**Evidence:** `packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/assignment.repository.ts:79–131`.

`upsertProgress` reads then writes by row ID without expected status/version; the insert path can race against another insert despite a unique index. **Fix:** conditional updates with expected state/version and conflict handling; tests with simultaneous start/complete.

### B-04 — High — Project submission accepts unpublished projects
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/project.service.ts:134–152`; `packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/tutorial-projects.ts:24`.

The existence, prerequisites and deliverable are checked, not `isPublished`. **Fix:** reject draft projects at the service boundary. **Test:** authenticated learner submitting an unpublished project ID.

### B-05 — High — Project idempotency cannot survive split Redis/DB transaction reliably
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/project.service.ts:153–205`; `packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/tutorial-project-submissions.ts:7–33`.

Redis NX marker is created inside a DB transaction but is not part of the SQL transaction; the result of `set` is not used as authoritative conflict control. The table has no logical unique constraint on a permitted active attempt. Publishing the QStash review event occurs after commit; failure can return an error after durable submission, without a durable outbox. **Fix:** define attempt identity; unique constraint and SQL-first idempotency; transactional outbox/reconciler. **Test:** duplicate concurrent submissions, Redis outage, DB rollback, and QStash outage after commit.

### B-06 — High — Project status updates race
**Evidence:** `packages/db-tutorial/src/repositories/project.repository.ts:114–163`.

Allowed transitions are checked against a fetched status, but UPDATE predicates contain ID/soft-delete only, not old status/version. **Fix:** compare-and-swap / `WHERE version = expected AND status = expected`, conflict response. **Test:** competing approval/revision transitions.

### B-07 — High — Review worker can discard retries as duplicates after failed processing
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/app/api/workers/review-project/route.ts:51–64,69–116`.

`processing` Redis marker is set before DB work; on DB failure the marker is not cleared, while subsequent retries return 200. **Fix:** recovery-aware lease, durable completion marker after commit, and operational replay path. **Test:** failure between claim and status updates, retry to final state.

### B-08 — Critical — Badge worker likewise suppresses failed retries
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/app/api/workers/award-project-badge/route.ts:52–89`.

The marker is claimed before lookup/transaction, without failure cleanup. **Fix/test:** same as B-07, with badge uniqueness verification.

### B-09 — High — Badge worker fails to revalidate authoritative submission ownership and approval
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/app/api/workers/award-project-badge/route.ts:65–89`.

The worker does not compare the submission's `userId`, `projectId`, status or approved badge association to the signed event before award. **Fix:** enforce approved submission, matching owner/project/badge atomically. **Test:** validly signed but inconsistent/stale event data.

### B-10 — Critical — Certificate worker suppresses retries after failure
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/app/api/workers/issue-certificate/route.ts:43–95,97–107`.

It claims a 24-hour Redis marker before SQL write and event publication, and treats any existing value as completed. **Fix:** durable idempotency, retryable completion state, outbox for emitted events. **Test:** insert failure and post-insert publish failure.

### B-11 — High — Certificate logical uniqueness not protected by schema
**Evidence:** `packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/certificates.ts:5–23`; `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/app/api/workers/issue-certificate/route.ts:56–91`.

Unique `verificationCode` exists, but `(userId, scope, parentId)` is not unique; check-then-insert can race. **Fix:** partial unique index for active certificates, with intentional reissue semantics. **Test:** simultaneous signed delivery.

### B-12 — High — Certificate worker does not independently verify eligibility
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/app/api/workers/issue-certificate/route.ts:38–91`; `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/project.service.ts:231–262`.

The issuing worker relies on event fields and checks only for an existing record; it does not call authoritative `checkCertificateEligibility`. **Fix:** revalidate at issuance against current learner/submission state or consume a durable authorized approval record. **Test:** stale/revoked eligibility.

### B-13 — High — Event handler type can disagree with custom schema
**Evidence:** `packages/events/src/consumer.ts:38–58`; `award-project-badge/route.ts:15–28,47–50`; `issue-certificate/route.ts:14–27,38–41`.

`createQStashHandler` uses `options.schema` instead of always validating the declared event type. Badge worker specifies `PROJECT_SUBMITTED` while custom schema expects `project.approved`; certificate worker specifies `CERTIFICATE_ISSUED` while schema expects `project.certificate_requested`. **Fix:** add command/event types and require an exact `parsed.type === declaredType` match. **Test:** wrong event-type rejection after signature verification.

### B-14 — High — Project-submitted event payload contracts differ
**Evidence:** `packages/events/src/types.ts:87`; `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/project.service.ts:191–204`; `review-project/route.ts:14–25`.

Central `PROJECT_SUBMITTED` payload schema requires `submittedAt` and lacks `submissionId`; project service emits `submissionId` and no `submittedAt`. Review worker uses its own custom schema. **Fix:** canonical versioned schema shared by publisher and consumer. **Test:** producer-generated event validated through central schema and signed handler.

### B-15 — High — Shared event consumer claims idempotency before success
**Evidence:** `packages/events/src/consumer.ts:58–74`.

When configured with an idempotency store, the handler writes its key before the business handler runs. A thrown handler can leave the event incorrectly treated as complete on retry. **Fix:** processed-state post-commit, recoverable leases or durable inbox. **Test:** handler failure then successful redelivery.

### B-16 — High — Remediation plan creation resets existing canonical learner progress
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/remediation.service.ts`, `createPlan` progress `onConflictDoUpdate` section (~lines 210–263); `packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/tutorial-progress.ts`.

The upsert resets `status`, `blocksCompleted`, `completedAt` on conflict. **Fix:** separate remediation attempts from canonical learning progress or explicitly authorize and audit reset semantics. **Test:** create a remediation plan for already completed content; assert no unintended loss of canonical progress.

### B-17 — High — Remediation completion directly sets tutorial completion
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/remediation.service.ts`, `markSubtopicRemediated` (~lines 345–405).

Direct `tutorialProgress.status='completed'` is not tied to block-level canonical completion policy. **Fix:** central completion authority or separate remediation state; integration tests for incomplete canonical blocks.

### B-18 — Medium — Remediation logical uniqueness/ownership needs explicit protection
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/remediation.service.ts`, `createPlan`, `markFailed`; `packages/db-tutorial/src/schema/remediation-triggers.ts:5–20`.

`getTrigger` uses `(userId, examResultId)` but schema has no unique constraint on that pair; simultaneous callers can insert duplicates. Redis key contains only `examResultId`, a potential cross-user namespace conflict if not globally unique. **Fix:** SQL uniqueness and user-scoped keys/strict globally-unique guarantee. **Test:** concurrent plan create across same user and users.

### B-19 — Medium — Help-request publish errors silently discarded, and event type is not registered
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/server/assignment.service.ts:137–170`; `packages/events/src/types.ts:3–22`.

`publishEvent('assignment.help_requested' as never, ...)` bypasses the type system and suppresses publish errors; the destination can default to `.invalid`. **Fix:** register a typed event, configured destination, outbox or retries, structured failure observability. **Test:** broker outage and replay.

### B-20 — Medium — Learner role boundary is broad
**Evidence:** `apps/realtutorialhub-web/src/lib/assignment-auth.ts:14–85`.

`requireStudent` accepts `student`, `admin`, `super_admin`, `faculty` and `user` on RTH brand. This might be intentional cross-role access, but it is not strict student-only authorization. **Fix:** document policy; separate learner/administrator authorization and add role matrix tests. Not a confirmed privilege escalation without policy and caller-context proof.

## Positive controls

- `requireStudent` validates user-audience token, RTH brand, non-empty ID and an allowed role before learner routes.
- `requireAssignmentAccess` requires a complete subtopic before exposing assignment completion endpoints; this is valuable but does not replace tier-specific validation.
- Assignment progress has a unique index on user, subtopic and difficulty.
- `ProjectRepository` has an allowed-transition map, though its DB update is not concurrency-safe.
- Badge record insertion uses `onConflictDoNothing` and the student-badge schema enforces `(userId, badgeId)` uniqueness.
- QStash handler checks signatures before processing.
- Project service test cases cover happy-path submission and basic prerequisite denial; not failures/concurrency.

## Required test and implementation acceptance gates

| Gate | Required evidence | Current result |
|---|---|---|
| Assignment eligibility | Tests proving all four tiers reject premature completion, including concurrency | FAIL — source permits bypass |
| Published-only learner content | DB test for unpublished assignments/projects | FAIL — filters missing |
| Submission integrity | Unique logical attempt, rollback/retry/outbox integration tests | FAIL — schema and logic insufficient |
| Project status transitions | Concurrent transition test proves no lost/invalid state | FAIL — unguarded UPDATE |
| Award/certificate consistency | Valid signed events, verified approval/ownership, recoverable retries | FAIL — source gaps |
| Certificate uniqueness | DB-level uniqueness plus race test | FAIL — no logical index |
| Event type consistency | Producer/consumer shared versioned schema and wrong-type test | FAIL — mismatch |
| Remediation preservation | Tests prove canonical progress not accidentally reset or forged complete | FAIL — source writes violate invariant |
| QStash/Redis resilience | Failure injection for claimed, processing, committed, published stages | NOT EXECUTED |
| End-to-end verification | Real database migration, build, integration tests, CI success | NOT EXECUTED |

## Remediation order (recommendation, not code changes)

1. **P0:** durable idempotency and retry-safe badge/certificate/review workers; guard badge/certificate identity/eligibility.
2. **P0/P1:** central signed event contracts, exact type enforcement, transactional outbox/inbox semantics.
3. **P1:** strict assignment tier lifecycle and published-only resource gates.
4. **P1:** SQL constraints and compare-and-swap status transitions for project submissions and certificates.
5. **P1:** separate remediation progress from canonical learning completion.
6. **P2:** typed help-request event delivery, role matrix, observability and regression suite.

## Scope limits and exit verdict

The reviewed Phase B functional source files supply adequate evidence for a consolidated pre-implementation defect register. However, an unconditional claim that **every possible Phase B file, migration, worker test, deployment configuration and external integration** has been audited would be unsupported. No commands or tests were executed against the application. Errors are characterized as source-derived risks, not observed production incidents.

**Decision:** Phase B **pre-implementation source audit report submitted**; Phase B **technical acceptance FAILED**. Keep the next audit phase on hold in accordance with the user's sequencing requirement. Fix, test and re-audit these gates before calling Phase B fully complete or production-ready.

# SkillUp-Web — Phase 03 Principal Architect Audit Report

**Audit date:** 2026-11-01
**Repository:** `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`
**Pinned source commit:** `e1b26a9e0e4feb0da38adf400e94dc911f495b2c` (`feature/project-llm-linux-worker`)
**Mode:** Read-only static review; no builds, tests, credentials, DB queries, deployments or modifications performed.
**Phase objective:** Trace student onboarding, dashboard, batch enrollment, attendance, payments, placement, programs and faculty from application API into relevant data helpers; establish correctness, truthful empty/error states, and authorization dependencies.

## Executive decision

**Phase 03 static assessment report: delivered. Phase 03 exit criteria: NOT PASSED.** Multiple confirmed user-facing data-integrity defects remain in the pinned source; full backend/payment/placement ownership verification and tests are not completed. The audit must not be equated with remediation or production certification. Phase 04 should remain on hold if the agreed rule is to advance only after phase exit criteria are passed.

## Reviewed source inventory (principal files)

Application data and API: `apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts` (624 lines), `src/lib/skillup-api.ts` (88), `src/app/api/onboarding/route.ts` (73), `src/app/api/onboarding/session/route.ts` (23), `src/app/api/profile/route.ts` (22), `src/app/api/student/dashboard/route.ts` (14), `src/app/api/student/attendance/route.ts` (14), `src/app/api/student/my-batch/route.ts` (14), `src/app/api/student/payments/route.ts` (14), `src/app/api/student/placement/route.ts` (14), `src/app/api/batches/route.ts` (14), `src/app/api/faculty/route.ts` (45), `src/app/api/programs/route.ts` (45), `src/app/api/programs/[slug]/route.ts` (62).

Related end-user pages and shared dependencies previously inspected and cross-referenced: `src/app/student/page.tsx`, `student/attendance/page.tsx`, `student/my-batch/page.tsx`, `student/payments/page.tsx`, `student/placement/page.tsx`, `student/exams/page.tsx`, `src/app/batches/page.tsx`, `src/app/programs/page.tsx`, `src/app/faculty/page.tsx`, `src/app/onboarding/page.tsx`, `src/app/placement/PlacementBridgeClient.tsx`, `src/share-branding/OnboardingEngine/components/OnboardingPage.tsx`, `src/share-branding/onboardingPageData.ts`, `src/share-branding/onboardingSessionCookie.ts`, `src/share-branding/auth/bffProfileHandler.ts`. App paths above are relative to `apps/skillup-web/`, unless beginning `src/share-branding/`.

This phase's evidence includes previous rounds' complete-source reviews and current selective cross-checks. It does not establish a fresh complete line-by-line re-review of every listed UI/backend dependency, so full integration certification is not claimed.

## Findings

### PH03-001 — P1 — Fake learner batch shown when no active enrollment (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-data.ts`, **88–107, 312–320, 512–517**.
- `getStudentBatchContext` returns null when no active enrollment; `getSkillupMyBatch()` and `getSkillupBatches()` return `FALLBACK_BATCH` instead of an explicit unenrolled state. The fallback includes faculty, sessions/materials and learner count.
- Consequence: Product reports nonexistent enrollment/classes as real. The `GET /api/student/my-batch` and `/api/batches` wrappers faithfully expose the fabricated response.
- Remediation: Return typed `not_enrolled`/empty state; distinguish DB outage from absent enrollment; render explicit CTA only when authorized.

### PH03-002 — P1 — Fabricated programs/faculty used on empty DB/errors (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `skillup-data.ts`, **37–87, 209–245, 548–589**.
- Program and faculty helpers fall back to hardcoded records; programs fallback occurs on empty result and in catch; faculty synthetic records and hero metrics are surfaced under failure/empty branches.
- Consequence: A learner sees invented offerings, faculty and statistics instead of accurate catalog or service error.
- Remediation: Remove production synthetic fallbacks; permit explicit demo-mode fixtures only; use typed empty/error responses.

### PH03-003 — P1/P2 — Synthetic placement readiness/interview counts and job matches (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `skillup-data.ts`, **109–123, 419–507**, notably **454, 464, 489, 501–506**.
- Interview count is derived from readiness score, and some job-match scores are generated from index/readiness rather than proven student-job matching. A hardcoded profile appears if no active record exists.
- Consequence: Learners receive misleading career guidance and fabricated activity metrics.
- Remediation: Derive interviews from actual interview records; return true matches or clearly label rankings as estimates with provenance; use a legitimate empty placement state.

### PH03-004 — P2 — Attendance numerator and denominator use different scopes (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `skillup-data.ts`, **265–280**.
- Present-count query aggregates attendance for the user across batches; denominator counts sessions for one selected active batch. Ratio can exceed 100%, and attendance may include irrelevant classes.
- Remediation: Filter numerator by the exact batch/session universe in denominator; avoid duplicate records; add zero-sessions and multi-batch tests.

### PH03-005 — P2 — Payment amounts from divergent sources / silent empty result (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `skillup-data.ts`, **248–274, 374–417**.
- Dashboard due amount uses `paymentInstallments` in the people DB; dedicated payments page uses an external payment DB query. If payment connection is absent, `getSkillupPayments` returns an empty list instead of misconfiguration error.
- Consequence: Payment due shown on dashboard may disagree with installments view; missing infrastructure can masquerade as paid/empty state.
- Remediation: Authoritative payment service and reconciliation contract; observable missing-DB error; tests for both endpoints for same learner.

### PH03-006 — P2 — Dashboard “placement matches” counts all open jobs (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `skillup-data.ts`, **294–300**.
- The count has no per-student match filter, despite UI label `Job matches` in `src/app/student/page.tsx`.
- Remediation: Join to matching results for authenticated student or relabel as `Open opportunities`.

### PH03-007 — P2 — Onboarding completion and skip redirect even after failed persistence (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `src/share-branding/OnboardingEngine/components/OnboardingPage.tsx`, **24–42, 67–113**.
- In both catch blocks an error is logged but router still navigates to `/dashboard`.
- Consequence: Failed saves appear successful; subsequent server redirect may loop/return to onboarding.
- Remediation: Preserve state, show error and retry; navigate only on verified success.

### PH03-008 — P2 — Onboarding BFF and client paths require end-to-end contract validation (CONDITIONAL)
- Source: `apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/onboarding/route.ts`, **20–68**; `OnboardingPage.tsx`, **24–42**.
- BFF maps `POST /api/onboarding` to gateway `/auth/onboarding` with `createInternalHeaders`; client submits `/api/auth/onboarding`. Verify actual gateway/Next auth proxy routing rather than assuming both are equivalent. The BFF chooses gateway URL from substring `hostname.includes('skillup')`; this is a fragile alternative to canonical brand resolution.
- Remediation: One documented route and canonical host/brand resolution; integration test client->BFF->gateway->backend->DB.

### PH03-009 — P2 — Unauthenticated onboarding-session endpoint stores client-provided journey state (CONFIRMED endpoint; downstream impact conditional)
- Source: `apps/skillup-web/src/app/api/onboarding/session/route.ts`, **8–22**; `src/share-branding/onboardingSessionCookie.ts`.
- Request sets HttpOnly cookie based on parsed client payload without authentication. It must not be treated as authoritative backend completion proof. `onboardingPageData.ts` uses it for form seeding; full set of other consumers must be verified.
- Remediation: Treat cookie as untrusted draft only; server-authoritative onboarding gate; explicit TTL and integrity strategy if used for decisions.

### PH03-010 — P2 — Program curriculum generated from marketing highlights (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `skillup-data.ts`, **594–624**.
- Detail helper constructs generic curricular sections instead of reading actual learning modules and published curriculum.
- Consequence: Program detail may promise content not tied to the course structure.
- Remediation: Use published curriculum records and represent missing curriculum as empty/unpublished.

### PH03-011 — P2 — Dashboard visual bars are hard-coded while values are dynamic (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `apps/skillup-web/src/app/student/page.tsx`, **around 78–103**.
- Attendance/progress/upcoming/job bars use fixed class widths (`86%`, `68%`, `54%`, `62%`) regardless of displayed values.
- Remediation: Compute proportional widths from actual bounded values; use appropriate scales for counts.

### PH03-012 — P2 — Exam/payments calls to action not functional (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `apps/skillup-web/src/app/student/exams/page.tsx` and `src/app/student/payments/page.tsx`.
- Static assessment tracks have `Start practice` buttons without handlers; payments page `Pay overdue installment` and `Download receipt` buttons have no implemented actions.
- Remediation: Wire authorized workflows, or disable clearly and remove misleading status claims.

### PH03-013 — P2 — SSR fallback masks program/faculty authentication or upstream failure (CONFIRMED)
- Source: `apps/skillup-web/src/lib/skillup-api.ts`, **55–87**.
- If programs or faculty HTTP fetch fails for any reason, SSR helper calls direct data service. Protected learner routes appropriately throw instead.
- Consequence: Service/authorization failures can be masked with data fallback; behavior differs across page categories.
- Remediation: Distinguish unauthorized, unavailable and genuine empty; only use direct DB helpers when explicitly allowed by architecture.

### PH03-014 — P2 — Attendance list record identity uses display dates (CONFIRMED risk)
- Source: `apps/skillup-web/src/app/student/attendance/page.tsx`.
- React list uses `entry.date` as key; duplicate classes on the same date collide. Attendance representation only includes formatted date/status/note, losing unique session/record ID.
- Remediation: Include stable attendance ID and scheduled session timestamp; group multiple sessions clearly.

## Positive controls
- Student API endpoints call `requireStudentAuth` and pass its resolved user ID to data helpers. This does not by itself prove the downstream identity mapping but avoids direct user ID from client query.
- Programs/faculty route handlers perform their own authentication and brand validation.
- The dedicated content-manager source-file writer endpoint returns HTTP 410 and is not available for learner editing.
- SSR learner API helper fails rather than using fake data when protected student API request fails.

## Unverified dependencies / missing tests
1. Gateway `/auth/onboarding` mapping, server-side authenticated persistence and brand-specific DB transaction semantics.
2. Student user-ID mapping (`shadowUserId` vs `originalUserId`) to people, payment and placement databases (Phase 02 carryover).
3. Payment ownership, tenant scoping, schema/version and transaction reconciliation across payment DB and people DB.
4. Placement ranking algorithm inputs, profile ownership and interview-count source of truth.
5. Program/subject/batch classification and published curriculum/availability policies.
6. Attendance semantics for multiple sessions, late arrivals, reschedules and deleted sessions.
7. Cross-tenant and malformed input regression tests and actual CI/build/test results.

2. Fix onboarding success/failure transitions and authoritative write path.
3. Reconcile learner/payment identity and payment-due source of truth.
4. Correct attendance aggregation and placement-match counting.
5. Replace static CTAs/visual indicators and cover legitimate empty states with tests.

# SUIA Marketing — Phase 03 Cross-System Integration and Security Audit

**Assessment date:** 2026-11-01
**Role:** Principal Architect — independent read-only source review
**Repository:** `skillupitacademy-alt/SUIA_RTH_SHC`
**Pinned commit:** `5efd1129d905d05c912acfef66e52df9ca15120b`
**Scope:** `packages/marketing-site/src`, with related deployment boundaries listed as unverified.
**Status:** Phase 03 source-level assessment delivered; **critical integration verification NOT PASSED**; production sign-off **WITHHELD**.

## Executive decision

The critical integration paths **cannot be certified production-safe** at this snapshot. The source shows clear deficiencies at consent enforcement, cross-brand analytics tracker isolation, delivery acknowledgement, identity resolution, and consent persistence. These findings are supported by direct pinned-commit source retrieval. Build, tests, live browser interactions, route mounting, runtime topology, and partner delivery receipts were **not executed/verified**. The work fulfills the Phase 03 assessment/reporting objective but **does not satisfy** the Phase 03 exit criterion requiring verified workflows.

## Evidence base

- Pinned complete files inspected directly in this review: `lib/privacy/{consent-manager,consent-storage,tracking-permissions}.ts`, `lib/analytics/{tracker,events}.ts`, `lib/analytics/server/{route,pipeline}.ts`, `lib/analytics/identity/{identity-resolver,identity-store,user-merge-engine}.ts`, `lib/analytics/providers/{internal,ga4,meta}.provider.ts`, `components/privacy/ConsentBanner.tsx`, `components/contact/ContactForm.tsx`, `components/CoursePages/Curriculum/mainCurriculum.tsx` (16 unique files).
- Historical pinned source inspection from preceding rounds was used for navigation (`NavBarMain`, `MobileMenu`, `useScrollSpy`), course CTA (`HeroContent`, `MainHeroSection`), curriculum (`MobileFilter`, `usseCurriculumState`, `CurriculumAccorrdion`), and content, but these files were not re-fetched in the present Phase 03 source batch.
- Source-derived architectural intent is compared with `FinalAechitecture.md`, `ProjectAuditReport.md`, `ResolveProjectAuditReport.md`, and the Phase 01/02 audit deliverables. Architecture targets are requirements rather than evidence of implementation.

## Critical workflow trace and findings

### P03-01 — High — Consent boundary is client-only on event dispatch

**Source:** `lib/analytics/tracker.ts:145–159` filters browser providers using `canDispatchProvider`; `lib/privacy/consent-manager.ts:52–63` maps providers to categories. In contrast, `lib/analytics/server/route.ts:14–31` accepts events without reading consent, and `lib/analytics/server/pipeline.ts:261–266` dispatches to GA4, Meta CAPI and internal processing without a consent check. The server event schema in `lib/analytics/events.ts:72–81` has no explicit consent grant/proof field.

**Impact:** Direct ingestion requests or events forwarded through another channel can reach third-party analytics without a source-level server consent gate. This is a verifiable authorization/enforcement gap; applicable legal conclusions depend on deployment and jurisdiction.

**Fix:** Enforce provider-specific consent server-side with trusted consent evidence and consent category mapping. Never trust arbitrary client-supplied consent booleans. Add negative tests for deny, revoke, expiry, and direct POST attempts.

### P03-02 — High — Cross-brand singleton can bind the wrong configuration

**Source:** `lib/analytics/tracker.ts:197–229`. `trackerSingleton` is module-level and `getAnalyticsTracker(brandId)` uses `trackerSingleton ??= createAnalyticsTracker(brandId)` without checking subsequent `brandId`s. `trackEvent`, `identifyUser`, `trackPageView` and others call it with arbitrary brand IDs (`:231–268`).

**Impact:** If both brands run through one JS runtime, the first brand's analytics runtime/provider configuration will be used for later requests from another brand, corrupting brand separation and potentially misrouting events. Whether the current deployment shares a runtime is unknown, but the API-level invariant fails.

**Fix:** Use a `Map<AnalyticsBrandId, AnalyticsTracker>` or a validated per-brand dependency injection scope; add same-runtime two-brand tests.

### P03-03 — High — Server accepts events despite provider failures; partial delivery can occur

**Source:** `lib/analytics/server/pipeline.ts:249–275,327–335` awaits queue processing, but `processAnalyticsQueue` swallows dispatch failures after pushing to an in-memory dead-letter queue. The caller returns accepted, and `lib/analytics/server/route.ts:33–39` emits HTTP 202. Providers in `pipeline.ts:84–113,122–148` do not check `response.ok`, so HTTP 4xx/5xx can also be treated as successful. A `Promise.all` can partially deliver to some providers before another rejects.

**Impact:** False success acknowledgement and unrecoverable partial delivery are possible; the dead-letter queue is in-memory and lacks a demonstrated replay mechanism in these files. Closely related historical findings MKT-223/228; consolidate rather than double-count blindly.

**Fix:** Persist accepted events in a durable queue, independently record per-provider status/idempotency, check response status, replay failed deliveries with limits, and return a truthful durable-acceptance contract.

### P03-04 — High — Identity merge silently chooses conflicting identifiers

**Source:** `lib/analytics/identity/user-merge-engine.ts:19–45`. Conflicts are detected (`:22–31`) but the merge proceeds using `{ ...secondary.identifiers, ...primary.identifiers }` and writes both nodes even if critical identifiers disagree. `identity-store.ts:20–41` uses unscoped in-memory maps and string keys. `identity-resolver.ts:35–96` resolves candidates and links nodes without a brand namespace or conflict rejection.

**Impact:** Incorrect joins are possible when identifiers collide, and brand isolation is not encoded into identity keys. This is particularly material to a two-brand shared-identity architecture. The current deployment's trust boundaries and persistence are unverified.

**Fix:** Define deterministic merge policies and reject/quarantine conflicting authenticated identities; namespace brand-local identifiers; separate globally authorized identity-linking operations from brand-local analytics; persist auditable merge decisions.

### P03-05 — Medium/High — Consent storage can crash and accepts schema-invalid records

**Source:** `lib/privacy/consent-storage.ts:10,15–18,27`. `localStorage.getItem` is outside `try`, `setItem` is unguarded, and `JSON.parse(raw) as ConsentState` does not validate categories, version, region, expiry or types. `lib/privacy/tracking-permissions.ts:12` then accesses `state.categories[category]` without checking `categories` exists. `ConsentBanner.tsx:15` directly accesses categories.

**Impact:** A malformed stored JSON object such as `{}` may crash the banner or permission logic; disabled/denied storage may throw during consent handling. Related to MKT-285 but the parsed-state validation issue deserves independent remediation.

**Fix:** Validate with a runtime schema, catch storage property reads/writes, default to deny for optional categories on errors, and test malformed data.

### P03-06 — Medium/High — Consent preferences cannot reliably be revisited through the banner

**Source:** `components/privacy/ConsentBanner.tsx:11–17` hides the banner whenever `analytics` or `advertising` is true. `:28–47` provides buttons only while the banner is shown. After accepting analytics only, no reopening control is present in this component. No independent preference-settings route or footer control was established by this particular source trace.

**Impact:** Users cannot change their choice through this component after consenting; a separate control may exist elsewhere but was not verified here.

**Fix:** Provide a persistent accessible preference launcher, including revocation and category-specific choices; verify on the fully mounted site.

### P03-07 — Medium — Direct provider functions bypass the tracker’s consent-gated flush

**Source:** `lib/analytics/tracker.ts:109–132` calls `identifyUser`, `setUserProperties` and `trackPageView` on available providers without `canDispatchProvider`, while `flush` does filter (`:149–152`). Public wrappers at `:240–268` expose these paths.

**Impact:** A direct page-view or identify call can invoke GA4/Meta when their consent categories have not been granted, if the providers are available. This is distinct from P03-01 server-side bypass.

**Fix:** Consolidate all analytics operations under the same consent policy, including identify and page views.

### P03-08 — Medium — Client-side tracker drops provider failures rather than retrying them

**Source:** `lib/analytics/tracker.ts:145–174` removes batch from queue, catches per-provider errors inside the mapped promise and calls `onError`, but never requeues failed provider deliveries. `lib/analytics/providers/internal.provider.ts:19–28` does not check HTTP status. This yields potential event loss after transient network/provider errors.

**Fix:** Durable/controlled retries by provider, response-status validation, bounded backpressure and end-to-end delivery tests.

## Cross-system trace matrix

| Integration | Evidence | Phase 03 conclusion | Validation still needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Consent → browser analytics | `consent-manager`, `tracker`, `ConsentBanner` | Gate exists only in flush; direct methods bypass | Browser consent matrix, revoke/expiry handling |
| Browser → ingestion endpoint | `internal.provider`, `server/route` | Brand header used for brand resolution; server has no consent check | Host/header spoof tests and proxy trust configuration |
| Server → GA4 / Meta | `server/pipeline` | Status not checked; dispatch errors swallowed | Simulated 4xx/5xx/timeout, delivery receipts |
| Identity → merge / store | `identity-resolver`, `user-merge-engine`, `identity-store` | Cross-brand scope and conflicts not safely handled | Multi-brand collision and authenticated link tests |
| Queue → automation / data features | `server/pipeline:181–234` | In-memory sequencing with no demonstrated durable guarantee | Delivery idempotency, recovery, downstream consumer tests |
| Lead capture → WhatsApp | Prior source `HeroContent.tsx:34–58`, `CertificateShowcase.tsx:86–97` | CTA opens WhatsApp and tracks lead; not a confirmed enrollment | Browser popup/failure behavior and consent path |
| Navigation → target sections | Prior source `useScrollSpy.ts:49–62`, `NavBarMain.tsx:20–23` | Missing target raises browser alert; mobile accessibility gaps | Route and anchor map, keyboard and mobile tests |
| Course metadata → curriculum | Prior source `MainHeroSection.tsx:62–70`, `mainCurriculum.tsx:38–74` | Hardcoded cross-course metrics, runtime content contracts inconsistent | Per-course rendered claims and navigation tests |

## Severity/priority

- **Release blockers to resolve before certifying tracking/security:** P03-01, P03-02, P03-03, P03-04; prioritize P03-07 as consent-related.
- **Must correct before production approval:** P03-05 and P03-08; P03-06 requires verification of site-level preference controls.
- **Pre-existing audit items carried forward:** MKT-219, 223, 228, 261, 271, 274, 275, 282, 283, 284, 285, 286 and others relevant to the integration paths. Do not interpret this as a complete deduplicated crosswalk.

## Architecture alignment

`FinalAechitecture.md` advocates separate brand boundaries and shared identity with explicit isolation, reliability and durable recoverability. The inspected in-memory identity, queue and singleton patterns do not establish those guarantees. The architecture document is an intended target, not proof that the code or infrastructure implements the target.

## Testing not performed / remaining exit gates

1. Reproduce both brands in one runtime and prove separate providers and event brand attribution.
2. Consent matrix testing for all providers on first visit, opt-out, analytics-only, accept-all, expiry and revocation—including direct ingestion and `trackPageView` / `identifyUser`.
3. Test provider 4xx/5xx, timeouts, retries, duplicate events, partial success, dead-letter replay and process restart.
4. Test conflicting identity keys, same email across brands, and unauthorized cross-brand associations.
5. Confirm route mounts, proxy trust boundaries, monitoring and retention policies outside the marketing subtree.
6. Validate keyboard/mobile navigation, course routes, actual enrollment vs enquiry behavior, and published course metrics.
7. Execute type checking, unit/integration tests, real-browser tests, performance/scalability checks and security verification in an authorized environment.

## Final Phase 03 decision

**Phase 03 report submitted; source-level critical-path audit performed.** There are **eight cross-system findings**, several overlapping previously recorded MKT issues. **Do not append eight unreviewed new MKT IDs automatically**; handle canonical mapping in Phase 04. Security/integration closure is **NOT PASSED** and production release is **NOT APPROVED**. No repository modifications or runtime execution occurred.
